body_en: With midterm elections less than a week away, Donald Trump and Barack Obama were set to appear at rallies on Wednesday night as Republicans and Democrats make some of their final appeals to voters in key states.

Obama, who was recently in Michigan to support Abdul El-Sayed, is in Georgia, where he will campaign for Keisha Lance Bottoms, the former Atlanta mayor seeking the governor’s office, and the senator Jon Ossoff.

Meanwhile, Donald Trump, who has appeared at more than 20 rallies in October, was returning to the battleground state of Ohio to support Republican candidates, including Vivek Ramaswamy, who is running for governor, and Jon Husted for Senate.
JD Vance was in North Carolina stumping for Michael Whatley, the former RNC chair, who faces a tough race for Senate against Democrat and former governor Roy Cooper.
body_zh: 距离中期选举还有不到一周的时间，唐纳德·特朗普和巴拉克·奥巴马定于周三晚上出席集会，共和党和民主党将向关键州的选民发出最后的呼吁。
奥巴马最近在密歇根州支持阿卜杜勒·赛义德，现在他正在佐治亚州为寻求州长职位的亚特兰大前市长凯莎·兰斯·博顿斯和参议员乔恩·奥索夫竞选。
与此同时，10 月份出席了 20 多场集会的唐纳德·特朗普 (Donald Trump) 正返回战场州俄亥俄州，支持共和党候选人，其中包括竞选州长的维韦克·拉马斯瓦米 (Vivek Ramaswamy) 和竞选参议员的乔恩·赫斯特 (Jon Husted)。
JD万斯在北卡罗来纳州为共和党全国委员会前主席迈克尔·沃特利(Michael Whatley)进行竞选，后者面临着与民主党人和前州长罗伊·库珀(Roy Cooper)激烈的参议院竞选。

title_en: Democrat Mary Peltola’s campaign reportedly recruited second Dan Sullivan in Alaska Senate race
title_zh: 据报道，民主党人玛丽·佩尔托拉的竞选团队在阿拉斯加州参议员竞选中招募了第二位丹·沙利文
summary: Republicans have condemned the presence of two Dan Sullivans on the ballot, calling it a ploy to split votes Alaska Democrat Mary Peltola’s campaign was behind an effort to recruit a challenger with almost the same name as the Republican US senator Dan Sulliva
summary_zh: 共和党人谴责两名丹·沙利文出现在选票上，称这是分裂选票的策略，阿拉斯加民主党人玛丽·佩尔托拉的竞选活动
body_en: Democrat Mary Peltola’s campaign reportedly recruited second Dan Sullivan in Alaska Senate race
Republicans have condemned the presence of two Dan Sullivans on the ballot, calling it a ploy to split votes

Alaska Democrat Mary Peltola’s campaign was behind an effort to recruit a challenger with almost the same name as the Republican US senator Dan Sullivan, both of whom will appear on the ballot in next week’s midterm elections, the New York Times reported on Wednesday.

Republicans have condemned the presence in the race of two candidates named Dan Sullivan – one the two-term US senator, the second a retiree living in south-eastern Alaska with scant political experience – calling the newcomer a ploy by Democrats to cost the incumbent re-election by splitting his supporters.

Peltola’s campaign has denied involvement with the other Dan Sullivan, but the Times reports that her officials together with the party’s campaign arm, the Democratic Senatorial Campaign Committee (DSCC), worked to find other people named Dan Sullivan in Alaska, and encourage them to run. Their reporting is based on interviews with Peltola’s former campaign manager and other sources, together with documents and text messages related to the recruitment effort.
Alaska Senate candidate Mary Peltola delays campaign stops after car crash
“Alaskan voters need to know,” Elisa Rios, whom Peltola fired in August, told the Times, which added that she later tried to retract her interview with the outlet.
Nate Adams, a spokesperson for Sullivan’s campaign, said: “Alaskans deserve the truth.”

“Not one player in this operation has acted in good faith with Alaska voters. Mary Peltola and her campaign have spent months gaslighting Alaskans, denying a scheme they were running all along. We always knew this was a concerted effort to deceive Alaskans, and Mary Peltola was hoping it would stay covered up until after the election,” he added.
Donald Trump shared a link to the Times’s article on Truth Social, calling it proof of “election fraud”.

“I don’t think Mary Peltola, after perpetrating such a terrible scheme, should be allowed to run,” he added. Last week, he acknowledged ordering the justice department to file a lawsuit attempting to block the certification of the election results, if Sullivan loses.

A spokesperson for Peltola’s campaign said: “The Alaskans for Mary campaign has no involvement with either Sullivan campaign. Like Mary, our campaign is focused on lowering costs and fixing the rigged system in DC.”

Sullivan’s bid for a third term in the US Senate against Peltola, a former US congresswoman, is one of the most important contests of next week’s midterm elections. Alaska is one of a handful of states with Senate races this year that Democrats are targeting in order to win back a majority in the chamber, where they hold 47 seats to the GOP’s 53, and recent polls have shown Peltola in the lead.

Election authorities in the state attempted to disqualify the other Dan Sullivan before the August primary, but the state supreme court ruled that he can appear on the ballot. Together with Sullivan and Peltola, the challenger was one of the top four vote-getters in the non-partisan primary.
On the general election ballot, the senator will be listed as “Sullivan, Dan S. (Registered Republican) Incumbent” and the challenger “Sullivan, Daniel J. Jr.”
At a rally in Alaska this month, Trump urged the senator’s supporters to vote for the “real” Dan Sullivan , and warned that errant votes for the challenger could cost the senator re-election.

“The DSCC is not involved with Dan J Sullivan,” a spokesperson for the Democratic Senate campaign arm said. They added that “Republicans have a long history of recruiting and propping up candidates in an attempt to boost their own campaigns”, including in Alaska’s and Ohio’s Senate races this year, and in previous elections in North Carolina and Montana.

The Times reports that Democrats began considering ways to get a spoiler candidate on to the midterm ballot in the summer of 2025. The DSCC introduced the Peltola campaign to a political operative and Ohio native named Jerid Kurtz, who specialized in such activities, which are typically legal. The aide unsuccessfully approached another potential candidate, who did not share a name with the senator, and ultimately recruited the other Dan Sullivan, the Times reports.

Peltola campaign officials also discussed with the DSCC creating a rightwing party to field a candidate in a race, but that did not pan out, according to the Times. After a second Democrat advanced through the August primary, the operative met with him and convinced him to drop out. He was replaced on the ballot by another Republican, Gerald Heikes, who told the Times he was recruited to run “by a guy from the midwest”, though the person did not resemble the Democratic operative from Ohio.
Heikes is a perennial candidate, who has previously run unsuccessfully for governor, US senator and House representative.
body_zh: 据报道，民主党人玛丽·佩尔托拉的竞选团队在阿拉斯加州参议员竞选中招募了第二位丹·沙利文
共和党人谴责两名丹·沙利文出现在选票上，称这是分裂选票的策略
据《纽约时报》周三报道，阿拉斯加州民主党参议员玛丽·佩尔托拉的竞选团队正在努力招募一位与美国共和党参议员丹·沙利文几乎同名的挑战者，两人都将出现在下周中期选举的选票上。
共和党人谴责两位名叫丹·沙利文(Dan Sullivan)的候选人参加竞选，其中一位是两届美国参议员，另一位是居住在阿拉斯加东南部的退休人员，缺乏政治经验。称这位新人是民主党的一个策略，目的是通过分裂他的支持者来损害现任连任。
佩尔托拉的竞选团队否认与另一位丹·沙利文有牵连，但《泰晤士报》报道称，她的官员与该党的竞选部门民主党参议员竞选委员会（DSCC）一起努力在阿拉斯加寻找其他名为丹·沙利文的人，并鼓励他们参选。他们的报道基于对佩尔托拉前竞选经理和其他消息来源的采访，以及与招聘工作相关的文件和短信。
阿拉斯加州参议院候选人玛丽·佩尔托拉因车祸推迟竞选活动
“阿拉斯加选民需要知道，”佩尔托拉八月份解雇的埃莉莎·里奥斯告诉《泰晤士报》，该报补充说，她后来试图撤回对该媒体的采访。
沙利文竞选团队发言人内特·亚当斯 (Nate Adams) 表示：“阿拉斯加人应该知道真相。”
“这次行动中没有一个参与者对阿拉斯加选民真诚地行事。玛丽·佩尔托拉和她的竞选团队花了几个月的时间对阿拉斯加人进行煽动，否认他们一直在实施的计划。我们一直都知道这是一次共同努力欺骗阿拉斯加人的行动，玛丽·佩尔托拉希望它能一直被掩盖，直到选举结束，”他补充道。
唐纳德·特朗普分享了《纽约时报》关于 Truth Social 的文章的链接，称其为“选举舞弊”的证据。
“我认为玛丽·佩尔托拉在实施了如此可怕的计划后，不应该被允许参选，”他补充道。上周，他承认，如果沙利文败选，他将命令司法部提起诉讼，试图阻止对选举结果的认证。
佩尔托拉竞选团队的一位发言人表示：“阿拉斯加支持玛丽竞选活动与沙利文的竞选活动没有任何关系。与玛丽一样，我们的竞选活动的重点是降低成本和修复华盛顿特区的被操纵系统。”
沙利文与美国前国会女议员佩尔托拉争夺美国参议院第三个任期，是下周中期选举中最重要的竞争之一。阿拉斯加是今年少数几个进行参议院竞选的州之一，民主党希望夺回众议院多数席位，目前阿拉斯加州拥有 47 个席位，而共和党拥有 53 个席位，最近的民意调查显示佩尔托拉处于领先地位。
该州选举当局试图在八月初选前取消另一位丹·沙利文的资格，但州最高法院裁定他可以参加选票。挑战者与沙利文和佩尔托拉一起，是无党派初选中得票最高的四名候选人之一。
在大选选票上，参议员将被列为“Sullivan, Dan S.（注册共和党人）现任”，挑战者为“Sullivan, Daniel J. Jr.”。
在本月阿拉斯加的一次集会上，特朗普敦促参议员的支持者投票给“真正的”丹·沙利文，并警告说，错误投票给挑战者可能会导致参议员连任。
民主党参议院竞选部门发言人表示：“DSCC 与丹·J·沙利文无关。”他们补充说，“共和党在招募和支持候选人以试图推动自己的竞选活动方面有着悠久的历史”，包括今年阿拉斯加州和俄亥俄州的参议员竞选，以及之前北卡罗来纳州和蒙大拿州的选举。
据《泰晤士报》报道，民主党开始考虑如何让一名搅局者候选人参加 2025 年夏季的中期投票。DSCC 将佩尔托拉竞选活动介绍给了一位俄亥俄州本地政治人士杰里德·库尔茨 (Jerid Kurtz)，他专门从事此类通常是合法的活动。据《泰晤士报》报道，这名助手未能成功接触另一位潜在候选人，该候选人与参议员没有同名，最终招募了另一位丹·沙利文。
据《泰晤士报》报道，佩尔托拉竞选官员还与 DSCC 讨论了创建一个右翼政党以派出一名候选人参加竞选，但这一计划并未成功。在第二位民主党人通过八月份的初选后，这名特工会见了他并说服他退出。他在选票上被另一位共和党人杰拉尔德·海克斯(Gerald Heikes)取代，他告诉《泰晤士报》，他是被“一个来自中西部的人”招募来竞选的，尽管这个人与来自俄亥俄州的民主党特工并不相似。
海克斯是一位常年候选人，此前曾竞选过州长、美国参议员和众议院代表，但均未成功。

title_en: Senate candidates built up massive campaign war chests with out-of-state donations
title_zh: 参议院候选人通过州外捐款建立了大量竞选资金
summary: In several competitive U.S. Senate contests, candidates have built healthy campaign accounts with out-of-state donations. But the messages to those donors is very different from the one back at home.
summary_zh: 在几场竞争激烈的美国参议院竞选中，候选人利用州外捐款建立了健康的竞选账户。但给那些人的信息确实
body_en: Senate candidates built up massive campaign war chests with out-of-state donations
📲 Get the latest on the midterms & more in the NPR App
In key U.S. Senate races this year, candidates are soliciting donations from outside of their home states, and their out-of-state messaging is different from what they're running locally.

An NPR analysis of Google Ads for four major Senate races — Iowa, Georgia, Ohio and Texas — found that the Democratic and Republican candidates spent more than $15 million on advertising related to fundraising in the 2025-26 election cycle. About three quarters of that went to ads that ran nationally.

Often, these ads focus on national talking points — such as attacking or defending President Trump, or turning the Senate blue or red — rather than local issues. For candidates like Georgia Sen. Jon Ossoff and Iowa Democratic nominee Josh Turek, more than 80% of their itemized individual contributions have come from out of state.

The funneling of funds has affected at least four of the competitive Senate races, where a majority of the money is coming from outside the state. ActBlue and WinRed, two major grassroots fundraising platforms, are a major catalyst for out-of-state fundraising.
Because this technology is inexpensive to run, it incentivizes candidates to rely on digital ads, according to Zachary Albert, a professor of politics at Brandeis University.

"ActBlue and WinRed really reduced the transaction costs for contributing," Albert said. "Even if you're only yielding like a $5 or $10 contribution from someone like the costs of soliciting that are so much lower than they used to be, that it makes it worthwhile."

With both parties — and each candidate — now having fundraising platforms, political hopefuls increasingly need to stand out from the crowd and are often shifting their messaging to a broader audience, which can result in using polarizing messaging to solicit funds.
For in-state and out-of-state ads, candidates tend to have two different sets of talking points, according to Wesleyan Media Project's Michael Franz.
Democrats still poised to make gains, but poll shows warning signs for just how many

"In a general election campaign for a [local] TV ad, a candidate will never say, 'I'm the Democrat,' because they want to appeal to moderates and swing voters and they want voters across the aisle," Franz said. "But with a digital ad that's airing outside of your state, the party label becomes more important."

This is reflected in many digital ads. Former Ohio Democratic Sen. Sherrod Brown — who is seeking to regain a place in the Senate — calls to turn his state blue while Georgia Republican Rep. Mike Collins asks people to help turn his state's Senate seat red. Republicans currently control the Senate but there are a number of toss-up races giving Democrats a path to taking back the chamber.
Iowa Republican Senate candidate, Rep. Ashley Hinson speaks at a rally on October 22, 2026 in Sioux City, Iowa as President Trump looks on. Anna Moneymaker/Getty Images hide caption
Iowa Republican Rep. Ashley Hinson touts her America First credentials in ads for her Senate race, saying she's "America First," while Ossoff in Georgia attacks Trump directly.

According to Michael Heseltine, a researcher at Oxford University who studies how members of congress use social media to communicate , says while there is a large amount of locally-focused messaging, candidates are increasingly spending more time and energy on national talking points.

"[If] we continue on that trend, you'll probably find more and more members who have neglected their constituencies or at least not presented themselves as representatives of their constituencies," he said.

In a statement to NPR, the Ossoff campaign denied targeting audiences by location, and says the campaign "is powered by small-dollar donors because the Senator refuses donations from corporate PACs and federal lobbyists."
The other campaigns declined to comment or did not respond to interview requests.

Daniel Hopkins, a political science professor at the University of Pennsylvania, believes we're in a new era of campaigning, where candidates now have two major stakeholders to appeal to: a voter base which is local, and a donor base which is often larger and nationwide.
body_zh: 参议院候选人通过州外捐款建立了大量竞选资金
📲 在 NPR 应用程序中获取有关中期选举的最新动态及更多信息
在今年的美国参议院关键竞选中，候选人正在向其所在州以外的州寻求捐款，而他们在州外传递的信息与他们在本地运行的信息不同。
NPR 对爱荷华州、佐治亚州、俄亥俄州和德克萨斯州这四个主要参议院竞选的 Google Ads 进行的分析发现，民主党和共和党候选人在 2025-26 选举周期的筹款相关广告上花费了超过 1500 万美元。其中大约四分之三用于在全国范围内投放的广告。
通常，这些广告关注的是全国性的话题——比如攻击或捍卫特朗普总统，或者将参议院变成蓝色或红色——而不是地方问题。对于佐治亚州参议员乔恩·奥索夫（Jon Ossoff）和爱荷华州民主党候选人乔什·图雷克（Josh Turek）等候选人来说，他们超过 80% 的个人捐款来自州外。
资金的输送至少影响了四场竞争激烈的参议院竞选，其中大部分资金来自州外。 ActBlue和WinRed这两个主要的草根筹款平台是州外筹款的主要催化剂。
布兰代斯大学政治学教授扎卡里·阿尔伯特表示，由于这项技术的运行成本低廉，它会激励候选人依赖数字广告。
“ActBlue 和 WinRed 确实降低了贡献的交易成本，”Albert 说。 “即使你只从某人那里得到 5 美元或 10 美元的捐款，比如拉客的成本比以前低得多，这也是值得的。”
由于两党以及每位候选人现在都拥有筹款平台，政治希望者越来越需要从人群中脱颖而出，并且经常将他们的信息转移给更广泛的受众，这可能会导致利用两极分化的信息来筹集资金。
卫斯理媒体项目的迈克尔·弗朗茨表示，对于州内和州外的广告，候选人往往有两套不同的谈话要点。
民主党仍准备取得进展，但民意调查显示了警告信号
“在[当地]电视广告的大选活动中，候选人永远不会说，‘我是民主党人’，因为他们想要吸引温和派和摇摆选民，他们希望选民能够站在两党的一边，”弗兰兹说。 “但是，随着数字广告在您所在州之外播放，政党标签就变得更加重要。”
这反映在许多数字广告中。正在寻求重新获得参议院席位的前俄亥俄州民主党参议员谢罗德·布朗呼吁将他的州变成蓝色，而佐治亚州共和党众议员迈克·柯林斯则请求人们帮助将他所在州的参议院席位变成红色。共和党目前控制着参议院，但有许多难以预测的竞选为民主党夺回参议院提供了一条途径。
2026 年 10 月 22 日，爱荷华州共和党参议院候选人、众议员阿什利·辛森 (Ashley Hinson) 在爱荷华州苏城举行的集会上发表讲话，特朗普总统在场。安娜摇钱树/盖蒂图片社隐藏标题栏
爱荷华州共和党众议员阿什利·辛森(Ashley Hinson)在参议院竞选广告中宣扬她的美国优先资格，称她是“美国优先”，而佐治亚州的奥索夫则直接攻击特朗普。
牛津大学研究国会议员如何使用社交媒体进行交流的研究员迈克尔·赫塞尔廷表示，虽然存在大量以本地为中心的信息，但候选人越来越多地将更多时间和精力花在全国性的话题上。
“如果我们继续这种趋势，你可能会发现越来越多的成员忽视了他们的选区，或者至少没有将自己表现为选区的代表，”他说。
在给 NPR 的一份声明中，奥索夫竞选团队否认按地点定位受众，并表示该竞选活动“由小额捐助者支持，因为参议员拒绝企业政治行动委员会和联邦游说者的捐款”。
其他竞选活动拒绝发表评论或没有回应采访请求。
宾夕法尼亚大学政治学教授丹尼尔·霍普金斯 (Daniel Hopkins) 认为，我们正处于竞选的新时代，候选人现在有两个主要利益相关者可以吸引：本地选民基础和往往更大、全国范围内的捐助者基础。

title_en: Here's how Democrats in Congress are preparing for election fraud claims
title_zh: 以下是国会民主党人如何为选举舞弊索赔做准备
summary: Congressional Democrats are working with good governance groups to create an action plan for any potential claims of election fraud.
summary_zh: 国会民主党人正在与善治团体合作，针对任何潜在的选举舞弊指控制定行动计划。
body_en: Here's how Democrats in Congress are preparing for election fraud claims : NPR

Here's how Democrats in Congress are preparing for election fraud claims Congressional Democrats are working with good governance groups to create an action plan for any potential claims of election fraud.
Here's how Democrats in Congress are preparing for election fraud claims
Congressional Democrats are forming a task force to protect election results
Voters are already casting votes in aa number of states ahead of the midterm election on Nov. 3. RYAN MURPHY/AFP hide caption
This story has been updated from a story first reported in August.

This midterm cycle, the Trump administration has gathered millions of state voter records for law enforcement purposes, endeavored to restrict mail-in voting nationwide , declined the typical practice of inviting international election observers and repeatedly raised the idea of dispatching armed federal personnel to voting locations .

The Trump administration broadly describes its actions as an effort to ensure the integrity of the American democratic system after the president's signature election overhaul effort, the SAVE America Act, foundered in the GOP-led Senate.

In a statement to NPR in October, White House spokeswoman Lauren Bis said that "President Trump has done more than any other President to ensure we have free and fair elections. While extreme Democrats and the media continue to dismiss concerns about voter fraud, the Trump Administration is taking decisive action to protect our elections including prosecuting election crimes, strengthening election infrastructure security, and protecting vulnerable voters from fraud and coercion."

This summer, NPR spoke to more than a dozen people who've formed what they describe as an election protection task force. It's a coordinated effort between Democratic lawmakers and their staffers, election litigators, scholars and nonpartisan good governance organizations.

Those involved worry that the administration will point to normal, but poorly understood, parts of American election infrastructure, including slow vote counting in California and Alaska, as evidence of fraudulent behavior. They also say that the administration has long worked to undermine public trust in a secure and transparent election system and has, without constitutional authority, inserted the executive branch into the state-led election process.

Democracy Forward — a legal nonprofit that says it works to advance democracy and social progress through litigation, policy and public education — has written that the Trump administration's efforts "harness the president's longstanding and baseless conspiracy theories in pursuit of discovering so-called 'election fraud.' These actions are reckless and run the risk of intimidating and disenfranchising voters."

Even as task force members acknowledged there is no magic "protect democracy" button tucked away in a Capitol cloakroom, they each emphasized the power of legislators as messengers and organizers. Their primary goal is to to prepare the public and their state and local counterparts to act when necessary to ensure election results are honored.
"We have very important elections coming up," Trump said in a July address from the East Room of the White House. "We want those elections to be honest."

He used the speech to call on Congress to pass the SAVE America Act, which would, among other measures, require voters to show proof of citizenship when registering to vote and a photo ID before they can cast a ballot.

"How easy is that to do, unless you want to cheat? The only reason you wouldn't do it is you want to cheat because your policies are so bad, and your candidates are so pathetic that you can't get away or can't get elected any other way," he said.
Members of the Democratic task force said the remarks should be understood as an effort to make voter fraud — which studies and investigations have found to be vanishingly rare — seem plausible.

Justin Vail, a leader at Protect Democracy, a cross-ideological group that says it uses litigation, advocacy and research to protect American elections is a member of the task force. He previously served as a special assistant to President Joe Biden, working on democracy issues. He told NPR that Trump's speech was an effort to sow doubt in November's elections, a first step in what his organization characterizes as a three-step playbook: deceive, disrupt and deny.

"First, he deceives Americans, manufacturing false claims about voter fraud and the security of our elections," Vail said. "Second, he seeks to disrupt the normal state and local management of elections," he continued, "in an attempt to coerce them to enact policies that threaten the eligible voters' access. And if that's all not enough, Trump is prepared to outright deny election results that he doesn't like."
Marc Elias, the prominent election litigator and a member of the task force, describes the election protection effort on a continuum.
body_zh: 以下是国会民主党人如何为选举舞弊索赔做准备：NPR
以下是国会民主党人如何为选举舞弊指控做准备国会民主党人正在与善治团体合作，针对任何潜在的选举舞弊指控制定行动计划。
以下是国会民主党人如何为选举舞弊索赔做准备
国会民主党人正在组建一个特别工作组来保护选举结果
在 11 月 3 日中期选举之前，选民已经在多个州进行投票。RYAN MURPHY/法新社 隐藏标题栏
这个故事是根据八月份首次报道的故事进行更新的。
在这个中期周期中，特朗普政府出于执法目的收集了数百万份州选民记录，努力限制全国范围内的邮寄投票，拒绝邀请国际选举观察员的典型做法，并多次提出派遣武装联邦人员前往投票地点的想法。
特朗普政府将其行动概括地描述为在总统标志性的选举改革计划《拯救美国法案》在共和党领导的参议院失败后，为确保美国民主制度完整性而做出的努力。
白宫发言人劳伦·比斯 (Lauren Bis) 在 10 月份向 NPR 发表的一份声明中表示，“特朗普总统在确保我们进行自由和公平的选举方面所做的工作比任何其他总统都多。虽然极端民主党人和媒体继续忽视对选民欺诈的担忧，但特朗普政府正在采取果断行动来保护我们的选举，包括起诉选举犯罪、加强选举基础设施安全以及保护弱势选民免受欺诈和胁迫。”
今年夏天，美国国家公共广播电台采访了十几位人士，他们组成了他们所说的选举保护工作组。这是民主党立法者及其工作人员、选举诉讼律师、学者和无党派善政组织之间的协调努力。
相关人士担心，政府将把美国选举基础设施中正常但人们知之甚少的部分（包括加利福尼亚州和阿拉斯加的计票速度缓慢）作为欺诈行为的证据。他们还表示，政府长期以来一直致力于破坏公众对安全和透明选举制度的信任，并在没有宪法授权的情况下将行政部门插入国家主导的选举程序。
民主前进是一家合法的非营利组织，自称致力于通过诉讼、政策和公共教育推动民主和社会进步。该组织写道，特朗普政府的努力“利用总统长期以来毫无根据的阴谋论来发现所谓的‘选举舞弊’。”这些行为是鲁莽的，有恐吓和剥夺选民选举权的风险。”
尽管工作组成员承认国会大厦衣帽间里并不存在神奇的“保护民主”按钮，但他们每个人都强调立法者作为信使和组织者的力量。他们的主要目标是让公众以及州和地方同行做好准备，在必要时采取行动，确保选举结果得到尊重。
“我们即将举行非常重要的选举，”特朗普在白宫东厅的七月讲话中说道。 “我们希望这些选举是诚实的。”
他在演讲中呼吁国会通过《拯救美国法案》，该法案除其他措施外，还要求选民在登记投票时出示公民身份证明，并在投票前出示带照片的身份证件。
“除非你想作弊，否则做起来有多容易？你不这样做的唯一原因是你想作弊，因为你的政策太糟糕了，你的候选人太可悲了，你无法逃脱或无法通过任何其他方式当选，”他说。
民主党特别工作组的成员表示，这些言论应该被理解为试图让选民欺诈——研究和调查发现这种行为极其罕见——看起来似乎合理。
保护民主组织（Protect Democracy）的领导人贾斯汀·韦尔（Justin Vail）是该工作组的成员之一，该组织是一个跨意识形态的组织，自称利用诉讼、宣传和研究来保护美国选举。他此前曾担任总统乔·拜登的特别助理，致力于民主问题。他告诉 NPR，特朗普的讲话是为了在 11 月的选举中播下怀疑的种子，这是他的组织所描述的三步剧本的第一步：欺骗、破坏和否认。
韦尔说：“首先，他欺骗美国人，制造有关选民欺诈和我们选举安全的虚假声明。” “其次，他试图扰乱州和地方对选举的正常管理，”他继续说道，“试图迫使他们制定威胁合格选民参与的政策。如果这还不够，特朗普准备彻底否认他不喜欢的选举结果。”
著名选举诉讼律师兼工作组成员马克·埃利亚斯 (Marc Elias) 描述了选举保护工作的连续过程。

body_en: New book makes fiery claims about Jared Kushner’s finances in Trump’s first term
Kushner threatens to sue, denying allegations that two slush funds were set up to influence his Middle East role
A new book containing incendiary claims about Jared Kushner ’s financial dealings during Donald Trump ’s first term has ignited a political and media firestorm.

The book by author Matthew Cole is called Princes and Thieves: Jared Kushner and Mohamed bin Zayed’s Secret Plot to Remake the Middle East and was released in the US this week. An excerpt was published by Vanity Fair last Thursday, and immediately drew a furious response from Kushner, who called its claims “completely insane”. The book contains numerous allegations about Kushner, whose father-in-law is Trump and who has served as one of his top diplomatic envoys in the Middle East – the most explosive of which are claims linking him to huge bank accounts allegedly funded by Gulf states.

Kusher denounced the book on his site last week, and writing on X : “We denied every one of these claims on the record, yet the author failed to provide a single shred of evidence to substantiate any of them.” He has demanded that Vanity Fair retract the excerpt and has threatened legal action against the book’s publisher, Simon & Schuster.

He added: “During the period in question, I was one of the most scrutinized people in the world, subjected to intense media coverage, multiple congressional investigations, and a special counsel investigation. I voluntarily cooperated with these investigations, providing over 30 hours of testimony. None of these allegations ever surfaced, because none of these events ever happened.”
The Guardian contacted Kushner’s legal counsel from Clare Locke as well as Chad Mizelle for comment and received no response.

Cole’s sources are predominantly anonymous and he does not print images of emails or other documentation to support his reporting. Extensive footnotes indicate sources of information, including confidential interviews.

In the book, the top intelligence official in the United Arab Emirates, Ali Al Shamsi, is reported to have called Kushner “the most expensive employee we’ve ever had”. The book details alleged payments into two “slush fund” bank accounts allegedly set up for Kushner by Emirati prince Mohamed bin Zayed (MBZ) and Saudi Arabian prince Mohammed bin Salman (MBS) during Trump’s first term. The Guardian contacted the Saudi Arabian and Emirati embassies for comment and did not receive a response.
In the book, Cole claims the accounts were partially managed by Kushner on an iPhone hacked by Russian and Dutch intelligence.

But despite the Emirati spymaster’s opinion of Kushner, Cole alleges that the New Jersey real estate scion was not entirely trusted. Cole describes a dangerous world in which blackmail is as common a tool of statecraft as torture and murder, as in the cases of the Saudi journalist Jamal Khashoggi, killed on the orders of MBS in Turkey in 2018, and the Emirati journalist and poet Habib Al Sayegh , whose killing by agents of MBZ in 2019 is described by Cole.

Kushner continues to steer US foreign policy despite having no official role, with questions about his business interests accompanying him as he travels the world with New York real estate magnate Steve Witkoff, this week seeking peace in Ukraine, if on terms favorable to Russia.

In response, an attorney “who has represented President Trump in multiple defamation lawsuits”, Alejandro Brito, told Cole that, “during his time working for President Trump, Kushner ‘always represented and sought the interests of the United States and the President of the United States and did not make any agreements or arrangements with leaders or officials in foreign countries that were not agreed by the President of the United States and in the best interests of the United States.’” He further said that “[a]ny allegation that Kushner knew of, had access to, had authorization for or engaged in or directed any conduct related to any government-funded or government-linked bank account is totally false and defamatory”.
Brito told Cole that “‘there are no accounts and never were.’” Cole writes that the Dutch government refused to comment in response to his questions about the alleged hacking of Kushner’s phone.

According to Cole, MBZ and MBS wanted Kushner to help achieve their “vision of a new Middle East, one in which Israel would become an integral part of the region, recognized diplomatically by Gulf Arabs today and eventually by the rest of the Arab world; the Palestinians would end their conflict with Israel and accept a peace built on prosperity; Islamic extremism would be defeated; and Iran’s expansionism and militancy would retreat, either by persuasion or force.”

Nearly 10 years later, the US and Israel are planning new strikes in their eight-month war with Iran; Saudi Arabia is at war with Houthi rebels in Yemen, and Israel has killed more than 74,000 Palestinians in Gaza since the Hamas attacks of 7 October 2023.

Kushner entered Trump’s first administration with his wife, Ivanka Trump, as close presidential advisers. MBZ and MBS, Cole claims, saw a chance to secure the best access money could buy. Cole alleges that in early 2017 the two princes “proposed to give Kushner a fund, a bank account, which the two leaders, working with Jared, would use to identify and pay for projects and foreign policy goals to advance for President Trump’s benefit”.

According to Cole, an idea to fund Trump’s proposed wall on the US border with Mexico apparently did not work out but the author claims that “MBZ and MBS initially, and then MBZ alone, put at least $2bn into at least two banks for Kushner.” Classifying the accounts as “Alpha” and “Beta”, Cole claims the Alpha account was held at First Abu Dhabi Bank, the largest in UAE, and contained “roughly $750m” to be “used as a foreign policy fund” overseen by Kushner and MBZ and meant to help end the Israel-Palestine conflict.

Cole quotes a source who says he knew of the UAE’s alleged deal with Kushner as saying: “‘Jared was looking for shortcuts in his diplomacy.’” Cole writes: “This person held discussions with both senior UAE and Israeli officials about the secret financial arrangement between Kushner, the UAE, and, at least initially, Saudi Arabia. ‘Jared promised MBZ that he’d push their agenda with Trump if they participated in a fund. He wanted normalization with Israel so that business could take off,’” the source alleged.

The same source claimed that “a slush fund – a shared pool of money for off-the-books diplomatic objectives – was a common form of Gulf Arab government corruption … ‘The Emiratis and the Saudis do this once a year. A billion or two is nothing for them, and if it gets them what they want, it’s money well spent.’”
body_zh: 新书对特朗普第一任期内贾里德·库什纳的财务状况提出了激烈的主张
库什纳威胁要提起诉讼，否认设立两个行贿基金以影响他在中东角色的指控
一本新书包含有关贾里德·库什纳在唐纳德·特朗普第一任期内的金融交易的煽动性言论，引发了一场政治和媒体风暴。
作者马修·科尔的书名为《王子与小偷：贾里德·库什纳和穆罕默德·本·扎耶德重塑中东的秘密阴谋》，本周在美国发行。 《名利场》上周四发表了一段摘录，立即引起了库什纳的愤怒回应，他称其说法“完全疯狂”。这本书包含了许多关于库什纳的指控，库什纳的岳父是特朗普，曾担任特朗普驻中东的高级外交特使之一——其中最具爆炸性的是，指控他与据称由海湾国家资助的巨额银行账户有联系。
库舍尔上周在他的网站上谴责了这本书，并在 X 上写道：“我们否认了记录中的每一项指控，但作者未能提供一丝证据来证实其中任何一项。”他要求《名利场》撤回该摘录，并威胁对该书的出版商西蒙与舒斯特采取法律行动。
他补充道：“在这段时期，我是世界上最受关注的人之一，受到媒体的广泛报道、多项国会调查和特别检察官的调查。我自愿配合这些调查，提供了 30 多个小时的证词。这些指控都没有浮出水面，因为这些事件都没有发生过。”
《卫报》联系了库什纳的法律顾问克莱尔·洛克（Clare Locke）和查德·米泽尔（Chad Mizelle）征求意见，但没有得到回应。
科尔的消息来源主要是匿名的，他不会打印电子邮件或其他文档的图像来支持他的报道。大量的脚注表明了信息来源，包括机密采访。
据报道，阿拉伯联合酋长国最高情报官员阿里·阿尔·沙姆西在书中称库什纳是“我们有史以来最昂贵的员工”。该书详细介绍了特朗普第一任期期间阿联酋王子穆罕默德·本·扎耶德（MBZ）和沙特阿拉伯王子穆罕默德·本·萨勒曼（MBS）据称为库什纳设立的两个“行贿基金”银行账户的付款情况。 《卫报》联系了沙特阿拉伯和阿联酋大使馆请其置评，但没有收到回复。
科尔在书中声称，这些账户的部分内容是由库什纳在一部被俄罗斯和荷兰情报机构黑客入侵的 iPhone 上管理的。

但尽管阿联酋间谍头子对库什纳有不同的看法，科尔声称这位新泽西房地产接班人并不完全值得信任。科尔描述了一个危险的世界，在这个世界中，勒索与酷刑和谋杀一样常见，是一种治国工具，例如 2018 年沙特记者贾迈勒·卡舒吉 (Jamal Khashoggi) 在土耳其被穆罕默德·本·穆罕默德 (MBS) 下令杀害，以及 2019 年阿联酋记者兼诗人哈比卜·阿尔·萨耶 (Habib Al Sayegh) 被 MBZ 特工杀害的案件。
库什纳尽管没有担任任何官方职务，但仍继续掌控美国外交政策，当他与纽约房地产巨头史蒂夫·威特科夫(Steve Witkoff)周游世界时，他的商业利益问题也随之而来。本周，他寻求在乌克兰实现和平，前提是条件对俄罗斯有利。
对此，一位“在多起诽谤诉讼中代表特朗普总统”的律师亚历杭德罗·布里托告诉科尔，“在为特朗普总统工作期间，库什纳‘始终代表并寻求美国和美国总统的利益，没有与外国领导人或官员达成任何未经美国总统同意且符合美国最大利益的协议或安排。’”他进一步表示，“任何指控库什纳知道、有权访问、获得授权、参与或指示任何与政府资助或政府关联的银行账户有关的行为都是完全虚假和诽谤性的”。
布里托告诉科尔，“‘没有任何账户，而且从来没有。’”科尔写道，荷兰政府拒绝就他有关库什纳手机被黑客入侵的问题发表评论。
科尔表示，穆罕默德·本·萨勒曼和穆罕默德·本·萨勒曼希望库什纳帮助实现他们的“新中东愿景，在这个愿景中，以色列将成为该地区不可分割的一部分，得到当今海湾阿拉伯国家的外交承认，并最终得到阿拉伯世界其他国家的承认；巴勒斯坦人将结束与以色列的冲突，接受建立在繁荣基础上的和平；伊斯兰极端主义将被击败；伊朗的扩张主义和好战情绪将通过说服或武力而消退。”
近十年后，美国和以色列正计划在与伊朗长达八个月的战争中发动新的袭击；沙特阿拉伯正在与也门胡塞叛军交战，自 2023 年 10 月 7 日哈马斯袭击以来，以色列已在加沙杀害了超过 74,000 名巴勒斯坦人。
库什纳与妻子伊万卡·特朗普一起进入特朗普第一届政府，担任总统的亲密顾问。科尔声称，MBZ 和 MBS 看到了获得金钱可以买到的最佳访问权限的机会。科尔声称，2017 年初，两位王子“提议向库什纳提供一笔基金，一个银行账户，两位领导人将与贾里德合作，用它来确定和支付项目和外交政策目标，以推进特朗普总统的利益”。
科尔表示，为特朗普提议的美墨边境隔离墙提供资金的想法显然没有成功，但作者声称“MBZ 和 MBS 最初，然后仅 MBZ 就为库什纳向至少两家银行投入了至少 20 亿美元。”科尔将这些账户分为“Alpha”和“Beta”，声称 Alpha 账户存放在阿联酋最大的阿布扎比​​第一银行，其中包含“大约 7.5 亿美元”，将被库什纳和 MBZ 监管“用作外交政策基金”，旨在帮助结束以色列-巴勒斯坦冲突。
科尔援引一位自称了解阿联酋与库什纳达成交易的消息人士的话称：“‘贾里德在外交上寻找捷径。’”科尔写道：“此人与阿联酋和以色列高级官员就库什纳、阿联酋以及沙特阿拉伯（至少在最初）之间的秘密财务安排进行了讨论。‘贾里德向 MBZ 承诺，如果他们参与一项基金，他将推动他们与特朗普的议程。他希望与以色列实现正常化，以便业务能够起飞。”据称。
同一消息人士称，“行贿基金——用于账外外交目标的共享资金池——是海湾阿拉伯国家政府腐败的一种常见形式……‘阿联酋人和沙特人每年都会这样做一次。一两个对他们来说没什么，如果这能让他们得到他们想要的东西，这笔钱花得值。’”

body_en: Keaton Denlay says agents handed him ‘poorly formatted Excel spreadsheet’ and threatened to criminally prosecute him

A California county elections official is speaking out about the Department of Justice’s campaign against purported “voter fraud”, saying federal officials provided him a disorganized list of names filled with inaccuracies – and threatened to criminally prosecute him if he didn’t take action.

Keaton Denlay, the county clerk-recorder for Butte county, a region north of Sacramento, said a federal agent on Friday hand-delivered what appeared to be a printout of a “poorly formatted Excel spreadsheet with missing and jumbled information”. The DoJ claimed the list was of 47 “likely” noncitizens who were unlawfully registered to vote and demanded the county set aside their ballots. But Denlay said the document was riddled with errors and lacking crucial details, and he declined to act on it.
body_zh: 基顿·丹莱 (Keaton Denlay) 表示，特工人员向他提供了“格式不良的 Excel 电子表格”，并威胁要对他进行刑事起诉
加州一名县选举官员公开谈论司法部打击所谓“选民欺诈”的运动，称联邦官员向他提供了一份杂乱无章的名单，其中充满了不准确之处，并威胁说，如果他不采取行动，将对他进行刑事起诉。
萨克拉门托以北地区比尤特县的县书记兼记录员基顿·丹莱 (Keaton Denlay) 表示，一名联邦特工周五亲手交付了一份似乎是“格式不良的 Excel 电子表格，其中信息缺失且混乱”的打印件。美国司法部声称，这份名单上有 47 名“可能”的非公民，他们非法登记投票，并要求该县搁置他们的选票。但丹莱表示，该文件充满错误，缺乏关键细节，他拒绝对此采取行动。

title_en: US ambassador suggests Trump could blame Canada if midterms don’t go his way
title_zh: 美国大使表示，如果中期选举不顺利，特朗普可能会责怪加拿大
summary: Pete Hoekstra, controversial US ambassador to Canada, has also accused Canadian officials of interfering in US elections The US ambassador has suggested Canada could be blamed if Republicans perform poorly in next week’s midterm elections, the latest intervent
summary_zh: 备受争议的美国驻加拿大大使皮特·霍克斯特拉(Pete Hoekstra)也指责加拿大官员干涉美国大选。
body_en: US ambassador suggests Trump could blame Canada if midterms don’t go his way
Pete Hoekstra, controversial US ambassador to Canada, has also accused Canadian officials of interfering in US elections

The US ambassador has suggested Canada could be blamed if Republicans perform poorly in next week’s midterm elections, the latest intervention from a controversial figure who has been accused of inflaming a bitter dispute that has angered and baffled residents of both countries.

On Wednesday, CTV news reported that Pete Hoekstra told business leaders at a closed door meeting that if a number of swing races – including Maine and Michigan – go to the Democrats, it could make things harder for Canada because Donald Trump might try to blame the loss on it.
“That’s an interesting way of framing it,” the prime minister, Mark Carney , told reporters when asked about the allegations.
For months, Canada and the US have been locked in a bitter tariff war, with Ottawa retaliating against illegal US tariffs and targeting goods in states that rely heavily on trade with Canada.
Carney said that Canada “will pursue” such a deal if it presents itself, but that Ottawa’s trade negotiators are “not in that position right now”.

Hoekstra is a deeply polarizing figure in Canada, particular for his response to Trump’s rhetoric about making Canada the 51st US state. Speaking to a Michigan radio station last year, he described the threats as a “sign of affection” and questioned why Canadians were offended by what he characterized as a “generous offer”. He had previously described Canada’s 2025 federal election as “anti-American”.

This year a House of Commons petition signed by more than 225,000 Canadians called for his expulsion, suggesting his statements violated diplomatic protocols, including the prohibition on diplomats interfering in the internal affairs of a host country.

More recently, Hoekstra has accused Canadian officials of interfering in US elections, pointing to Canadian politicians who have criticized the tariffs in US media, and the province of Ontario’s anti-tariff advertisement that ran on US television.

“We see all of that. We are monitoring it. We are evaluating it. And if some of it becomes election interference, America will respond to it,” Hoekstra, who comes from Michigan, recently told a Canadian podcast , adding that Canadians should “keep your nose out of American politics”.

Canada’s industry minister, Mélanie Joly, who was a target of Hoekstra’s comments, told reporters in Ottawa that her country “would never do that” and said Canada would “never accept that also being done to us in Canada”.
Carney, while in Turkey, told reporters there was “no merit” to the claims of interference and that he was “disappointed that their envoy sees that as his role, to make these suggestions”.

Roland Paris, the director of the Graduate School of Public and International Affairs at the University of Ottawa and a foreign affairs adviser to the former Canadian prime minister Justin Trudeau, said the remarks were an “extraordinary thing” for a US ambassador to say about his host country and looked like an effort to “manufacture a pretext for the Trump administration’s own political difficulties”.
“The job of an ambassador is to represent the interests of his country, but it’s also to maintain channels of communication and build relationships and manage disagreements,” he said.

“His comments have repeatedly aggravated tensions instead of helping to manage them. I don’t think that he’s serving American interests very well. I’m not even sure that he’s serving the interests of his president.”

Paris points to polling in the US that shows voters have increasingly linked tariffs, the war and cost of living. There is also widespread confusion over why the White House has chosen to treat Canada as a trade adversary.

“It’s certainly not working in Canada. It’s on the contrary. It seems that every time Mr Hoekstra opens his mouth, the Canadians are more determined than before to stand up to the bullying of the Trump administration,” he said. “That’s not serving American interests.”
The US embassy denied Hoekstra said Canada would face blame for a poor Republican showing, suggesting the remarks were “grossly taken out of context” from a broader discussion.

“The ambassador has consistently said that the Canadian media is attempting to overstate the relevance of Canadian issues in American elections. As we have previously stated, Americans will decide American elections based on issues that are important to them,” the embassy said in a statement.
body_zh: 美国大使表示，如果中期选举不顺利，特朗普可能会责怪加拿大
备受争议的美国驻加拿大大使皮特·霍克斯特拉(Pete Hoekstra)也指责加拿大官员干涉美国大选
美国大使表示，如果共和党在下周的中期选举中表现不佳，加拿大可能会受到指责，这是一位有争议的人物的最新干预行动，他被指控煽动一场激烈的争端，这场争端激怒了两国居民，让两国居民感到困惑。
周三，CTV 新闻报道称，皮特·霍克斯特拉 (Pete Hoekstra) 在一次闭门会议上告诉商界领袖，如果包括缅因州和密歇根州在内的一些摇摆竞选落入民主党手中，这可能会让加拿大的处境变得更加困难，因为唐纳德·特朗普可能会试图将失败归咎于民主党。
“这是一种有趣的表述方式，”英国首相马克·卡尼在被问及这些指控时告诉记者。
几个月来，加拿大和美国一直陷入激烈的关税战，渥太华对美国的非法关税进行报复，并针对严重依赖加拿大贸易的州的商品。
卡尼表示，如果这样的协议出现，加拿大“将寻求”达成，但渥太华的贸易谈判代表“目前不处于这个位置”。
霍克斯特拉在加拿大是一个两极分化严重的人物，特别是他对特朗普关于让加拿大成为美国第 51 个州的言论的回应。去年，他在密歇根一家广播电台发表讲话时，将这些威胁描述为“感情的表现”，并质疑为什么加拿大人会对他所说的“慷慨的提议”感到冒犯。他此前曾将加拿大2025年联邦选举形容为“反美”。
今年，超过 225,000 名加拿大人签署的一份下议院请愿书要求将他驱逐出境，称他的言论违反了外交协议，包括禁止外交官干涉东道国内政的规定。
最近，霍克斯特拉指责加拿大官员干涉美国大选，并指出加拿大政界人士在美国媒体上批评关税，以及美国电视上播放的安大略省反关税广告。
来自密歇根州的霍克斯特拉最近在加拿大播客上表示：“我们正在监视它。我们正在评估它。如果其中一些成为选举干扰，美国将会做出回应。”他补充说，加拿大人应该“不要插手美国政治”。
加拿大工业部长梅兰妮·乔利（Mélanie Joly）是霍克斯特拉言论的目标，她在渥太华告诉记者，她的国家“永远不会这样做”，并表示加拿大“永远不会接受加拿大也对我们这样做”。
卡尼在土耳其期间告诉记者，干涉的说法“没有任何依据”，他“对他们的特使认为这是他的职责并提出这些建议感到失望”。
渥太华大学公共与国际事务研究生院院长、加拿大前总理贾斯汀·特鲁多的外交顾问罗兰·帕里斯表示，美国大使对东道国发表这样的言论是“不同寻常的事情”，看起来像是“为特朗普政府自身的政治困境制造借口”。
“大使的工作是代表国家利益，但也要维持沟通渠道、建立关系并处理分歧，”他说。
“他的言论一再加剧紧张局势，而不是帮助解决紧张局势。我认为他没有很好地服务于美国的利益。我什至不确定他是否正在服务于他的总统的利益。”
巴黎指出，美国的民意调查显示，选民越来越多地将关税、战争和生活成本联系起来。对于白宫为何选择将加拿大视为贸易对手也存在广泛的困惑。
“这在加拿大肯定行不通。恰恰相反。霍克斯特拉先生每次开口，加拿大人似乎都比以前更有决心反抗特朗普政府的欺凌，”他说。 “这不符合美国的利益。”
美国大使馆否认了霍克斯特拉所说的加拿大将因共和党表现不佳而受到指责的说法，并暗示这些言论是从更广泛的讨论中“严重断章取义”的。
“大使一直表示，加拿大媒体试图夸大加拿大问题在美国选举中的相关性。正如我们之前所说，美国人将根据对他们来说重要的问题来决定美国选举，”大使馆在一份声明中表示。

body_en: RFK Jr assailed over ‘wildly racist tirade’ about Arabs at Michigan campaign stop
US health secretary falsely claims at Mike Rogers rally that Arabs have never won major prizes in science or literature

Robert F Kennedy Jr , the US health secretary, faced backlash on Wednesday for a “wildly racist tirade” during a campaign stop in Michigan in which he falsely asserted that Arabs never won leading awards in science or literature.

Kennedy was speaking at the Monday night event in Grand Rapids in support of Mike Rogers, the Republican US Senate candidate trailing his Democratic midterms opponent Abdul El-Sayed , who is Muslim, in polling.

“There’s 500 million Arabs in the world, and yet they don’t produce science, they don’t win the ⁠Nobel prize, they don’t win the Fields prize, they don’t win the Wolf prize, they don’t produce literature,” Kennedy said.
A factcheck published on Tuesday by the Associated Press showed that Arabs have won, or been shortlisted, for all those awards in recent years.

The ⁠Council on American-Islamic Relations called Kennedy’s Islamophobic remarks “a ⁠textbook display of ​unvarnished racism and bigotry”, and the US healthcare advocacy organization Protect Our Care condemned his “wildly racist tirade”.
JD Vance steps up extreme attacks on Democratic Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed
Hillary Scholten, a Democratic congresswoman representing west Michigan, who declined to endorse El-Sayed this summer, said Kennedy’s comments were “disgraceful and have no place in public service”.

In a statement posted to her Facebook page late Tuesday, Scholten said: “As secretary of health and human services, he has a responsibility to serve all Americans, not use his position to demean entire communities with bigoted and demonstrably false claims.

“Arab Americans are our neighbors, colleagues, health care professionals, scientists, educators, and public servants. Their contributions to science, literature, medicine, and countless other fields are undeniable.
“The last I checked, Secretary Kennedy has neither a medical degree nor a Nobel peace prize, and his rhetoric has undermined public confidence in health science. Maybe he should sit this one out.”
Kennedy’s comments came as part of an attack on the Muslim Brotherhood , a global Islamic group with branches that have been designated terrorist organizations by the US government.

The rise of the group had “created stagnant societies”, Kennedy said, ending what he called “a golden age [in which] Islamic lands were the center, the foundation for art and literature and science and engineering, and they were highly tolerant and pluralistic and cosmopolitan”.

Other Trump administration officials have tried to paint El-Sayed as a supporter of Islamic radicalism, including the president himself, who at a rally in Port Huron, Michigan, on Sunday called the Democrat “a jihadist” who was “on the side of the terrorists”.

JD Vance, the vice-president, escalated the inflammatory attacks at an event in Howell, Michigan, on Tuesday, during which he sought to connect El-Sayed’s politics to violent leftwing protests in Paris that saw thousands arrested.

“I guarantee you, if those rioters were burning down New York, or Detroit, the Hasan Pikers and El-Sayeds would be right there leading them and cheering them on,” Vance said, referring to Piker , an outspoken socialist commentator and influencer .

Rogers has also spoken out against El-Sayed’s alleged links to the Muslim Brotherhood, despite questions over his own relationship with the group. In 2012, as chair of the House intelligence committee, he said the US should have talks with the movement after Mohamed Morsi, who was backed by the Muslim Brotherhood, won the Egyptian election.

El-Sayed has repeatedly denied any ties to the group, and disavowed it in a town hall event in Michigan last week that went viral for a confrontation over the issue with a heckler who turned out to be a former aide to Josh Hawley, the Republican US senator for Missouri.
Chris Murphy, the US senator for Connecticut who joined other senior Democratic politicians canvassing for El-Sayed in Michigan last week, also condemned Kennedy’s comments.
body_zh: 小肯尼迪因在密歇根州竞选站对阿拉伯人进行“疯狂的种族主义长篇大论”而受到攻击
美国卫生部长在迈克·罗杰斯集会上错误地声称阿拉伯人从未赢得过科学或文学方面的重大奖项
周三，美国卫生部长小罗伯特·F·肯尼迪(Robert F Kennedy Jr)因在密歇根州竞选期间发表“疯狂的种族主义长篇大论”而遭到强烈反对，他在演讲中错误地声称阿拉伯人从未赢得过科学或文学方面的领先奖项。
肯尼迪周一晚上在大急流城举行的活动中发表讲话，支持美国共和党参议员候选人迈克·罗杰斯(Mike Rogers)。罗杰斯在民意调查中落后于他的民主党中期选举对手阿卜杜勒·赛义德(Abdul El-Sayed)，后者是穆斯林。
“世界上有 5 亿阿拉伯人，但他们没有创造科学，他们没有赢得诺贝尔奖，他们没有赢得菲尔兹奖，他们没有赢得沃尔夫奖，他们没有创作文学，”肯尼迪说。
美联社周二发布的事实核查显示，阿拉伯人近年来赢得或入围了所有这些奖项。
美国伊斯兰关系委员会称肯尼迪的仇视伊斯兰言论是“教科书式的赤裸裸的种族主义和偏执”，美国医疗保健倡导组织“保护我们的关怀”谴责了他的“疯狂的种族主义长篇大论”。
JD 万斯加大对民主党参议院候选人阿卜杜勒·赛义德的极端攻击力度
代表西密歇根州的民主党女议员希拉里·肖尔滕今年夏天拒绝支持埃尔·赛义德，她表示肯尼迪的言论“可耻，在公共服务中没有地位”。
周二晚间，肖尔滕在她的脸书页面上发布了一份声明，她说：“作为卫生与公众服务部部长，他有责任为所有美国人服务，而不是利用他的职位，用偏执和明显虚假的言论来贬低整个社区。
“阿拉伯裔美国人是我们的邻居、同事、医疗保健专业人员、科学家、教育工作者和公务员。他们对科学、文学、医学和无数其他领域的贡献是不可否认的。
“我上次查到，肯尼迪国务卿既没有医学学位，也没有诺贝尔和平奖，他的言论削弱了公众对健康科学的信心。也许他应该袖手旁观。”
肯尼迪的言论是针对穆斯林兄弟会的攻击的一部分，穆斯林兄弟会是一个全球性的伊斯兰组织，其分支机构已被美国政府认定为恐怖组织。
肯尼迪说，该组织的崛起“造成了停滞的社会”，结束了他所谓的“黄金时代，在这个时代，伊斯兰土地是中心，是艺术、文学和科学与工程的基础，他们高度宽容、多元化和国际化”。
特朗普政府的其他官员试图将埃尔-赛义德描绘成伊斯兰激进主义的支持者，其中包括总统本人，他周日在密歇根州休伦港的一次集会上称这位民主党人是“圣战分子”，“站在恐怖分子一边”。
副总统 JD 万斯周二在密歇根州豪厄尔举行的一次活动中升级了煽动性攻击，期间他试图将埃尔赛义德的政治观点与巴黎的暴力左翼抗议活动联系起来，该抗议活动导致数千人被捕。
“我向你保证，如果那些暴徒烧毁纽约或底特律，哈桑·派克和埃尔-赛义德就会在那里领导他们并为他们加油，”万斯说，他指的是直言不讳的社会主义评论员和影响者派克。
罗杰斯还公开反对埃尔赛义德与穆斯林兄弟会的所谓联系，尽管他本人与该组织的关系受到质疑。 2012年，作为众议院情报委员会主席，他表示，在穆斯林兄弟会支持的穆罕默德·穆尔西赢得埃及大选后，美国应该与该运动进行对话。
埃尔-赛义德一再否认与该组织有任何联系，并在上周密歇根州的一次市政厅活动中否认了这一点，该活动因与一名质问者发生冲突而走红，而这名质问者原来是美国密苏里州共和党参议员乔什·霍利的前助手。
美国康涅狄格州参议员克里斯·墨菲上周与其他民主党高级政治家一起在密歇根州为埃尔·赛义德拉票，他也谴责了肯尼迪的言论。

body_en: Up First briefing: Midterms; Israel; Fed Reserve rate cuts; Ebola : NPR

Up First briefing: Midterms; Israel; Fed Reserve rate cuts; Ebola Israeli voters turned out in record numbers, and the results remain too close to call. And, more than 10,000 people have been infected with Ebola since the outbreak was first declared in May.

Israel's election too close to call. And, the Ebola outbreak reaches grim milestone
Trump Rallies For Republicans, Israel Election Results, Fed Interest Rates Meeting

Midterm ad spending has surpassed a record $11 billion , according to Ad Impact. An NPR analysis found that candidates in four major Senate races spent more than $15 million on fundraising ads in the 2025-26 election cycle. Meanwhile, President Trump has been campaigning in tight races across states like Texas, Mississippi, and Kansas.

🎧 Trump has not been sticking with his standard midterm pitch , which includes touting GOP tax cuts and attacking Democrats, NPR's Danielle Kurtzleben tells Up First . His jokes, including comments about Ohio Sen. Jon Husted's physique, entertain rally crowds but distract from the key issues the median voter cares about, like the economy and gas prices. Midterm turnout is usually low, but the GOP base still supports him, suggesting many MAGA votes are available, Kurtzleben says. But Trump needing to rally votes in very red states indicates a potential problem for his party.

The election in Israel is too close to call after voters turned out in record numbers to decide whether to keep Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu in office or oust him for an alternative. Netanyahu was in a tight race with his top rival Gadi Eisenkot, a center-right former military chief of staff. Final vote tallies may take time, and if no bloc secures a majority, it could take days or weeks for party leaders to form a governing coalition and determine the next prime minister.

🎧 Israelis went to bed thinking Eisenkot had the advantage , but by morning, Netanyahu pulled ahead, making the election too close to call, NPR's Daniel Estrin says. Election officials tell NPR that they expect to finish counting votes by tomorrow afternoon. The leading candidate will have six weeks to form a governing coalition, likely competing for support from defectors in each other's camps. Eisenkot could gain the majority of lawmakers' support in parliament, thanks to a strong showing from Arab-led parties eager to see him as prime minister. Eisenkot's camp is hesitant to form a coalition with Arab parties due to mistrust and demonization of Arab political leaders after the Oct. 7, 2023, attacks, Estrin says. He adds that both candidates don't have a clear path to a majority coalition.
The Federal Reserve typically combats inflation by raising interest rates. While prices are currently rising faster than average wages, investors don't expect a rate hike at today's meeting.

🎧 The Labor Department's latest cost-of-living report shows consumer prices rose 3.7% in September compared to last year. NPR's Scott Horsley says that marks a larger annual increase than the previous month. Fed policymakers raised interest rates in September, but investors believe the central bank will remain low-key ahead of Election Day and may increase rates again in December.

The Ebola outbreak has surpassed 10,000 people infected since its declaration in May , according to the latest figures from the Democratic Republic of Congo. This outbreak has spread faster than any in history . It is also the largest in geographic scope, spanning from Nigeria to Kenya, and is second in death toll with nearly 5,000 deaths. Around one-third of those who have died have been children.

The results of the 2026 midterm elections will shape the final two years of President Trump's second term and serve as a precursor to the 2028 general election. This month, Morning Edition is reporting from six states that could change the balance of power in Washington.

With Election Day less than a week away, Morning Edition 's Michel Martin went to the Midwest to hear from voters about what is important to them this midterm cycle. In Springfield, Ohio, the Trump administration has conducted an aggressive campaign to deport Haitian residents who have been living legally in the country with Temporary Protected Status. The administration revoked TPS for Haitians during Trump's second term. And in Michigan, Abdul El-Sayed has narrowly won the Democratic Senate nomination, a victory for the party's progressive wing. The swing state is important to both parties, which is why Trump and former President Barack Obama campaigned for their party's Senate candidate over the weekend.
Hear what voters in these two states had to say
🎧 In Michigan, many voters expressed burnout as they worry about gas prices and healthcare.
🎧 Trump's tariffs are hitting Michigan households harder than any other state because many people depend on cross-border trade. But voters affected said the issue isn't so clear-cut .
🎧 Winning a statewide office in Michigan without Detroit is challenging, and El-Sayed didn't perform well there in the primary. Some Black Detroiters said they remain skeptical of him .
🎧 Some Springfield, Ohio voters said they are voting early because they are angry about the administration's treatment of Haitians .

根据 Ad Impact 的数据，中期广告支出已超过创纪录的 110 亿美元。 NPR 分析发现，在 2025-26 年选举周期中，四场主要参议院竞选的候选人在筹款广告上花费了超过 1500 万美元。与此同时，特朗普总统一直在德克萨斯州、密西西比州和堪萨斯州等州进行激烈的竞选活动。

NPR 的丹妮尔·库茨莱本 (Danielle Kurtzleben) 告诉《Up First》，特朗普并没有坚持他的标准中期宣传，其中包括宣传共和党减税和攻击民主党。他的笑话，包括对俄亥俄州参议员乔恩·赫斯特德体格的评论，娱乐了集会人群，但分散了中间选民关心的关键问题的注意力，比如经济和汽油价格。库尔茨莱本说，中期选举投票率通常较低，但共和党基础仍然支持他，这表明有许多“MAGA”选票可用。但特朗普需要在非常红的州拉票，这表明他的政党存在潜在问题。
以色列的选举结果势均力敌，投票人数创历史新高，以决定是继续留任总理内塔尼亚胡还是罢免他以寻求替代方案。内塔尼亚胡与他的头号竞争对手、中右翼前军事参谋长加迪·艾森科特展开了激烈的竞争。最终计票结果可能需要时间，如果没有哪个集团获得多数席位，政党领导人可能需要数天或数周的时间才能组建执政联盟并确定下一任总理。

美国国家公共广播电台 (NPR) 的丹尼尔·埃斯特林 (Daniel Estrin) 表示，以色列人上床睡觉时认为艾森科特占据优势，但到了早上，内塔尼亚胡领先，使得选举结果势均力敌。选举官员告诉 NPR，他们预计将于明天下午完成计票。领先的候选人将有六周的时间组建执政联盟，可能会争夺彼此阵营中叛逃者的支持。由于阿拉伯领导的政党渴望看到他担任总理，艾森科特可能会在议会中获得大多数议员的支持。埃斯特林表示，由于 2023 年 10 月 7 日袭击事件后对阿拉伯政治领导人的不信任和妖魔化，艾森科特阵营对于与阿拉伯政党组建联盟犹豫不决。他补充说，两位候选人都没有明确的通往多数联盟的道路。
美联储通常通过提高利率来对抗通货膨胀。尽管目前物价上涨速度快于平均工资，但投资者预计今天的会议上不会加息。
🎧 劳工部最新生活成本报告显示，9月份消费者价格较去年上涨3.7%。 NPR 的斯科特·霍斯利 (Scott Horsley) 表示，这标志着年度增幅比上个月更大。美联储政策制定者在 9 月份加息，但投资者认为央行将在选举日之前保持低调，并可能在 12 月份再次加息。
根据刚果民主共和国的最新数据，自 5 月份宣布埃博拉疫情爆发以来，感染人数已超过 10,000 人。这次疫情的传播速度比历史上任何一次都要快。它的地理范围也是最大的，从尼日利亚到肯尼亚，死亡人数排名第二，有近 5,000 人死亡。死亡者中约有三分之一是儿童。
2026年中期选举的结果将决定特朗普总统第二任期的最后两年，并成为2028年大选的前兆。本月，《晨报》报道了六个可能改变华盛顿权力平衡的州。

距离选举日还有不到一周的时间，《晨报》的米歇尔·马丁前往中西部，听取选民的意见，了解本次中期选举对他们来说最重要的事情。在俄亥俄州斯普林菲尔德，特朗普政府开展了一场积极的运动，驱逐在该国合法居住且具有临时保护身份的海地居民。在特朗普第二任期内，政府取消了海地人的 TPS。在密歇根州，阿卜杜勒·赛义德以微弱优势赢得了民主党参议院提名，这是该党进步派的胜利。这个摇摆州对两党都很重要，这就是特朗普和前总统巴拉克·奥巴马周末竞选本党参议员候选人的原因。
听听这两个州的选民怎么说
🎧 在密歇根州，许多选民因担心汽油价格和医疗保健而表示精疲力尽。
🎧 特朗普的关税对密歇根州家庭的打击比任何其他州都严重，因为许多人依赖跨境贸易。但受影响的选民表示，这个问题并不那么明确。
🎧 在没有底特律的情况下赢得密歇根州的全州办公室具有挑战性，而埃尔赛义德在初选中表现不佳。一些底特律黑人表示，他们仍然对他持怀疑态度。
🎧 俄亥俄州斯普林菲尔德的一些选民表示，他们提前投票是因为他们对政府对待海地人的方式感到愤怒。

title_en: Trump says Peltola "shouldn't be allowed to run" due to second Dan Sullivan
title_zh: 特朗普表示，由于第二位丹·沙利文，佩尔托拉“不应该被允许参选”
summary: A report alleged that people aligned with Democrat Mary Peltola's campaign helped recruit a candidate with the same first and last name as Republican Sen. Dan Sullivan. Peltola denied the allegations.
summary_zh: 一份报告称，与民主党玛丽·佩尔托拉竞选团队结盟的人帮助招募了一名与共和党同名的候选人
body_en: Trump says Peltola "shouldn't be allowed to run" for Alaska Senate seat over report on why 2 Dan Sullivans are in the race - CBS News

President Trump said Democrat Mary Peltola "shouldn't be allowed to run" in next week's Alaska Senate race, after The New York Times reported that people aligned with Peltola's campaign helped recruit a candidate with the same first and last name as her main opponent, Republican Sen. Dan Sullivan.

"I don't think Mary Peltola, after perpetrating such a terrible scheme, should be allowed to run, because this is ELECTION FRAUD," the president wrote in one of several Truth Social posts about the issue. "The Democrats cheated!"
Peltola's campaign and the Democratic Senatorial Campaign Committee, or DSCC, have strongly denied any hand in getting the duplicate Sullivan on the ballot.

Voters in Alaska's closely watched Senate contest are choosing between four candidates who survived a nonpartisan primary earlier this year. Those include Peltola and Sullivan, along with a retired teacher named Daniel J. Sullivan Jr. The ballot — which allows voters to rank the candidates rather than just selecting one — identifies the sitting senator as a Republican and an incumbent, while Danial J. Sullivan Jr. has no party affiliation listed.

On Wednesday, the Times reported that a Democratic operative who worked with Peltola's campaign and national Democrats helped encourage Daniel J. Sullivan to run, citing text messages and interviews. The newspaper reported that it appeared to be part of a wider effort to draw more candidates into the race.

The second Sullivan has vexed Republicans for months, with the incumbent senator calling his same-name challenger a "sham candidate" who was trying to trick voters. Daniel J. Sullivan has denied those allegations and insisted he is genuinely interested in running for Senate.

State officials initially sought to keep him off the ballot, finding that he was trying to confuse voters and arguing his was not a "good-faith candidacy." The Alaska Supreme Court rejected that decision and ruled that the other Sullivan can appear on the ballot.

Last week, the Justice Department filed a lawsuit seeking to prevent the election from being certified if Sen. Dan Sullivan loses due to "voter confusion" about the dueling Sullivans, in what Attorney General Todd Blanche described as an effort to "put guardrails in place." Asked what he thought about the suit, Mr. Trump told reporters: "Well, I'm the one that said, 'Do it.'"
Nate Adams, a spokesperson for Sen. Dan Sullivan's campaign, said in a statement in reaction to the Times' reporting that "Alaskans deserve the truth."
"Mary Peltola and her campaign have spent months gaslighting Alaskans, denying a scheme they were running all along," Adams said.
Mr. Trump called the situation "voter fraud at the highest level" in comments to reporters.
"It's terrible what's happened in Alaska," he said Wednesday. "They created a fake candidate."
Democrats have denied any role in Daniel J. Sullivan's candidacy. A Peltola campaign spokesperson said it "has no involvement with either Sullivan campaign."

"Mary got in this race because Alaskans deserve a champion who is fighting to lower their costs and put Alaska first, and no tweet or threat from any DC politician will keep her away from that fight," the campaign spokesperson said.
A spokesperson for the DSCC, Senate Democrats' campaign arm, also said it "is not involved with Dan J. Sullivan."

The spokesperson argued Republicans "have a long history of recruiting and propping up candidates in an attempt to boost their own campaigns." The organization pointed to a man serving a 20-year prison sentence in New York who ran for Alaska's House seat in 2024, and an Arizona man who ran in this year's Alaska Senate primary.
Seiji Yamashita and Alan He contributed to this report.

body_zh: 特朗普表示，佩尔托拉“不应该被允许竞选”阿拉斯加参议院席位，原因是关于丹·沙利文两名成员参加竞选的原因的报道 - 哥伦比亚广播公司新闻
特朗普总统表示，民主党人玛丽·佩尔托拉“不应该被允许参加”下周的阿拉斯加州参议员竞选，此前《纽约时报》报道称，与佩尔托拉竞选团队结盟的人帮助招募了一名与她的主要对手、共和党参议员丹·沙利文同名的候选人。
“我认为玛丽·佩尔托拉在实施了如此可怕的计划后，不应该被允许参选，因为这是选举舞弊，”总统在有关该问题的几篇《真相社会》帖子中写道。 “民主党作弊了！”
佩尔托拉的竞选团队和民主党参议员竞选委员会（DSCC）强烈否认对让重复的沙利文参与投票有任何帮助。
阿拉斯加州备受关注的参议院竞选中，选民们正在今年早些时候的无党派初选中幸存的四名候选人中进行选择。其中包括佩尔托拉和沙利文，以及一位名叫小丹尼尔·J·沙利文的退休教师。投票允许选民对候选人进行排名，而不仅仅是选择一名候选人，将现任参议员确定为共和党人和现任参议员，而小丹尼尔·J·沙利文没有列出党派关系。
周三，《泰晤士报》援引短信和采访报道称，一名与佩尔托拉竞选团队和全国民主党合作的民主党工作人员帮助鼓励丹尼尔·J·沙利文参选。该报报道称，这似乎是吸引更多候选人参加竞选的更广泛努力的一部分。
第二任沙利文已经让共和党人烦恼了几个月，现任参议员称他的同名挑战者是试图欺骗选民的“假候选人”。丹尼尔·J·沙利文否认了这些指控，并坚称他确实有兴趣竞选参议员。
州官员最初试图阻止他参加投票，发现他试图迷惑选民，并认为他不是“善意的候选人”。阿拉斯加最高法院驳回了这一决定，并裁定另一位沙利文可以出现在选票上。
上周，司法部提起诉讼，寻求在参议员丹·沙利文因“选民对沙利文决斗感到困惑”而失败的情况下阻止选举获得认证，司法部长托德·布兰奇称这是为了“设置护栏”。当被问及对这套诉讼的看法时，特朗普告诉记者：“好吧，我就是那个说‘做吧’的人。”
参议员丹·沙利文竞选团队的发言人内特·亚当斯在一份声明中回应《纽约时报》的报道，称“阿拉斯加人应该知道真相”。
亚当斯说：“玛丽·佩尔托拉和她的竞选团队花了几个月的时间对阿拉斯加人进行煽动，否认他们一直在实施的计划。”
特朗普在对记者的评论中称这种情况是“最高级别的选民欺诈”。
“阿拉斯加发生的事情太可怕了，”他周三表示。 “他们创造了一个假候选人。”
民主党人否认与丹尼尔·J·沙利文的竞选有任何关系。佩尔托拉竞选团队发言人表示，它“与沙利文的竞选活动没有任何关系”。
竞选发言人说：“玛丽参加这场竞选是因为阿拉斯加人值得一位为降低成本而奋斗并将阿拉斯加放在第一位的冠军，任何华盛顿政客的推文或威胁都不会阻止她参加这场斗争。”
参议院民主党竞选部门 DSCC 的发言人也表示，该机构“与丹·J·沙利文无关”。
该发言人辩称，共和党人“长期以来一直在招募和支持候选人，以推动自己的竞选活动。”该组织指出，一名在纽约服刑 20 年徒刑的男子曾在 2024 年竞选阿拉斯加州众议院席位，而一名亚利桑那州男子则参加了今年阿拉斯加州的参议院初选。
Seiji Yamashita 和 Alan He 对本报告做出了贡献。

title_zh: 人们纷纷向劳工领袖多洛雷斯·韦尔塔致敬：“为农场工人奋斗到底”

summary_zh: 美国各地的立法者、活动人士和工会领导人缅怀联合农场工人工会的联合创始人
body_en: Tributes pour in for labor leader Dolores Huerta: ‘Fought for farm workers to the very end’
Lawmakers, activists and union leaders across the US remember the co-founder of United Farm Workers union

Following the news that Dolores Huerta – the civil rights icon who popularized the rallying cry “Sí, se puede! – had died at the age of 96 on Wednesday, activists, lawmakers and civil rights leaders paid tribute to Hureta’s long and lasting legacy.

In California – where Huerta helped found the United Farm Workers (UFW) union – her death was deeply felt. It was in California’s central valley that she laid the foundations for the United Farm Workers, and helped organize the 1965 Delano grape strike – a national boycott of table grapes that resulted in better wages and working conditions for grape pickers. Several schools in California bear her name, and murals across the state depict her likeness. And in 2018, California declared 10 April – her birthday – Dolores Huerta Day.
Dolores Huerta, California labor leader and civil rights champion, dies aged 96

“From the fields of California to the halls of Congress and the White House, Dolores dedicated her life to ensuring that every voice – especially those too often silenced – was heard,” said Hector Sanchez Barba, the president of the voter mobilization organization Mi Familia Vota. “Her historic rallying cry, ‘Sí, se puede,’ is not just a slogan; it is a living call to action that continues to unite and inspire millions across the world.”

“Our greatest monument to her memory is for the union she helped found to continue to grow. Dolores fought for farm workers to the very end of her life,” said UFW president Teresa Romero. “The greatest possible tribute to her life is for her work of organizing to continue.”

Huerta’s legacy is national and international; her portrait hangs at some US embassies and schools in several US states are named after her. She helped negotiate national immigration policy, and remained, until her death, intimately involved in promoting civil and labor rights in Washington DC and across the US.
Tributes also came from some of California’s biggest political names, including Nancy Pelosi, the former House speaker, Gavin Newsom, the governor, and former vice-president Kamala Harris .

“Dolores was a dear friend, and we all responded to her rallying cry, ‘Sí se puede,’ which inspired generations of Americans to believe in the power of collective action,” said Pelosi. “May it be a comfort to her family and loved ones that so many mourn their loss and are praying for them at this sad time.”

“I was blessed to know Dolores for many years and proud to organize alongside my dear friend to champion working families and immigrant rights,” said Harris. “I will always be grateful for her support and friendship. We will honor her legacy by continuing the fight for the dignity of every person.”

“Dolores Huerta represented the best of us,” said Newsom. “California – and the United States – would not be what we are today without her resolute spirit, her passion for justice and fairness, and her commitment to those overlooked and forgotten.”

“The best tribute we can pay is to carry on the work, which means standing with workers, defending civil rights and organizing for a more just California,” echoed Alex Padilla, US senator representing California.

“¡Adiós, Dolores! You were everywhere. You did everything,” said Xavier Becerra, the former California attorney general and former US health secretary who is running for governor. “If you want to know where a leader will take you, know where they come from. Dolores never let us forget where she came from. Si, se pudo [Yes, we did].”

Lawmakers across the US, including Alexandria Ocasio Cortez, the New York congressperson, also hailed her trailblazing legacy. “For decades after the Delano Grape Strike, she continued to organize for the rights of working people, women and immigrants. She continued to fight for the idea that when ordinary people come together, they can change the course of history,” said Ocasio Cortez. “While we mourn her devastating loss, we will continue her fight to build a country where every worker, regardless of race, gender, or economic status, is treated with dignity.”
Lawmakers thanked Huerta for her efforts to promote female candidates to public office.

Eloise Gómez Reyes, the state senator who brought legislation in 2018 to mark 10 April as Dolores Huerta Day in California, said that she was mourning “the loss of someone who profoundly shaped my own life”.

“Dolores Huerta taught generations of us that we did not have to accept the world as it was. That ordinary people, working together, could challenge powerful institutions, overcome injustice, and build something better. She didn’t simply open doors for women like me. She taught us that we had the power to open them for others,” Reyes said.

Hilda Solis, a former Democratic congresswoman who became the first Latina to serve in a cabinet position as Barack Obama’s labor secretary, thanked Huerta for her mentorship. “Growing up in the San Gabriel Valley, I rarely saw Latinas in positions of leadership. Dolores was one of the few women who showed me what was possible,” she said. “From the state legislature to Congress and my time serving in President Barack Obama’s cabinet, Dolores remained a constant in my life. We joined demonstrations and rallies, stood with workers fighting for their rights and demanded action when people in power looked away … Dolores understood the importance of showing up, bearing witness and refusing to let the suffering of women go ignored.”

Huerta for years was considered the second-in-command to UFW co-founder César Chávez – and spoke about how she had to fight the sexism within the movement, and was often forced to cede credit to Chávez. Earlier this year, in the aftermath of a New York Times investigation uncovering Chávez’ pattern of sexual abuse of women and girls, Huerta revealed that Chávez had raped her, too.
body_zh: 人们纷纷向劳工领袖多洛雷斯·韦尔塔致敬：“为农场工人奋斗到底”
美国各地的立法者、活动人士和工会领导人纪念联合农场工人工会的联合创始人
周三，民权偶像多洛雷斯·韦尔塔 (Dolores Huerta) 去世，享年 96 岁，她的口号是“Sí，se puede！”。继周三，活动人士、立法者和民权领袖向胡雷塔长期留下的遗产表示敬意。

在加利福尼亚州，韦尔塔帮助成立了联合农场工人工会 (UFW)，人们对她的去世深感悲痛。正是在加利福尼亚州的中央山谷，她为联合农场工人奠定了基础，并帮助组织了 1965 年的德拉诺葡萄罢工——一场全国性的抵制鲜食葡萄的运动，为葡萄采摘者带来了更好的工资和工作条件。加利福尼亚州的几所学校都以她的名字命名，全州的壁画都描绘了她的肖像。 2018 年，加州宣布 4 月 10 日——她的生日——多洛雷斯·韦尔塔日。
加州劳工领袖和民权斗士多洛雷斯·韦尔塔 (Dolores Huerta) 去世，享年 96 岁
选民动员组织 Mi Familia Vota 主席赫克托·桑切斯·巴尔巴 (Hector Sanchez Barba) 表示：“从加州的田野到国会大厅和白宫，多洛雷斯一生致力于确保每一个声音——尤其是那些经常被压制的声音——都能被听到。” “她历史性的战斗口号‘Sí，se puede’不仅仅是一个口号；它是一个活生生的行动号召，继续团结和激励全世界数百万人。”
UFW 主席特雷莎·罗梅罗 (Teresa Romero) 表示：“我们纪念她最伟大的纪念碑是她帮助建立的工会继续发展。多洛雷斯为农场工人奋斗到生命的最后一刻。” “对她一生最大的致敬就是让她的组织工作继续下去。”
韦尔塔的遗产是国家和国际的；她的肖像挂在一些美国大使馆，美国几个州的学校也以她的名字命名。她帮助谈判国家移民政策，并一直密切参与促进华盛顿特区和美国各地的公民和劳工权利，直至去世。
加州一些最著名的政治人物也表达了哀悼，包括前众议院议长南希·佩洛西、州长加文·纽瑟姆和前副总统卡马拉·哈里斯。
佩洛西说：“多洛雷斯是一位亲爱的朋友，我们都响应了她的战斗口号‘Sí se puede’，这激励了几代美国人相信集体行动的力量。” “在这个悲伤的时刻，这么多人哀悼她的去世并为他们祈祷，愿她的家人和亲人得到安慰。”
哈里斯说：“我很幸运认识多洛雷斯很多年，并很自豪能够与我亲爱的朋友一起组织起来捍卫工薪家庭和移民权利。” “我将永远感谢她的支持和友谊。我们将继续为每个人的尊严而奋斗，以纪念她的遗产。”
“多洛雷斯·韦尔塔代表了我们中最好的人，”纽瑟姆说。 “如果没有她坚定的精神、对正义和公平的热情以及对那些被忽视和遗忘的人的承诺，加州和美国就不会成为今天的样子。”
“我们能给予的最好的致敬就是继续工作，这意味着与工人站在一起，捍卫公民权利并组织起来建设一个更加公正的加州，”代表加州的美国参议员亚历克斯·帕迪拉(Alex Padilla)附和道。
“再见，多洛雷斯！你无处不在。你做了一切，”正在竞选州长的加州前总检察长、前美国卫生部长泽维尔·贝塞拉 (Xavier Becerra) 说道。 “如果你想知道领导者会带你去哪里，就知道他们来自哪里。多洛雷斯永远不会让我们忘记她来自哪里。Si, se pudo [是的，我们做到了]。”
包括纽约国会议员亚历山大·奥卡西奥·科尔特斯在内的美国各地立法者也对她的开创性遗产表示赞赏。 “德拉诺葡萄罢工后的几十年里，她继续为劳动人民、妇女和移民的权利组织起来。她继续为这样的理念而奋斗，即当普通人走到一起时，他们可以改变历史的进程，”奥卡西奥·科尔特斯说。 “在我们哀悼她的毁灭性损失的同时，我们将继续为建设一个让每个工人，无论种族、性别或经济状况如何，都受到尊严对待的国家而奋斗。”
立法者感谢韦尔塔为推动女性候选人担任公职所做的努力。
州参议员埃洛伊丝·戈麦斯·雷耶斯 (Eloise Gómez Reyes) 于 2018 年立法将 4 月 10 日定为加利福尼亚州的多洛雷斯·韦尔塔日 (Dolores Huerta Day)，她表示，她正在哀悼“失去了一位深刻影响了我自己生活的人”。
“多洛雷斯·韦尔塔教导我们几代人，我们不必接受世界本来的样子。普通人通过共同努力，可以挑战强大的机构，克服不公正，建设更好的国家。她不仅仅是为像我这样的女性打开大门。她告诉我们，我们有能力为其他人打开大门，”雷耶斯说。

前民主党国会女议员希尔达·索利斯（Hilda Solis）成为第一位担任巴拉克·奥巴马（Barack Obama）劳工部长内阁职位的拉丁裔女性，她感谢韦尔塔的指导。 “我在圣盖博谷长大，很少看到拉丁裔担任领导职务。多洛雷斯是少数向我展示可能性的女性之一，”她说。 “从州立法机关到国会，以及在巴拉克·奥巴马总统内阁任职期间，多洛雷斯一直是我生活中的一个常客。我们参加示威和集会，与争取权利的工人站在一起，并在当权者移开目光时要求采取行动……多洛雷斯明白出现、见证和拒绝让妇女的痛苦被忽视的重要性。”
多年来，韦尔塔被认为是 UFW 联合创始人塞萨尔·查韦斯 (César Chávez) 的二号人物，她谈到了她如何必须与运动中的性别歧视作斗争，但常常被迫将功劳拱手让给查韦斯。今年早些时候，在《纽约时报》调查揭露查韦斯对妇女和女孩进行性虐待的行为后，韦尔塔透露查韦斯也强奸了她。

summary: The race for the Senate has moved from off-the-radar a year ago to a dramatic, hard-to-predict finish where Democrats stand a chance of retaking the chamber. The contest will come down to just over a dozen races across the country. Lisa Desjardins takes a look
summary_zh: 参议院竞选已经从一年前的冷门变成了戏剧性的、难以预测的结局，民主党有机会重新夺回席位。
body_en: Where key Senate races stand in the final days of campaigning
https://www.pbs.org/newshour/show/where-key-senate-races-stand-in-the-final-days-of-campaigning

The race for the Senate has moved from off-the-radar a year ago to a dramatic, hard-to-predict finish where Democrats stand a chance of retaking the chamber. The contest will come down to just over a dozen races across the country. Lisa Desjardins takes a look at the map and what might happen.
Notice: Transcripts are machine and human generated and lightly edited for accuracy. They may contain errors.
The fight for control of the U.S. Senate is coming down to a hard-to-predict finish, where Democrats see a possible path to reclaiming the chamber in a year where that seemed like a long shot.
Our Lisa Desjardins joins us now from the super screen to break down the map, the key contests, and what it will take for either party to win.
All right, Lisa, so where does the race for the U.S. Senate stand?
It is unpredictable and it is also incredibly dramatic. Let's jump right in with Cook Political Report's view of things to help us out.

First of all, Democrats, right now, they are defending four vulnerable competitive seats. However, for Cook, three of these, you see them in the dark blue, they don't think are likely to go to Republicans. There is, however, a toss-up seat for Democrats, Michigan. That's number one on their watch list.

How about Republicans? Look at this. Their job is much harder. You can see they're defending far more places, and far more of them are that light color. That means that they are toss-ups or a state that is about to lean potentially for Democrats. Now, in order to take over the Senate, the magic number, I want everyone to remember this, is four. Democrats need a net gain of four seats here.

To do that, you can read the map as well as I,they have got to win in some of these deep red states, but they are competing there. I want to give everyone a sense of how extraordinary this is by looking at the 2024 presidential results of some of these states where Democrats are competing this year.

Ohio, where there's a toss-up race, look at that. Trump won by 11 points. Let's go not far away over to Iowa, also a state that is in competition this year. Trump won that state by 13 points. And go just down the way to Kansas. Look at that. Trump won Kansas by 16 points just two years ago, but, right now, Senate Democrats think they might be able to pick this or other deep red states up to turn over the Senate entirely.
So Democrats, as you say, need to pick up four seats. What's the path to do that or the Republican path to block it?
All right. This is your cheat sheet for election night. Remember this. Again, four seats is the magic number. Let's talk about where each party may have some likely or potential pickups.

First, where can Democrats pick something up? North Carolina. Both parties will tell you that they do think this is likely to go from red to blue this year. Now, how about likely pickups for Republicans, per The Cook Political Report? There are none right now. There are some potential hopes that Republicans have, but right now there are none that are forecast to go their way.

So this leaves the ball game right here, everyone, in the toss-ups. Look at these seats. These seats are the ones likely to determine the fate of the U.S. Senate. Now, how do you figure this out on election night? Again, it does come back to that magic number. Democrats need to pick up four. So it's actually a little bit simple.

Let's imagine North Carolina goes, as it's expected to, for Democrats. That's one. Now it comes down to Michigan. If Democrats keep it, that means they need to pick up three seats among these swing states. If Democrats lose Michigan, they have got to pick up four. And that's what it comes down to.
And how does that compare to the map two years ago?
Right. This is far more seats. In fact, we have 14 competitive seats right now versus nine two years ago, so a lot more.
Lisa Desjardins, I don't know how you do it, but you always do. Thanks so much.
body_zh: 竞选最后几天参议院关键竞选的情况
参议院的竞选已经从一年前的冷门变成了戏剧性的、难以预测的结局，民主党有机会重新夺回众议院。比赛将在全国范围内进行十几场比赛。丽莎·德贾丁斯 (Lisa Desjardins) 看了一下地图，想知道可能会发生什么。
注意：文字记录由机器和人工生成，并经过轻微编辑以确保准确性。它们可能包含错误。
美国参议院控制权之争正面临难以预测的结局，民主党人看到了一条可能的途径，可以在一年内夺回参议院，而这看起来希望渺茫。
我们的丽莎·德贾丁 (Lisa Desjardins) 现在从超级屏幕加入我们，详细介绍地图、关键比赛以及任何一方获胜所需的条件。
好吧，丽莎，那么美国参议院的竞选情况如何呢？
这是不可预测的，也是令人难以置信的戏剧性。让我们直接进入库克政治报告的观点来帮助我们解决问题。
首先，民主党目前正在捍卫四个脆弱的竞争席位。然而，对于库克来说，其中三个，你看到他们是深蓝色的，他们认为不太可能落入共和党手中。然而，密歇根州的民主党却有一个席位悬而未决。这是他们观察名单上的第一名。
那么共和党人呢？看看这个。他们的工作要困难得多。你可以看到他们正在防守更多的地方，而且其中更多的是浅色的。这意味着他们是一个难以抉择的州，或者是一个可能倾向于民主党的州。现在，为了接管参议院，我希望每个人都记住这一神奇数字，那就是四。民主党需要在这里净增加四个席位。
要做到这一点，你可以和我一样阅读地图，他们必须在其中一些深红色州获胜，但他们在那里竞争。我想通过看看民主党今年竞选的一些州的 2024 年总统选举结果，让每个人都感受到这是多么的非凡。
俄亥俄州，那里有一场势均力敌的比赛，看看那个。特朗普以11个百分点获胜。让我们去不远的爱荷华州，也是今年的竞争州。特朗普以 13 个百分点的优势赢得了该州。然后沿着路往堪萨斯走去。看看那个。就在两年前，特朗普以 16 个百分点的优势赢得了堪萨斯州，但现在，参议院民主党人认为他们可能能够选择这个州或其他深红色州来完全交出参议院的席位。
因此，正如你所说，民主党需要获得四个席位。做到这一点的途径是什么，或者共和党阻止它的途径是什么？
好的。这是你的选举之夜备忘单。记住这一点。同样，四个座位是一个神奇的数字。让我们来谈谈各方可能在哪些方面有可能或潜在的选择。
首先，民主党可以从哪里得到一些东西？北卡罗来纳州。双方都会告诉你，他们确实认为今年的情况可能会由红转蓝。现在，根据库克政治报告，共和党人可能会回升怎么样？现在还没有。共和党人有一些潜在的希望，但目前预计没有一个会如愿。
所以，这让大家都陷入了犹豫不决的局面。看看这些座位。这些席位可能决定美国参议院的命运。现在，你如何在选举之夜弄清楚这一点？再次，它确实回到了那个神奇的数字。民主党需要选出四个。所以它实际上有点简单。
让我们想象一下，北卡罗来纳州如预期的那样支持民主党。这是一个。现在归结为密歇根州。如果民主党保留这一席位，这意味着他们需要在这些摇摆州中获得三个席位。如果民主党失去密歇根州，他们就必须拿下四个。归根结底就是这样。
与两年前的地图相比如何？
正确的。这是更多的座位。事实上，我们现在有 14 个竞争席位，而两年前有 9 个，所以多了很多。
Lisa Desjardins，我不知道你是怎么做到的，但你总是这么做。非常感谢。

title_en: Trump administration will allow pharmacies to make popular peptides
title_zh: 特朗普政府将允许药店生产受欢迎的肽
summary: The Department of Health and Human Services will let small compounding pharmacies make six peptides that haven't been approved by the Food and Drug Administration. It may not be enough to meet demand.
summary_zh: 卫生与公众服务部将允许小型复合药房生产六种未经食品药品广告批准的肽
body_en: Trump administration will allow pharmacies to make popular peptides

Secretary of Health and Human Services Robert F. Kennedy Jr. has supported broader access to peptides. A new policy will make it easier for small compounding pharmacies to make them. Heather Diehl/Getty Images hide caption

Unproven but popular peptides touted for wellness have been available on the gray market, despite an official ban. Now, the Department of Health and Human Services is looking to bring them out of the shadows.
HHS said in a new policy that it will exercise enforcement discretion for a half dozen peptides, essentially looking the other way when they're made by small compounding pharmacies.
Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. has been a vocal supporter of peptides , saying he has used some of them himself.

Peptides are strings of amino acids, shorter than proteins, that can exert powerful effects in the body. Some occur naturally and others are synthetic variations. Wellness influencers and some clinicians have promoted unproven peptides for a wide range of uses, though the evidence for their safety and effectiveness is sparse.

So even though these peptides have not been through the Food and Drug Administration's rigorous drug review and approval process, they could become easier to get. But the policy's focus on smaller producers may mean that pharmacists will have a tough time meeting demand.

In July, a panel of advisers to the FDA voted in favor of expanded access to six peptides through compounding pharmacies. However, at the same meeting the FDA's own scientists recommended against unwinding the existing restrictions on them.
The new policy says compounding is a safer alternative to illicit "research-use-only" peptides that are available online. They're often sourced from sketchy suppliers overseas.
The peptides, and some of their unproven uses, are

Joshua Fritzler, the president of Olympia and Wesley Pharmaceuticals in central Florida, says people have been asking about these peptides for years. But because they were illegal to compound, his company didn't make them.

The new policy doesn't change their legal status, but it does create a path for small compounders, called 503A compounding pharmacies. It doesn't apply to the larger ones, called 503Bs, that are outsourcing facilities producing higher volumes of medicines.
So at Fritzler's company, only its smaller compounding facility will be able to make the peptides – and only in small quantities, he says.

"We won't be able to meet demand," he says, explaining that Olympia will likely only compound one of the six peptides and needs to get its facility ready first. "I don't think all the [503]As in the country could meet the demand."

The Alliance for Pharmacy Compounding's CEO Scott Brunner wrote in a statement that his group is pleased with the administration's decision to allow the peptides to be compounded because it offers a "more accountable alternative" for patients seeking gray market peptides.
FDA panel supports broadening access to peptides popular on the gray market
"It also brings patients into a system where pharmacy standards, regulatory oversight, and serious adverse event reporting apply," he says.

Brunner warned, however, that it may take some time for compounding pharmacies to begin dispensing these products to patients. That's because ingredient suppliers need to make sure their active ingredients meet the policy's requirements — and pharmacies need to verify that, too.

Several consumer advocacy groups say the policy puts patients at risk, however. The nonprofit Public Citizen noted that Kennedy seems to have acted unilaterally rather than through the typical rulemaking process.

"By allowing unproven and potentially unsafe peptides to be manufactured, marketed and prescribed without concern about potential federal enforcement actions, Kennedy has undermined the FDA and threatened public health," Dr. Robert Steinbrook, Health Research Group Director at Public Citizen wrote in a statement. "All peptide substances should go through the standard FDA approval process for new drugs. The HHS Secretary should support, not sabotage, needed FDA enforcement actions to protect consumers."
body_zh: 特朗普政府将允许药店生产受欢迎的肽
卫生与公众服务部部长小罗伯特·F·肯尼迪支持更广泛地获取肽。新政策将使小型复方药房更容易生产它们。希瑟迪尔/盖蒂图片社隐藏标题栏
尽管有官方禁令，但未经证实但流行的以健康为目的的肽已在灰色市场上出售。现在，卫生与公众服务部正在努力让他们走出阴影。
美国卫生与公众服务部在一项新政策中表示，它将对六种肽行使执法自由裁量权，本质上是对小型复合药房生产的肽视而不见。
卫生部长小罗伯特·F·肯尼迪一直是肽的大力支持者，称他自己也使用过其中一些肽。
肽是一串氨基酸，比蛋白质短，可以在体内发挥强大的作用。有些是自然发生的，有些是人工合成的。健康影响者和一些临床医生已经推广了未经证实的肽的广泛用途，尽管其安全性和有效性的证据很少。
因此，即使这些肽尚未通过美国食品和药物管理局严格的药物审查和批准程序，它们也可能变得更容易获得。但该政策对小型生产商的关注可能意味着药剂师将很难满足需求。
7 月，FDA 的一个顾问小组投票赞成通过复合药房扩大对六种肽的获取。然而，在同一次会议上，FDA 自己的科学家建议不要放松对它们的现有限制。
新政策称，复合是比在线提供的非法“仅供研究使用”肽更安全的替代品。它们通常是从海外的粗略供应商那里采购的。
这些肽及其一些未经证实的用途是
佛罗里达州中部奥林匹亚和韦斯利制药公司总裁约书亚·弗里茨勒 (Joshua Fritzler) 表示，多年来人们一直在询问这些肽。但由于它们的合成是非法的，他的公司没有生产它们。
新政策并没有改变它们的法律地位，但确实为小型配药商创造了一条道路，称为503A配药房。它不适用于称为 503B 的较大型工厂，这些工厂是生产大量药品的外包设施。
因此，在弗里茨勒的公司，只有较小的复合设施才能生产肽，而且产量很小，他说。
“我们将无法满足需求，”他说，并解释说奥林匹亚可能只会合成六种肽中的一种，并且需要首先准备好其设施。 “我认为国内所有的[503]A 都无法满足需求。”
药房复合联盟的首席执行官斯科特·布伦纳在一份声明中写道，他的团队对政府允许复合肽的决定感到高兴，因为这为寻求灰色市场肽的患者提供了“更负责任的替代方案”。
FDA 小组支持扩大灰色市场上流行的肽的获取范围
“它还将患者带入一个适用药房标准、监管监督和严重不良事件报告的系统，”他说。
然而，布伦纳警告说，复合药房可能需要一些时间才能开始向患者配发这些产品。这是因为成分供应商需要确保他们的活性成分符合政策的要求——药店也需要验证这一点。
然而，一些消费者权益团体表示，该政策将患者置于危险之中。非营利组织“公共公民”指出，肯尼迪似乎是单方面采取行动，而不是通过典型的规则制定程序。
Public Citizen 健康研究小组主任 Robert Steinbrook 博士在一份声明中写道：“肯尼迪允许未经证实和可能不安全的肽在不担心潜在的联邦执法行动的情况下生产、销售和开处方，这损害了 FDA 的利益并威胁到公众健康。” “所有肽物质都应经过 FDA 新药的标准审批流程。美国卫生与公众服务部部长应该支持而不是破坏 FDA 保护消费者所需的执法行动。”
