body_en: Non-profit group leaks data of more than 40,000 homeland security workers | Trump administration
Non-profit group leaks data of more than 40,000 homeland security workers
Information released by Distributed Denial of Secrets is the third such government data disclosure in the last month

The leak website Distributed Denial of Secrets said on Wednesday it has released data on more than 40,000 Department ⁠of Homeland Security (DHS) employees, including details about officials working in sensitive fields such as surveillance and human intelligence.
DHS did not immediately return a message seeking comment.

The disclosure – which the ⁠non-profit data transparency group says draws ⁠on information obtained ​by an entity calling itself “Department of Peace” – is the third government data leak to have made headlines in the past month.

In September, the hacking group ShinyHunters claimed ⁠the theft of a massive trove of data from the Federal Bureau of Investigation, including sensitive job details and medical information from thousands of bureau employees. Last week, the defense department was hit with ⁠a class action lawsuit following a breach that exposed data on millions of current and former military personnel.

The DHS data includes ​names, phone numbers and email addresses of employees from Immigration ‌and Customs Enforcement, Customs and Border ‌Protection, Homeland Security Investigations, the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency and other DHS component agencies.

Also included in the data were job ‌titles and email groups, which, among other details, showed which agents were assigned to special operations, surveillance jobs, computer forensics and undercover work.

In a statement, Emma Best, a Distributed Denial of Secrets co-founder, said the hacktivist known as “maia arson crimew” developed a search tool for the data that would allow the public to browse it. Best said the tool would “replace anonymity with accountability” and empower journalists, guide public records requests and boost congressional oversight.

The Department of Peace did not immediately respond ‌to a request for comment, but in a statement included with the data, it said that DHS employees “have our information, so it’s only fair that we have theirs” and that it hoped the data “can ​be used to limit further harm by the DHS and supports all efforts in that direction”.
The Department of Peace in March claimed responsibility for hacking DHS and posting documents related to contracts with outside vendors.

Best’s statement said Department of Peace harvested the data from the Okta sign-on service used by DHS. Reuters could not immediately corroborate the claim. Okta said in response to a Reuters query: “Okta is ⁠secure, and we have no evidence our data or systems were compromised.”

Reuters could not immediately ​verify the authenticity of the entire data ​trove but it was able to match ​personal information of about six DHS employees named in the leak to credit bureau records and breach data ​carried by the dark ‌web intelligence platform District 4 ​Labs. In other cases, ​Reuters called three DHS employees directly and was able to confirm their phone numbers and other details. One said it was the first they had heard of a breach.

In several cases, the data tracked information available on DHS employees’ LinkedIn profiles. But in others, the data revealed nonpublic data about internal DHS organization charts or previously undisclosed programs or operations.
body_zh: 非营利组织泄露超过 40,000 名国土安全人员的数据特朗普政府
非营利组织泄露 40,000 多名国土安全人员的数据
Distributed Denial of Secrets 发布的信息是上个月第三次此类政府数据泄露
泄密网站 Distributed Denial of Secrets 周三表示，已公布了超过 40,000 名国土安全部 (DHS) 员工的数据，其中包括在监视和人类情报等敏感领域工作的官员的详细信息。
国土安全部没有立即回复寻求置评的消息。
非营利数据透明组织表示，此次披露是根据一个自称“和平部”的实体获得的信息，这是过去一个月内第三次成为头条新闻的政府数据泄露事件。
9 月，黑客组织 ShinyHunters 声称联邦调查局的大量数据被盗，其中包括该局数千名员工的敏感工作详细信息和医疗信息。上周，由于泄露了数百万现任和前任军事人员的数据，国防部遭到集体诉讼。
国土安全部数据包括来自移民和海关执法局、海关和边境保护局、国土安全调查局、网络安全和基础设施安全局以及其他国土安全部组成机构的员工的姓名、电话号码和电子邮件地址。
数据中还包括职务和电子邮件组，其中除其他详细信息外，还显示哪些特工被分配到特殊行动、监视工作、计算机取证和卧底工作。
Distributed Denial of Secrets 联合创始人艾玛·贝斯特 (Emma Best) 在一份声明中表示，这位被称为“maia arsoncrimew”的黑客活动分子开发了一种数据搜索工具，允许公众浏览数据。贝斯特表示，该工具将“用问责制取代匿名”，并赋予记者权力、指导公共记录请求并加强国会监督。
和平部没有立即回应置评请求，但在数据中包含的一份声明中表示，国土安全部员工“拥有我们的信息，因此我们拥有他们的信息是公平的”，并希望这些数据“可用于限制国土安全部的进一步伤害，并支持朝这个方向的所有努力”。
和平部三月份声称对黑客入侵国土安全部并发布与外部供应商合同相关的文件负责。
贝斯特的声明称，和平部从国土安全部使用的 Okta 登录服务中收集了数据。路透社无法立即证实这一说法。 Okta 在回应路透社的询问时表示：“Okta 是安全的，我们没有证据表明我们的数据或系统受到了损害。”
路透社无法立即验证整个数据库的真实性，但它能够将泄密事件中提到的约六名国土安全部员工的个人信息与暗网情报平台 District 4 Labs 携带的信用局记录和泄露数据进行匹配。在其他情况下，路透社直接致电三名国土安全部员工，并确认了他们的电话号码和其他详细信息。有人表示，这是他们第一次听说违规行为。
在一些情况下，数据跟踪了国土安全部员工 LinkedIn 个人资料上的信息。但在其他情况下，这些数据揭示了有关国土安全部内部组织结构图或之前未公开的计划或运营的非公开数据。

body_en: Seawater surges into low-lying communities from San Diego to San Francisco Bay Area, submerging streets, homes and businesses

Historic high tides have caused chaos up and down the California coast this week, as parts of the state were inundated by record-breaking water levels. Seawater surged into low-lying communities from San Diego to the San Francisco Bay Area, submerging streets, flooding homes and businesses, and jamming important transportation corridors and train routes.

Kayakers and paddle boarders could be seen gliding through typically busy thoroughfares in Marin county, north of San Francisco, on Monday and Tuesday. Several drivers had to be rescued from floating cars in the area, while cyclists who had attempted to cross the temporary lagoon that had formed quickly found themselves waist-deep. Further south, in cities such as Newport Beach, water pounded the emergency infrastructure set up to keep out the swelling sea, which seeped through berms, seawalls and sandbag blockades along the shoreline.
body_zh: 海水涌入从圣地亚哥到旧金山湾区的低洼社区，淹没街道、房屋和企业
本周，历史性的涨潮在加州海岸造成了混乱，该州部分地区被破纪录的水位淹没。海水涌入从圣地亚哥到旧金山湾区的低洼社区，淹没街道、淹没房屋和企业，并堵塞重要的交通走廊和火车路线。
周一和周二，可以看到皮划艇和桨板冲浪者在旧金山北部马林县通常繁忙的街道上滑行。几名司机必须从该地区漂浮的汽车中获救，而试图穿越很快形成的临时泻湖的骑自行车者却发现自己深及齐腰。再往南，在纽波特海滩等城市，水冲击了为抵御汹涌的海水而设立的应急基础设施，海水渗入了海岸线的护堤、海堤和沙袋封锁区。

title_en: Midwest Dems face their do or die moment to win back Trump districts before 2028
title_zh: 中西部民主党面临着在 2028 年之前赢回特朗普选区的生死攸关时刻
summary: Voters from western Wisconsin over to southern Minnesota and down to eastern Iowa are hurting. The question is whether they blame the president’s policies enough to elect Democrats.
summary_zh: 从威斯康星州西部到明尼苏达州南部，再到爱荷华州东部，选民都受到了伤害。问题是他们是否归咎于总统的政策
body_en: EAU CLAIRE, Wisconsin — In this rural-heavy stretch of the upper Midwest, Democrats are trying to claw back districts where their party brand is still deeply toxic.

It won’t be easy, even in a midterm environment that heavily favors their party. Local Democratic organizers in western Wisconsin, where Rebecca Cooke is trying to oust GOP Rep. Derrick Van Orden, know that elections here are decided by the slimmest of margins. They have no room for error.
“Everything's on a razor's edge,” Clara Serrano, who volunteers for the local Democratic Party, said as she drove along farms and cornfields outside Eau Claire.

But a decade after President Donald Trump’s populism and culture wars swung the formerly Democratic-leaning region right, many voters from western Wisconsin over to southern Minnesota and down to eastern Iowa are hurting — and blame the president’s policies. Family farms are reeling from his tariffs. Diesel is over $6 a gallon. The cost of fertilizer has shot up more than 30 percent since the war in Iran began earlier this year.

“[Rural voters are] mad when we get to the door — and not at us,” said William Garcia, co-chair of the La Crosse County Democratic Party who has been out canvassing. “They're mad about gas prices. They're mad about fertilizer. They're mad about the tariffs. And so all we do as Democrats is say, ‘Hey, we agree. We rejected all of these things. We've been fighting all of these things.’ So it’s much more receptive now than really it's ever been.”

Local Democrats have pulled out all the stops to propel Cooke in Wisconsin’s 3rd District, knocking endless doors in redder areas . There have been national reinforcements as well: Populist Sen. Bernie Sanders (I-Vt.) endorsed Cooke during the primary and hit the campaign trail with her this week in Eau Claire. The national party is trying to make generational gains in Minnesota’s 1st District — where they’re hoping to pull off a major upset to unseat GOP Rep. Brad Finstad in a Trump +12 district — and in deep-red Iowa, where Democrats are targeting three GOP House seats, a Senate seat and the governorship.

Democrats for years have faltered with rural voters in these districts. Now, with polling showing Democrats gaining ground in redder territory and an electorate that’s souring on the GOP, Democrats hope they can finally make up ground this November — and lay a solid foundation for the 2028 presidential election.
If that doesn’t happen, it’s an ominous sign for the party.

“If we can’t win these seats now in this environment, it seems like we’re in for a world of hurt in 2028,” said one House Democrat, who, like others in this article, was granted anonymity to speak candidly.

Wisconsin Democrats have worked nearly-year round to build up a ground game. A major new initiative from the state party has helped to boost organizing, especially in rural counties and other places they’ve struggled.
“We haven't really stopped organizing since 2024,” said Pete Huff, co-chair of the nearby Dunn County Democratic party, where Trump won by 16 points.

Cooke, who grew up on a farm in the area, has tried to create a more durable brand of politics in the district by largely trying to distance herself from the national Democratic party as she seeks to win over a broader base of voters. It helped in 2024: She overperformed Kamala Harris by 9,000 votes across the district, even though she narrowly lost to Van Orden.

“I think that the party doesn't know how to speak the language of rural America, and I feel like I uniquely do,” Cooke said in an interview. She regularly canvasses in rural communities and has tried to tie Van Orden to increasingly unpopular data center developments, after local projects sparked backlash. On Sunday, before the campus rally, Cooke attended a meeting for residents worried about a new high-voltage transmission line that would cut through farmland.

This cycle, she’s especially leaned into the rare House endorsement from Sanders, who’s built his own populist and anti-establishment brand. At a Sunday rally on the University of Wisconsin-Eau Claire campus, she introduced the Vermont senator by saying: “Everyone forgets he’s an independent.”
Potential 2028 Democratic presidential contenders see the stakes of winning back rural-heavy districts as well.
Former Transportation Secretary Pete Buttigieg is traveling to Minnesota’s 1st District on Sunday to rally voters for Democrat Jake Johnson in Rochester.

It’s one of the many once-safe red seats that Republicans and Trump’s political operation are scrambling to shore up in these final days, with Johnson and Finstad running in what’s become a highly competitive race. Minnesota’s Democratic Gov. Tim Walz, then a high school teacher, won a House seat here in a 2006 wave election amid voter anger at the Iraq war and their GOP incumbent. Also that year, a local prosecutor named Amy Klobuchar swept to a big Senate win, part of a Democratic surge across the region.
Democrats are hopeful that history is repeating, with high costs and a president unpopular because of a Middle East incursion hurting the GOP in the region and nationally.
“The price of diesel is devastating,” said Ted Winter, who farms with his son near Fulda.

“We've patterned a lot of our campaign after Amy Klobuchar, who famously shows up in every single county every single year,” Johnson, a math teacher, said in an interview. “And so I just said, ‘hey guys, let's host a town hall in every county.’”
body_zh: 威斯康星州欧克莱尔——在中西部北部这个农村人口较多的地区，民主党人正试图夺回其政党品牌仍然具有严重毒性的地区。
即使在非常有利于他们的政党的中期环境中，这也不容易。威斯康星州西部的当地民主党组织者丽贝卡·库克(Rebecca Cooke)正试图推翻共和党众议员德里克·范·奥登(Derrick Van Orden)，他们知道这里的选举是由微弱的优势决定的。他们没有犯错的余地。
“一切都在刀刃上，”当地民主党的志愿者克拉拉·塞拉诺(Clara Serrano)一边开车沿着欧克莱尔郊外的农场和玉米地行驶，一边说道。
但在唐纳德·特朗普总统的民粹主义和文化战争使这个曾经倾向民主党的地区右倾十年后，从威斯康星州西部到明尼苏达州南部，再到爱荷华州东部的许多选民都受到了伤害，并指责总统的政策。家庭农场正受到他的关税的影响。柴油每加仑超过 6 美元。自今年早些时候伊朗战争爆发以来，化肥成本已飙升超过 30%。
“当我们走到门口时，[农村选民]很生气，而不是对我们，”一直在拉克罗斯县民主党拉票拉票的联合主席威廉·加西亚说。 “他们对天然气价格感到愤怒。他们对化肥感到愤怒。他们对关税感到愤怒。所以我们作为民主党人所做的就是说，‘嘿，我们同意。我们拒绝了所有这些事情。我们一直在与所有这些事情作斗争。’所以现在比以往任何时候都更容易接受。”
当地民主党人已竭尽全力推动库克在威斯康星州第三选区的发展，在红色地区不断敲门。全国范围内也有增援：民粹主义参议员伯尼·桑德斯（佛蒙特州）在初选期间支持库克，并于本周在欧克莱尔与她一起参加竞选活动。国家党正试图在明尼苏达州第一选区（他们希望在特朗普+12选区击败共和党众议员布拉德·芬斯塔德）和深红色爱荷华州取得代际收益，民主党的目标是共和党众议院的三个席位、参议院席位和州长职位。
多年来，民主党在这些地区的农村选民中一直举步维艰。现在，民意调查显示民主党在较红的地区取得进展，而选民对共和党的态度也越来越差，民主党希望他们最终能在今年 11 月收复失地，为 2028 年总统选举奠定坚实的基础。
如果这种情况没有发生，这对党来说是一个不祥的征兆。
一位众议院民主党议员表示：“如果我们现在无法在这种环境下赢得这些席位，那么 2028 年我们似乎将面临一个痛苦的世界。”他和本文中的其他人一样，被允许匿名坦率地发言。
威斯康星州民主党人几乎全年都在努力建立基础游戏。该州的一项重大新举措有助于促进组织，特别是在农村县和其他他们陷入困境的地方。
“自 2024 年以来，我们一直没有真正停止组织活动，”附近邓恩县民主党的联合主席皮特·赫夫 (Pete Huff) 说，特朗普在该党以 16 个百分点的优势获胜。
库克在该地区的一个农场长大，在寻求赢得更广泛的选民基础时，她试图在该地区创建一个更持久的政治品牌，主要是试图与全国民主党保持距离。这在 2024 年起了作用：尽管她以微弱优势输给了范奥登，但她在整个选区以 9,000 票的优势击败了卡玛拉·哈里斯 (Kamala Harris)。
“我认为该党不知道如何说美国农村的语言，而我觉得我是独一无二的，”库克在接受采访时说。她定期在农村社区进行游说，并在当地项目引发强烈反对后，试图将范奥登与日益不受欢迎的数据中心开发项目联系起来。周日，在校园集会之前，库克参加了一场居民会议，担心一条新的高压输电线路会穿过农田。
这一周期，她特别倾向于桑德斯罕见的众议院支持，桑德斯建立了自己的民粹主义和反建制品牌。在威斯康星大学欧克莱尔校区举行的周日集会上，她介绍这位佛蒙特州参议员时说：“每个人都忘记了他是独立人士。”
2028 年民主党总统候选人也看到了赢回农村地区的利害关系。
前交通部长皮特·布蒂吉格将于周日前往明尼苏达州第一选区，在罗切斯特为民主党人杰克·约翰逊集会选民。

这是共和党和特朗普的政治运作在最后几天争先恐后地巩固的众多曾经安全的红色席位之一，约翰逊和芬斯塔德的竞选竞争已经变得非常激烈。时任高中教师的明尼苏达州民主党州长蒂姆·沃尔兹 (Tim Walz) 在 2006 年的一次选举中赢得了众议院席位，当时选民对伊拉克战争和共和党现任议员感到愤怒。同年，当地检察官艾米·克洛布彻 (Amy Klobuchar) 在参议院大获全胜，这是该地区民主党崛起的一部分。
民主党人希望历史重演，代价高昂，而且由于中东入侵损害了该地区和全国范围内的共和党，总统也不得人心。
“柴油价格是毁灭性的，”与儿子在富尔达附近务农的特德·温特 (Ted Winter) 说。
“我们的很多活动都模仿了艾米·克洛布彻（Amy Klobuchar），众所周知，她每年都会出现在每个县，”数学老师约翰逊在接受采访时说。 “所以我只是说，‘嘿伙计们，让我们在每个县举办一次市政厅吧。’”

summary: Minnesota has become a flashpoint in the political dispute between President Trump and Democrats. Clashes over immigration and recent accusations of fraud are spilling into the U.S. Senate race.

body_en: Minnesota becomes battleground as political clashes shape Senate race : NPR

Minnesota becomes battleground as political clashes shape Senate race Minnesota has become a flashpoint in the political dispute between President Trump and Democrats. Clashes over immigration and recent accusations of fraud are spilling into the U.S. Senate race.
Minnesota becomes battleground as political clashes shape Senate race
Minnesota has become a flashpoint in the political dispute between President Trump and Democrats. Clashes over immigration and recent accusations of fraud are spilling into the U.S. Senate race.

The U.S. Senate race in Minnesota is especially competitive. It's an open seat. A Democrat is retiring. So while Democrats expect to gain Senate seats elsewhere in the country, Republicans hope to gain a seat in Minnesota. Democratic voters this year are motivated by immigration after a Trump administration crackdown led to protests and deaths in Minnesota. President Trump and the Republican Party are also focused on immigrants - in particular, Somali Americans and Representative Ilhan Omar. Minnesota Public Radio's Clay Masters reports.
CLAY MASTERS, BYLINE: Lieutenant Governor Peggy Flanagan sits in an elementary school library for a recent roundtable to talk about the local effects of President Trump's immigration enforcement.
PEGGY FLANAGAN: If folks just want to introduce yourself, and then just...

MASTERS: Flanagan is the Democratic candidate for the open U.S. Senate race here. She says what happened in her state shows how the Trump administration wields its power, and it's what this midterm election is about.

FLANAGAN: This is, I think, the model of what the most corrupt, cruel administration in our nation's history - what they can get away with when, you know, this goes unchecked. So this is a choice in this race.

MASTERS: Flanagan faces Republican Michele Tafoya, who is running as a moderate and has the endorsement of President Trump. At a debate earlier this month hosted by Minnesota Public Radio, Tafoya was asked to comment on how Operation Metro Surge was handled. She brings up the two Americans who were killed by federal agents that sparked nationwide protests.

MICHELE TAFOYA: Those two things go hand in hand. The loss of Renee Good and Alex Pretti is devastating. I did not like the way that ICE rollout was handled by Kristi Noem, and she was appropriately fired. We also had a massive failure in leadership from Governor Tim Walz and Lieutenant Governor Peggy Flanagan.

MASTERS: The Trump administration used both alleged and proven fraud in state social service programs as part of its reason for targeting Minnesota. And now voters are being flooded with ads tying hundreds of millions of dollars in alleged fraud to the state's Democratic leaders, including Minnesota's governor, Tim Walz, the party's former vice presidential candidate. That speaks to conservative voter Dale Johnson. He's a retired snowplow driver who says he brings the issue up at his union meetings, only to be met with pushback.

DALE JOHNSON: And one of the fellow members said, oh, that was mostly federal money. As if, well, don't worry about it. It's federal money that they're blowing. That shows you that people aren't really using their head.

MASTERS: In the final weeks before election day, President Trump continues to focus on Minnesota. Here he is in the Oval Office just last week, talking about a new program to report suspected fraud. And he used the opportunity to attack Minnesota and its Somali American community.

PRESIDENT DONALD TRUMP: I remember Minnesota in the old days. What a beautiful - with lakes all over the place. They have more lakes than any place I've ever seen. So beautiful. They've - they're destroying it. Probably - maybe they've destroyed it.

MASTERS: In that same appearance, Trump brought up the federal investigation into allegations of immigration fraud regarding Representative Ilhan Omar. The Minnesota congresswoman says it's an intimidation attempt ahead of the midterms. UC Berkeley law professor Ian Lopez studies the exploitation of race as a basis for mobilizing political support.

IAN LOPEZ: These allegations of fraud against people of color in Minnesota as a way to whip up racial resentment and to try and transmute that into political energy - those are classic techniques of dogmas of politics.

MASTERS: But immigration and fraud are among the issues Democrats and the Trump administration have been fighting over all year long, and the race for Minnesota's open U.S. Senate seat is closer than expected in a state that historically tilts blue.
For NPR News, I'm Clay Masters in Minneapolis.

政治冲突影响参议院竞选，明尼苏达州成为战场
明尼苏达州已成为特朗普总统与民主党之间政治争端的热点。围绕移民的冲突和最近的欺诈指控正在蔓延到美国参议院竞选中。
明尼苏达州的美国参议员竞选尤其激烈。这是一个开放的座位。一位民主党人即将退休。因此，虽然民主党希望在该国其他地方获得参议院席位，但共和党希望在明尼苏达州获得席位。在特朗普政府的镇压导致明尼苏达州发生抗议和死亡之后，今年的民主党选民受到了移民的推动。特朗普总统和共和党也关注移民问题，特别是索马里裔美国人和众议员伊尔汗·奥马尔。明尼苏达州公共广播电台的克莱大师报道。
克莱马斯特斯连线：副州长佩吉·弗拉纳根 (Peggy Flanagan) 坐在一家小学图书馆，参加最近举行的圆桌会议，讨论特朗普总统移民执法对当地的影响。
PEGGY FLANAGAN：如果人们只是想自我介绍，然后......
大师：弗拉纳根是这里公开的美国参议院竞选的民主党候选人。她说，她所在州发生的事情表明了特朗普政府如何运用权力，这也是这次中期选举的意义所在。
弗拉纳根：我认为，这就是我们国家历史上最腐败、最残酷的政府的典范——当你知道，这种情况不受控制时，他们可以逍遥法外。所以这是本次比赛的一个选择。
大师赛：弗拉纳根将对阵共和党人米歇尔·塔福亚，后者以温和派身份参选，并得到了特朗普总统的支持。在本月早些时候由明尼苏达州公共广播电台主办的一场辩论中，塔福亚被要求就地铁激增行动的处理方式发表评论。她提到了两名被联邦特工杀害的美国人，这引发了全国范围的抗议活动。
米歇尔·塔福亚：这两件事是相辅相成的。蕾妮·古德 (Renee Good) 和亚历克斯·普雷蒂 (Alex Pretti) 的去世是毁灭性的。我不喜欢 Kristi Noem 处理 ICE 部署的方式，因此她被适当地解雇了。州长蒂姆·沃尔兹（Tim Walz）和副州长佩吉·弗拉纳根（Peggy Flanagan）在领导方面也遭遇了巨大失败。
大师们：特朗普政府利用州社会服务计划中涉嫌和已证实的欺诈行为作为针对明尼苏达州的部分原因。现在，选民们充斥着广告，这些广告涉嫌与该州的民主党领导人涉嫌欺诈，其中包括明尼苏达州州长、该党前副总统候选人蒂姆·沃尔兹(Tim Walz)。这是保守派选民戴尔·约翰逊所说的。他是一名退休的扫雪机司机，他说他在工会会议上提出了这个问题，但遭到了抵制。
戴尔·约翰逊：一位成员说，哦，那大部分是联邦资金。好像，好吧，不用担心。他们花的是联邦钱。这表明人们并没有真正使用他们的头脑。
大师们：在选举日前的最后几周，特朗普总统继续关注明尼苏达州。上周，他在椭圆形办公室谈论一项举报涉嫌欺诈的新计划。他还利用这个机会攻击明尼苏达州及其索马里裔美国人社区。
唐纳德·特朗普总统：我记得过去的明尼苏达州。多么美丽——到处都是湖泊。他们的湖泊比我见过的任何地方都多。如此美丽。他们已经——他们正在摧毁它。可能——也许他们已经毁掉了它。
马斯特斯：在同一次露面中，特朗普提出了联邦对众议员伊尔汗·奥马尔移民欺诈指控的调查。明尼苏达州女议员表示，这是中期选举前的一次恐吓行为。加州大学伯克利分校法学教授伊恩·洛佩兹研究利用种族剥削作为动员政治支持的基础。
伊恩·洛佩兹：这些针对明尼苏达州有色人种的欺诈指控是煽动种族怨恨并试图将其转化为政治能量的一种方式 - 这些是政治教条的经典技巧。
马斯特斯：但移民和欺诈是民主党和特朗普政府一整年都在争论的问题之一，而明尼苏达州的美国参议院空缺席位的竞争比预期的更加激烈，因为这个州历来都是偏蓝的。
我是 NPR 新闻的明尼阿波利斯克莱大师。

title_zh: 特朗普政府希望取消对超级行星加热气体的监管
summary: The Trump administration wants to undo a Biden-era rule that would reduce methane emissions from the oil and gas industry.
summary_zh: 特朗普政府希望废除拜登时代减少石油和天然气行业甲烷排放的规定。
body_en: Trump administration wants to remove regulations on a super planet-heating gas : NPR

Trump administration wants to remove regulations on a super planet-heating gas The Trump administration wants to undo a Biden-era rule that would reduce methane emissions from the oil and gas industry.
Trump administration wants to remove regulations on a super planet-heating gas
Flares burn off methane and other hydrocarbons at an oil and gas facility in Lenorah, Texas, Oct. 15, 2021. David Goldman/AP hide caption
The Trump administration is proposing to dramatically scale back a Biden-era rule that aimed to cut methane emissions from the oil and gas industry at drilling sites nationwide.

Methane is a major contributor to climate change and is estimated to be 80 times more planet-warming than carbon dioxide in a twenty-year time frame. In 2023, the Biden administration finalized rules that were meant to rein in methane emissions from the oil and gas sector.

President Trump made the announcement while campaigning in Lubbock, Texas, Tuesday, saying his administration's revision, under the Clean Air Act, would save the industry billions in production costs and spur more domestic drilling. The proposal comes as Republicans face a backlash from voters over high gas prices heading into the midterms.

"Behind every barrel of oil and every cubic foot of natural gas produced in the U.S. are millions of workers, businesses, and the heartbeat of this nation's economy. The Biden EPA destructively targeted all this," EPA Administrator Lee Zeldin said in a press release.
The oil and gas industry, which vigorously opposed the 2023 rules, said EPA's proposed rollback will address some of the challenges companies have faced in trying to comply with the regulations.

"We look forward to working with the Trump administration on a more workable approach that supports American energy production, provides greater regulatory certainty and advances continued emissions reductions," Dustin Meyer, vice president at the American Petroleum Institute, a trade organization for the U.S. oil and gas industry, said in a statement.
But environmentalists say this may end up actually costing the industry more.

"Methane is natural gas, or natural gas is methane," says Jon Goldstein, associate vice president at the Environmental Defense Fund. "And so if you're capturing more natural gas, you're not allowing it to leak out, you're not allowing it to be flared, you have more product that you can sell. And so that offsets a lot of the costs."
"That is harmful to our energy security, and it's harmful to taxpayers that ought to be seeing royalty and tax revenue collected off of this gas that's going to waste," Goldstein adds.

One of the regulations the EPA wants to cut is the " Methane Super Emitter Program ." Across the U.S., oil and gas pipelines, refineries, and other energy facilities sometimes have huge leaks of methane. But methane is invisible and difficult, not to mention expensive, to detect. The super emitter program is supposed to take effect in January 2027. It would allow the government to delegate monitoring for big methane leaks to certified third parties, including private and nonprofit methane satellite programs.
New satellite is designed to track methane emitted from the oil and gas industry

"The easiest way to think about it is that if the government is alerted to a big leak, then if it's reported by certified third parties, then they could use that information," says Paasha Mahdavi, a political science professor at UC Santa Barbara who studies the oil industry.
"[The government] needs help from other people to say, 'Hey! You're breaking the law!' so they're able to prosecute," Mahdavi adds.

If that program goes away, Mahdavi says it will be harder for the government to spot large leaks of the planet-heating gas from oil and gas facilities. "And we need that because it's really hard to see this stuff," he says.
The EPA's announcement would also loosen regulations on methane leaks coming from low-volume "marginal" oil wells that are considered "marginally economic," meaning they don't make much money.

"People assume marginal well must equal small emissions," Goldstein says. But he says satellites and new technology find that's not true. "These old sort of end-of-life wells nearing the end of their production life are actually responsible for the lion's share of methane pollution from the [oil and gas] production sector," Goldstein says.
body_zh: 特朗普政府希望取消对超级行星加热气体的监管：NPR
特朗普政府希望取消对超级行星加热气体的规定 特朗普政府希望取消拜登时代减少石油和天然气行业甲烷排放的规定。
特朗普政府希望取消对超级行星加热气体的监管
2021 年 10 月 15 日，得克萨斯州莱诺拉的一家石油和天然气设施中，耀斑燃烧了甲烷和其他碳氢化合物。大卫·戈德曼/美联社隐藏标题栏
特朗普政府提议大幅缩减拜登时代的一项规定，该规定旨在减少全国钻井场所石油和天然气行业的甲烷排放。
甲烷是气候变化的主要原因，据估计，在 20 年内，甲烷造成的地球变暖程度是二氧化碳的 80 倍。 2023 年，拜登政府敲定了旨在控制石油和天然气行业甲烷排放的规则。
特朗普总统周二在德克萨斯州拉伯克竞选时宣布了这一消息，称他的政府根据《清洁空气法》进行的修订将为该行业节省数十亿美元的生产成本，并刺激更多的国内钻探活动。该提议出台之际，共和党在中期选举前面临选民对高油价的强烈反对。
美国环保局局长李·泽尔丁在一份新闻稿中表示：“美国生产的每一桶石油和每立方英尺天然气的背后都有数以百万计的工人、企业和这个国家经济的心跳。拜登环保局破坏性地针对了这一切。”
石油和天然气行业强烈反对 2023 年规则，表示 EPA 提议的回滚将解决公司在遵守规则时面临的一些挑战。
美国石油和天然气行业贸易组织美国石油学会副会长达斯汀·迈耶在一份声明中表示：“我们期待与特朗普政府合作，采取更可行的方法来支持美国能源生产，提供更大的监管确定性并推动持续减排。”
但环保人士表示，这实际上可能会让该行业付出更多代价。
“甲烷就是天然气，或者天然气就是甲烷，”环境保护基金会副总裁乔恩·戈德斯坦说。 “因此，如果你捕获更多的天然气，你就不会让它泄漏，你就不会让它被燃烧，你就有更多的产品可以出售。这样就抵消了很多成本。”
戈德斯坦补充道：“这对我们的能源安全有害，对纳税人也有害，他们本应从这些即将被浪费的天然气中收取特许权使用费和税收收入。”
美国环保局想要取消的法规之一是“甲烷超级排放器计划”。在美国各地，石油和天然气管道、炼油厂和其他能源设施有时会发生大量甲烷泄漏。但甲烷是看不见的，检测起来很困难，更不用说价格昂贵了。超级排放计划预计于 2027 年 1 月生效。该计划将允许政府将大规模甲烷泄漏的监测委托给经过认证的第三方，包括私人和非营利性甲烷卫星计划。
新卫星旨在追踪石油和天然气行业排放的甲烷
“最简单的思考方法是，如果政府收到重大泄漏警报，那么如果经过认证的第三方报告了这一情况，那么他们就可以使用这些信息，”加州大学圣巴巴拉分校研究石油行业的政治学教授帕莎·马赫达维 (Paasha Mahdavi) 说。
“[政府]需要其他人的帮助说，‘嘿！你违法了！’这样他们就能够起诉，”马赫达维补充道。
马哈达维表示，如果该计划取消，政府将更难发现石油和天然气设施中大量泄漏的地球供暖气体。 “我们需要它，因为很难看到这些东西，”他说。
美国环保署的声明还将放宽对低产量“边际”油井甲烷泄漏的监管，这些油井被认为是“边际经济”，这意味着它们赚不了多少钱。
“人们认为边际井一定等于小排放量，”戈德斯坦说。但他说卫星和新技术发现事实并非如此。戈尔茨坦说：“这些即将结束生产寿命的老式井实际上是[石油和天然气]生产部门产生的大部分甲烷污染的罪魁祸首。”

title_en: Education secretary Linda McMahon plans to spend nearly $43,000 on office furniture
title_zh: 教育部长 Linda McMahon 计划花费近 43,000 美元购买办公家具
summary: Trump ally, who is seeking to shutter the department, had said office relocation would save taxpayers $4.8m annually The Trump administration has insisted its controversial education cuts are saving “millions of dollars” after it was reported that Linda McMaho
summary_zh: 正在寻求关闭该部门的特朗普盟友曾表示，办公室搬迁每年将为纳税人节省 480 万美元。
body_en: Education secretary Linda McMahon plans to spend nearly $43,000 on office furniture | Trump administration
Education secretary Linda McMahon plans to spend nearly $43,000 on office furniture
Trump ally, who is seeking to shutter the department, had said office relocation would save taxpayers $4.8m annually

The Trump administration has insisted its controversial education cuts are saving “millions of dollars” after it was reported that Linda McMahon, secretary of education, is planning to spend roughly $43,000 on new furniture for her office.

McMahon’s office told Congress that the secretary’s current furniture was worn out and “cannot be configurationally or aesthetically integrated into the agency’s new office space”, according to non-public records seen by the New York Times.

In March, McMahon – who is seeking to permanently shutter the Department of Education – announced the department would relocate from its headquarters in the Lyndon B Johnson building to a smaller building in downtown Washington DC, which housed the US Agency for International Development (USAID) before the Trump administration closed it down.

McMahon claimed the relocation would save taxpayers $4.8m annually. Now, the education secretary’s office needs new furniture for the office, including a new desk, conference table, chairs and other items, an unnamed senior official told the New York Times.
The new furnishings are expected to cost $43,278.64.

Savannah Newhouse, the education department’s press secretary, claimed in a statement the administration was “saving taxpayers millions of dollars” through its education cuts, adding: “Believe it or not, just like in the private sector, new federal offices need places to sit, write, and meet.”

Though McMahon is reportedly planning to furnish her new office at the department, her overall goal is to diminish staffing and remove responsibilities that her department oversees, in effect shutting it down.

Shortly after returning to office in 2025, Donald Trump signed an executive order directing McMahon, a former executive at World Wrestling Entertainment turned cabinet member, to close the Department of Education.

The Department of Education was established by Congress and can only be dissolved at the direction of Congress, but the Republican-controlled chambers have not moved to do so. But the administration has taken steps to reduce the department’s power. So far, the administration has nearly halved the department’s staffing through workforce reductions and moved department-specific responsibilities to other agencies through “interagency agreements”.
Among those, special education services have been moved to the Department of Health and Human Services and civil rights enforcement efforts have been moved to the justice department.

Trump and McMahon have insisted that effectively shuttering the Department of Education will give states more authority over education, despite states already controlling most of their education policies, and eliminate unnecessary bureaucratic processes.
body_zh: 教育部长 Linda McMahon 计划花费近 43,000 美元购买办公家具 |特朗普政府
教育部长 Linda McMahon 计划花费近 43,000 美元购买办公家具
正在寻求关闭该部门的特朗普盟友曾表示，办公室搬迁每年将为纳税人节省 480 万美元
在有报道称教育部长琳达·麦克马洪计划花费约 43,000 美元为其办公室购买新家具后，特朗普政府坚称其备受争议的教育削减措施正在节省“数百万美元”。
根据《纽约时报》看到的非公开记录，麦克马洪的办公室告诉国会，国务卿目前的家具已经破旧，“无法在配置或美观上融入该机构的新办公空间”。
今年三月，寻求永久关闭教育部的麦克马洪宣布教育部将从林登·B·约翰逊大楼的总部搬迁到华盛顿特区市中心的一栋较小的大楼，在特朗普政府关闭之前，该大楼是美国国际开发署 (USAID) 的所在地。
麦克马洪声称搬迁每年将为纳税人节省 480 万美元。一位不愿透露姓名的高级官员告诉《纽约时报》，现在，教育部长办公室需要新家具，包括新办公桌、会议桌、椅子和其他物品。
新家具预计售价 43,278.64 美元。
教育部新闻秘书萨凡纳·纽豪斯 (Savannah Newhouse) 在一份声明中声称，政府通过教育削减“为纳税人节省了数百万美元”，并补充道：“不管你信不信，就像私营部门一样，新的联邦办公室需要坐下、写作和开会的地方。”
尽管据报道麦克马洪计划为她在该部门的新办公室提供家具，但她的总体目标是减少人员配备并取消她所在部门监督的职责，实际上是关闭该部门。
2025 年重返办公室后不久，唐纳德·特朗普签署了一项行政命令，指示世界摔跤娱乐公司前高管、现内阁成员麦克马洪关闭教育部。
教育部是由国会设立的，只能根据国会的指示解散，但共和党控制的众议院尚未采取行动。但政府已采取措施削弱该部门的权力。到目前为止，政府已通过裁员将该部门的人员配置减少了近一半，并通过“机构间协议”将特定部门的职责转移给其他机构。
其中，特殊教育服务已移至卫生与公众服务部，民权执法工作已移至司法部。
特朗普和麦克马洪坚称，尽管各州已经控制了大部分教育政策，但实际上关闭教育部将赋予各州更多的教育权力，并消除不必要的官僚程序。

title_en: Fed holds interest rates steady in last decision before midterms
title_zh: 美联储在中期选举前的最后决定中保持利率稳定
summary: Fed chair Kevin Warsh said politics played no role in pause of interest rate hikes, despite inflation remaining above 3% The US Federal Reserve left interest rates unchanged on Wednesday during its last board meeting before the midterm elections, keeping rates
summary_zh: 美联储主席凯文·沃什表示，尽管通胀率仍高于 3%，但政治因素并未对暂停加息产生影响。
body_en: Fed holds interest rates steady in last decision before midterms
Fed chair Kevin Warsh said politics played no role in pause of interest rate hikes, despite inflation remaining above 3%

The US Federal Reserve left interest rates unchanged on Wednesday during its last board meeting before the midterm elections, keeping rates at one of the highest pre-election levels seen in over 20 years.
Two out of 12 board members voted against the pause, preferring to raise rates by a quarter point this meeting, the Fed board said in a statement.

Last month, Fed officials raised rates for the first time since 2023, citing rising inflation, bringing rates to a range of 3.75% to 4%. Inflation has hovered for years above the Fed’s target rate of 2%, and for most of this year, the annualized inflation rate has remained above 3%.
Though inflation rose higher in September, going from 3.4% in August to 3.7%, the pause signals the central bank is taking a wait-and-see approach ahead of the midterms next week.
During a press conference on Wednesday afternoon, the Fed chair, Kevin Warsh, told reporters that the upcoming election played no role in deliberations.
“Politics played no role in the decision,” he said. “I didn’t hear an utterance about politics.”
The central bank is still focused on price stability, he said, but emphasized that “the information that we receive over the coming period will help us determine where want policy to be”.
“The period right in front of us is information rich, there’s a lot that’s happening in the world, my colleagues and I are keen to take notice of it,” he said.
September’s rate hike infuriated Donald Trump, who said that “interest rates in the United States should be 1% or less”.

Warsh declined to comment on a remark from Donald Trump that, besides Warsh, the Fed board is full of Democratic-appointed members who “would like to see the country do badly”, but said that the latest meeting was “a heck of a family fight”.
“I’m honored to be here, and I’m honored to be chairman of this group,” he said.
Interest rates determine the cost of interest for loans, including for credit cards, mortgage and some savings accounts. During times of high inflation, raising rates can slow price increases.
Multiple Fed leaders have suggested in recent weeks that the central bank has room for a pause, even if most Fed economists are predicting one more rate hike before the end of the year.
“The hikes do not need to come at consecutive meetings, but they should be in place in an acceptable period of time,” the Fed governor Christopher Waller said earlier this month.
The proximity of the election also made it more likely that the Fed will “not take any radical action”, said Nicholas Economides, a professor of economics at the NYU Stern Business School.
“Even if the Fed were to do something radically different, the economy would not have time to adjust before the elections,” he said.

Rising prices this year have largely been driven by war in the Middle East with Iran. Oil prices have soared with the closure of the strait of Hormuz, a crucial passageway for trade. Inflation rose last month to its highest level since the spring, while oil traded briefly above $117 a barrel earlier this week, its highest price in more than six months.

The higher cost of living is expected to play a crucial role in the upcoming midterm elections that will determine which party will control Congress. Across multiple polls, the economy has been cited as the top issue for voters.
body_zh: 美联储在中期选举前的最后决定中保持利率稳定
美联储主席凯文·沃什表示，尽管通胀率仍高于3%，但政治因素并未对暂停加息产生影响
周三，美联储在中期选举前的最后一次董事会会议上维持利率不变，将利率维持在 20 多年来选举前的最高水平之一。
美联储董事会在一份声明中表示，12 名董事会成员中有两人投票反对暂停，他们更愿意在本次会议上加息 25 个基点。
上个月，美联储官员以通胀上升为由，自 2023 年以来首次加息，将利率升至 3.75% 至 4% 的区间。多年来，通胀率一直徘徊在美联储2%的目标利率之上，而今年大部分时间，年化通胀率一直保持在3%以上。
尽管 9 月份通胀率上升，从 8 月份的 3.4% 升至 3.7%，但这一暂停表明央行在下周中期选举前采取观望态度。
在周三下午的新闻发布会上，美联储主席凯文·沃什告诉记者，即将到来的选举在审议中没有发挥任何作用。
“政治在这个决定中没有发挥任何作用，”他说。 “我没有听到任何有关政治的言论。”
他表示，央行仍然关注价格稳定，但强调“我们在未来一段时间内收到的信息将帮助我们确定政策的方向”。
“我们面前的这个时期信息丰富，世界上正在发生很多事情，我和我的同事们都渴望注意到它，”他说。
9月份的加息激怒了唐纳德·特朗普，他表示“美国的利率应该在1%或更低”。
沃什拒绝对唐纳德·特朗普的言论发表评论，即除了沃什之外，美联储董事会成员都是民主党任命的成员，他们“希望看到国家表现糟糕”，但他表示，最近的会议是“一场激烈的家庭斗争”。
“我很荣幸来到这里，也很荣幸成为这个小组的主席，”他说。
利率决定贷款（包括信用卡、抵押贷款和某些储蓄账户）的利息成本。在高通胀时期，加息可以减缓价格上涨。
多位美联储领导人最近几周表示，尽管大多数美联储经济学家预测年底前会再次加息，但美联储仍有暂停的空间。
美联储理事克里斯托弗·沃勒本月早些时候表示：“加息不需要在连续会议上进行，但应该在可接受的时间内实施。”
纽约大学斯特恩商学院经济学教授尼古拉斯·伊科诺米德斯表示，大选临近也使得美联储更有可能“不会采取任何激进行动”。
“即使美联储采取完全不同的措施，经济也没有时间在选举前进行调整，”他表示。
今年价格上涨主要是由中东与伊朗的战争推动的。随着重要贸易通道霍尔木兹海峡的关闭，石油价格飙升。上个月通货膨胀率升至春季以来的最高水平，而本周早些时候油价一度升至每桶 117 美元上方，为六个月多来的最高价格。
预计较高的生活成本将在即将到来的中期选举中发挥至关重要的作用，这将决定哪个政党将控制国会。在多项民意调查中，经济被视为选民最关心的问题。

title_en: Ex-FBI officials due back in court in Hunter Biden laptop case
title_zh: 前联邦调查局官员将因亨特·拜登笔记本电脑案重返法庭
summary: A federal judge has scolded the Justice Department for its unorthodox handling of a criminal case against two former FBI officials accused of making false statements to Congress about their participation in and knowledge of investigations involving Hun...
summary_zh: 两名前联邦调查局官员被控在参与涉及前总统之子亨特·拜登的调查时向国会撒谎
body_en: Ex-FBI officials due back in court in Hunter Biden laptop case

A federal judge has scolded the Justice Department for its unorthodox handling of a criminal case against two former FBI officials accused of making false statements to Congress about their participation in and knowledge of investigations involving Hun...
By ERIC TUCKER Associated Press , ALANNA DURKIN RICHER Associated Press , and MICHAEL KUNZELMAN Associated Press

WASHINGTON -- A federal judge on Tuesday scolded prosecutors for their unorthodox handling of a criminal case against two former FBI officials accused of making false statements to Congress about their knowledge of a laptop the Justice Department says belonged to Hunter Biden , the son of former President Joe Biden.

U.S. Magistrate Zia Faruqui rejected an amended criminal complaint filed overnight by the Justice Department that added a new obstruction charge against the two former officials, Nikki Floris and Bradley Benavides, after concluding that it was improperly submitted. Such charging documents require sign-off from a judge that probable cause exists to believe a crime was committed by a defendant, but this complaint was filed straight to the docket with no court approval.

The ruling came during a dramatic, hourslong hearing in which an agent who worked the case conceded under defense lawyer questioning that the investigation was launched after a July speech from President Donald Trump on election interference and that the inquiry was mandated by FBI Director Kash Patel. The agent, Bryan Witt, suggested he had been begrudgingly assigned to the investigation and had regarded it as a “huge distraction” from other casework.
“I had concerns that this would be political,” he said.

The testimony was elicited by defense lawyers looking to bolster their argument that the prosecution was politically motivated. Faruqui's rebuke, meanwhile, marked a setback for a Justice Department that has employed unusual maneuvers in splashy investigative actions ahead of next week’s midterm elections. Newly unsealed documents in a separate case, for instance, revealed that prosecutors are attempting to again prosecute former FBI Director James Comey, an outspoken Trump critic, in a manner that Comey's lawyers say is legally invalid.

The judge said he had never before seen a prosecutor file an unsigned criminal complaint, describing it as “inappropriate” given defendants’ presumption of innocence. He ticked off several atypical aspects of the case, including the decision to file charges via criminal complaint, which the judge noted is more often used when the government has disrupted an active crime or needs to take a defendant into custody immediately because of a potential danger to society.
“Everything is a little sideshow on top of a sideshow,” Faruqui said, saying prosecutors appeared to be throwing “gas” on defendants’ assertions that there is nothing typical about this case.

Witt testified that Patel had directed that the investigation be opened after a Trump primetime address in July in which the president amplified debunked theories about the 2020 election he lost and elevated his yearslong push to raise doubts about the legitimacy of U.S. elections.

Among the grievances the White House raised at the time was a disputed FBI intelligence report about an alleged effort by China to influence the election through fraudulent driver's licenses. Trump and some allies have cited the memo as proof of what they contend was a Chinese plot to intervene in favor of Joe Biden, his Democratic opponent. But senior FBI officials ordered the document recalled because of concerns about the validity of the intelligence.

Witt, who works in Kansas City, Missouri, said Patel assigned the investigation to his office and said he was directed to investigate Floris and other officials who were believed to be involved in recalling the memo.

He said the basis for the investigation was Trump administration suspicions that the FBI in 2020 had suppressed intelligence that could have been harmful to the Bidens. He said he understood the fact that the inquiry was opened in the aftermath of a Trump speech, and at the behest of the FBI director, made it appear like a “political" investigation. Patel and FBI leadership, he said, maintained a keen interest in the probe.
“They wanted us to investigate aggressively,” Witt said.

Even before that testimony was given, Mary Dohrmann, another lawyer for Floris, broached what she called the “elephant in the room,” saying “evidence is mounting that this prosecution is about some political football — and not the law or the facts.”
The case, announced Friday, accuses Floris and Benavides of falsely playing down their knowledge about a laptop the Justice Department says Hunter Biden abandoned at a computer repair shop in 2019.
body_zh: 前联邦调查局官员将因亨特·拜登笔记本电脑案重返法庭
一名联邦法官斥责司法部对两名前联邦调查局官员刑事案件的非正统处理，两名前联邦调查局官员被指控向国会就他们参与和了解涉及匈牙利的调查做出虚假陈述。
作者：ERIC TUCKER 美联社、ALANNA DURKIN RICHER 美联社和 MICHAEL KUNZELMAN 美联社
华盛顿——周二，一名联邦法官斥责检察官对两名前联邦调查局官员刑事案件的非正统处理，两名前联邦调查局官员被控向国会作出虚假陈述，称他们了解司法部称属于前总统乔·拜登之子亨特·拜登的一台笔记本电脑。
美国治安法官齐亚·法鲁基 (Zia Faruqui) 驳回了司法部连夜提交的修改后的刑事申诉，该申诉增加了对两名前官员尼基·弗洛里斯 (Nikki Floris) 和布拉德利·贝纳维德斯 (Bradley Benavides) 的新妨碍罪指控，并得出结论认为该申诉提交不当。此类指控文件需要法官签字证明存在可能的理由相信被告实施了犯罪，但该申诉未经法院批准直接提交到备审案件中。
这项裁决是在一场戏剧性的、长达数小时的听证会上做出的，在听证会上，一名负责此案的特工在辩护律师的质疑下承认，调查是在唐纳德·特朗普总统7月份就干预选举发表演讲后启动的，而且调查是由联邦调查局局长卡什·帕特尔授权的。特工布莱恩·维特表示，他被不情愿地分配到调查中，并认为这“极大地分散了”其他案件工作的注意力。
“我担心这会涉及政治，”他说。
这些证词是由辩护律师提出的，他们希望支持他们的论点，即检方是出于政治动机。与此同时，法鲁基的谴责标志着司法部的一次挫折，司法部在下周中期选举之前采取了不寻常的手段进行引人注目的调查行动。例如，另一起案件中新近启封的文件显示，检察官正试图再次起诉直言不讳的特朗普批评者、前联邦调查局局长詹姆斯·科米，科米的律师称这种方式在法律上无效。
法官表示，他以前从未见过检察官提出未签名的刑事起诉书，并称鉴于被告无罪推定，这是“不适当的”。他列举了该案的几个非典型方面，包括通过刑事起诉提出指控的决定，法官指出，当政府制止正在进行的犯罪或因对社会存在潜在危险而需要立即拘留被告时，更常使用这种做法。
法鲁基说：“一切都是余兴节目之上的小余兴节目。”他表示，检察官似乎对被告关于本案不具有典型性的说法进行了“煽动”。
威特作证说，帕特尔在特朗普 7 月黄金时段演讲后指示启动调查，总统在演讲中放大了有关他在 2020 年大选中落败的被揭穿的理论，并强化了多年来对美国选举合法性提出质疑的努力。
白宫当时提出的不满之一是一份有争议的联邦调查局情报报告，该报告称中国涉嫌通过伪造驾驶执照影响选举。特朗普和一些盟友引用这份备忘录作为证据，证明他们认为中国阴谋进行干预，以支持他的民主党对手乔·拜登。但由于担心情报的有效性，联邦调查局高级官员下令撤回该文件。
在密苏里州堪萨斯城工作的威特说，帕特尔将调查工作交给了他的办公室，并表示他被指示调查弗洛里斯和其他据信参与召回备忘录的官员。
他表示，调查的依据是特朗普政府怀疑联邦调查局在 2020 年压制了可能对拜登家族有害的情报。他表示，他理解调查是在特朗普演讲后展开的，并且是在联邦调查局局长的要求下展开的，这使得调查看起来像是一项“政治”调查。他说，帕特尔和联邦调查局领导层对调查保持着浓厚的兴趣。
“他们希望我们积极调查，”威特说。

甚至在作证之前，弗洛里斯的另一位律师玛丽·多尔曼就提出了她所说的“房间里的大象”，她说，“越来越多的证据表明，这次起诉是关于政治足球的，而不是法律或事实。”
该案于周五宣布，指控弗洛里斯和贝纳维德斯错误地淡化了他们对司法部称亨特·拜登于 2019 年遗弃在一家电脑维修店的一台笔记本电脑的了解。

body_en: Trump, Vance and Obama are making closing stretch appeals to midterm voters in pivotal states - ABC News
Trump, Vance and Obama are making closing stretch appeals to midterm voters in pivotal states
President Donald Trump’s campaign to keep Republicans in control of Congress in the Nov. 3 midterms is returning to Ohio for the third time in a month

President Donald Trump's campaign to keep Republicans in control of Congress in the Nov. 3 midterms is returning to Ohio for the third time in a month on Wednesday, while former President Barack Obama is set to rally Democrats in Georgia .
With less than a week until Election Day, Trump is keeping his focus on states that he won handily two years ago as Americans confront record fuel prices , rising costs and an unpopular war in Iran .

Vice President JD Vance is scheduled to be in North Carolina, where Republicans have been pessimistic about retaining a Senate seat . Former national party chair Michael Whatley faces Democrat Roy Cooper, a former governor, in the race to succeed retiring Republican Sen. Thom Tillis .

Trump's stops in the closing stretch of the campaign reflect Republicans' defensive posture as the party's finances — and the president's signature super PAC, MAGA Inc. — have helped sustain candidates. He visited Mississippi on Monday and Texas on Tuesday, and plans to be in South Carolina, Florida, Kansas and Iowa in the coming days.

Obama, the last Democratic president to serve two terms, is increasingly campaigning for his party, acting as a foil to Trump. In Michigan recently, Obama criticized the Republican over his White House renovations and for becoming wealthier while in office.

Obama plans to appear in Georgia with former Atlanta Mayor Keisha Lance Bottoms, who is seeking to become the first Black woman elected governor in the United States, and Sen. Jon Ossoff, who is running for reelection and is considered a potential future presidential candidate.
In Ohio, the Republican ticket includes wealthy biotech executive Vivek Ramaswamy for governor and Sen. Jon Husted who hopes to fulfill the remainder of Vance's term.

Husted, who played football in college, has been the recipient of Trump's lavish praise for Republican candidates' physical appearance, and the president often diverts into tangents about the senator's physique no matter where he s campaigning.
Former Sen. Sherrod Brown is Democratic nominee.

Ramaswamy faces former public health official Amy Acton. His campaign has created a late-season controversy over an ad it ran , with Acton's mother, Donna Arthur, calling her daughter “a liar” who “needs help” due to a “a serious problem” being honest about her past.

Arthur has not seen her daughter in nearly 50 years and lost custody of her children after her husband, the children’s stepfather, was indicted for raping Acton when she was 12. Acton, Ohio’s former state health director , says she has not seen her mother since 1978.
Trump backed the ad but other Republicans, including Husted, have distanced themselves from it.
body_zh: 特朗普、万斯和奥巴马正在向关键州的中期选民发出最后的呼吁 - ABC News
特朗普、万斯和奥巴马正在向关键州的中期选民发出最后的呼吁
唐纳德·特朗普总统在 11 月 3 日中期选举中让共和党控制国会的竞选活动将在一个月内第三次返回俄亥俄州
唐纳德·特朗普总统为让共和党在 11 月 3 日中期选举中控制国会而开展的竞选活动将于周三第三次回到俄亥俄州，而前总统巴拉克·奥巴马也将在佐治亚州集结民主党人。
距离选举日还有不到一周的时间，特朗普将注意力集中在他两年前轻松赢得的州上，因为美国人面临着创纪录的燃油价格、不断上升的成本和不受欢迎的伊朗战争。
副总统 JD 万斯计划访问北卡罗来纳州，那里的共和党人对保住参议院席位持悲观态度。前国家党主席迈克尔·沃特利 (Michael Whatley) 在接替退休共和党参议员托姆·蒂利斯 (Thom Tillis) 的竞选中面临民主党人、前州长罗伊·库珀 (Roy Cooper)。
特朗普在竞选最后阶段的停顿反映了共和党的防御姿态，因为该党的财务状况以及总统标志性的超级政治行动委员会 MAGA Inc. 帮助维持了候选人的地位。他周一访问了密西西比州，周二访问了德克萨斯州，并计划在未来几天访问南卡罗来纳州、佛罗里达州、堪萨斯州和爱荷华州。
奥巴马是最后一位连任两届的民主党总统，他越来越多地为自己的政党竞选，充当特朗普的陪衬。最近在密歇根州，奥巴马批评共和党人对白宫的翻修以及在任期间变得更加富有。
奥巴马计划与前亚特兰大市长凯莎·兰斯·博顿斯(Keisha Lance Bottoms)和参议员乔恩·奥索夫(Jon Ossoff)一起出现在佐治亚州。凯莎·兰斯·博顿斯正在寻求成为美国第一位当选的黑人女性州长，而参议员乔恩·奥索夫正在竞选连任，被认为是未来潜在的总统候选人。
在俄亥俄州，共和党候选人包括富有的生物技术高管维韦克·拉马斯瓦米（Vivek Ramaswamy）竞选州长，以及希望完成万斯剩余任期的参议员乔恩·赫斯特德（Jon Husted）。
