亚瑟已经近 50 年没有见过她的女儿了，在她的丈夫（孩子们的继父）被指控在她 12 岁时强奸阿克顿后，阿瑟失去了孩子们的监护权。阿瑟是俄亥俄州前州卫生局长，她说自 1978 年以来她就没有见过她的母亲。
特朗普支持这则广告，但包括赫斯特德在内的其他共和党人已与该广告保持距离。

title_en: Republicans wanted Rubio on the stump. Trump coaxed him there.
title_zh: 共和党人希望卢比奥上台。特朗普把他哄到了那里。
summary: “We love you, Texas,” the secretary of State told the crowd.
summary_zh: “我们爱你，德克萨斯州，”国务卿对人群说。
body_en: Secretary of State Marco Rubio on Tuesday came as close to the campaign trail as he’s been all year. And even then, he tried to stay just offshore.

Rubio appeared with President Donald Trump in Corpus Christi, Texas, as he rallied alongside an oil tanker carrying Venezuelan crude. The visit helped spotlight a proud White House accomplishment — toppling the Venezuelan dictator Nicolás Maduro and opening the country’s energy supply — in a political battleground state.

The unexpected nature of Rubio’s presence, after the president coaxed him up on stage during the rally, is likely enough to shield the nation’s top diplomat from allegations that he is interfering in the midterm campaign. The former Florida senator has kept a careful distance from partisan politics, even as colleagues like Attorney General Todd Blanche have defied longstanding norms against some administration officials engaging in electioneering.

“It's an honor to work for the greatest country in the world, for the greatest president in the history of the United States of America,” Rubio said in brief remarks from the stage. “We love you, Texas.”

A White House official, who like others in this article was granted anonymity to share details of the trip, said that Rubio was backstage during the rally when the president brought him up and that he was only there in his capacity as national security adviser, not to stump ahead of the midterms.

While Rubio, who was not expected to speak at the event, has maintained the tradition of secretaries of State not campaigning, Republicans have been clamoring for the potential 2028 presidential hopeful to do so, seeing him as one of the party’s strongest messengers in a bruising midterm cycle in which they have been desperate for any additional help. One GOP official in a state with a key Senate race, granted anonymity to share private conversations, said that they asked for Rubio to attend a recent political event but were told the secretary of State wasn't doing political events given his role as chief diplomatic officer.

“Rubio is Trump’s best asset, and they know they are in a dog fight to win in Texas,” said Bill Cortese, a GOP operative who has advised Rep. Elise Stefanik (R-N.Y.). Even if Rubio had not come up on stage, “news of Rubio simply being in the state could potentially boost the GOP’s chances in places that they need it.”

Plus, the secretary of State had another good reason for being there: Rubio was one of the central architects of the administration’s Venezuela strategy and has been a leading figure in managing the country’s political transition and economic arrangements with the U.S. in the wake of Maduro’s ouster.
“It’s his win and his deal,” a Trump administration official added about Rubio and the Venezuela link.

Asked why Rubio accompanied Trump on the Texas trip, the White House referred to one of Trump’s Truth Social posts from August in which he credited Rubio and Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth for negotiating the oil deal with Venezuela.

A State Department spokesperson noted Rubio’s role as national security adviser and said that he “needs time with the president on all kinds of issues. The president will be on the go, so being on the plane with him gives him a chance to talk to him about these items.”
The secretary of State notably skipped the Republican National Committee’s midterm convention in Dallas last month, opting instead to go on a diplomatic trip to Colombia.

“Marco loves campaigns and politics and he cares desperately about making sure that the House and Senate remain in Republican hands, but I think he also realizes that part of being secretary of State is you don’t engage in overt political activity,” said a person close to Rubio.

In Trump’s first term, Secretary of State Mike Pompeo broke with tradition and made a handful of public appearances that directly or indirectly appeared campaign related, including delivering remarks to the Republican National Convention in 2020.

On a practical level, most secretaries of State travel overseas so much that it’s hard to spare time for campaigns. But Rubio travels more infrequently than his predecessors, in part because of his national security adviser role, which keeps him at the White House.

And Rubio also has a more nontraditional role even as secretary of State, focusing most of his energy on Latin America while the president’s special envoys, including Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner, have handled negotiations to try to end the wars in Iran, Ukraine and Gaza.

Yet the Texas visit — in which Trump sought to link one of his signature foreign policy accomplishments with efforts to reduce prices — came as a relief to the Republicans who believe Rubio is one of the party’s most trusted messengers on the economy and have for months wanted to see him on the trail.

Results from The POLITICO Poll suggest Rubio can be a useful surrogate on the campaign trail. Across three polls this month, Republican midterm voters consistently selected Rubio as their third-highest choice to hit the campaign trail to help their party, behind Trump and Vice President JD Vance but ahead of Texas Sen. Ted Cruz, Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. and others.

Support for Rubio on the campaign trail is also fairly steady across Trump’s 2024 coalition, with only an 8-point gap between the MAGA base (31%) and non-MAGA Trump voters (23%) saying the secretary of State would help Republicans if he campaigned. Meanwhile, MAGA loyalists were significantly more likely than non-MAGA Trump voters to support Trump and Vance hitting the trail.

Notably, Rubio also generates less negative backlash than other figures. Democrats widely support the impeachment of Trump, Vance, Kennedy and others. But support for impeaching Rubio is lower than the other figures, pushing overall public opinion against impeachment.
body_zh: 国务卿马可·卢比奥周二接近竞选活动，这是他全年以来最接近的一次。即便如此，他还是试图留在离岸地区。
卢比奥与唐纳德·特朗普总统一起出现在德克萨斯州科珀斯克里斯蒂，当时他在一艘运载委内瑞拉原油的油轮旁边集会。这次访问凸显了白宫在这个政治战场国家取得的令人自豪的成就——推翻委内瑞拉独裁者尼古拉斯·马杜罗并开放该国的能源供应。
在总统在集会期间将卢比奥哄上台后，卢比奥的出人意料的出现可能足以使该国最高外交官免受有关他干涉中期选举的指控。这位前佛罗里达州参议员一直与党派政治保持着谨慎的距离，尽管司法部长托德·布兰奇等同事违反了长期以来反对一些​​政府官员参与竞选的规范。
“为世界上最伟大的国家、为美利坚合众国历史上最伟大的总统工作是我的荣幸，”卢比奥在台上发表简短讲话时说道。 “我们爱你，德克萨斯。”
一位与本文中的其他人一样被要求匿名分享此行细节的白宫官员表示，总统在集会期间提到卢比奥时，他正在后台，他只是以国家安全顾问的身份出现在后台，而不是为了在中期选举前作秀。
虽然预计不会在活动中发言的卢比奥保持了国务卿不竞选的传统，但共和党人一直呼吁有望在 2028 年当选的总统发言，认为他是该党在艰难的中期周期中最强大的使者之一，在这个周期中，他们迫切需要任何额外的帮助。参议院竞选关键州的一名不愿透露姓名的共和党官员表示，他们要求卢比奥参加最近的一次政治活动，但被告知，鉴于国务卿担任首席外交官，他不会参加政治活动。
“卢比奥是特朗普最好的资产，他们知道他们正在为赢得德克萨斯州而进行一场恶战，”为纽约州共和党众议员埃莉斯·斯特凡尼克提供咨询的共和党特工比尔·科特斯说。即使卢比奥没有上台，“卢比奥在该州的消息也可能会增加共和党在他们需要的地方的机会。”
此外，国务卿出席还有另一个充分的理由：卢比奥是政府委内瑞拉战略的核心设计师之一，并且在马杜罗下台后一直是管理该国政治过渡和与美国的经济安排的领军人物。
“这是他的胜利和他的协议，”特朗普政府官员在谈到卢比奥和委内瑞拉的联系时补充道。
当被问及卢比奥为何陪同特朗普前往德克萨斯州时，白宫提到了特朗普八月份在《真相社会》上发布的一篇帖子，其中他称赞卢比奥和国防部长皮特·赫格塞斯在与委内瑞拉的石油协议谈判中做出了贡献。
美国国务院发言人提到了卢比奥作为国家安全顾问的角色，并表示他“需要与总统就各种问题进行交流。总统会经常出差，因此与他一起乘坐飞机让他有机会与总统讨论这些问题。”
国务卿特别缺席了上个月在达拉斯举行的共和党全国委员会中期大会，而是选择对哥伦比亚进行外交访问。
“马可热爱竞选和政治，他非常关心确保众议院和参议院仍掌握在共和党手中，但我认为他也意识到，担任国务卿的一部分就是不要参与公开的政治活动，”一位与卢比奥关系密切的人士表示。
在特朗普的第一个任期内，国务卿迈克·蓬佩奥 (Mike Pompeo) 打破传统，进行了几次直接或间接与竞选相关的公开露面，包括在 2020 年共和党全国代表大会上发表讲话。
实际上，大多数国务卿经常出国，很难抽出时间参加竞选活动。但卢比奥的出行频率比他的前任要少，部分原因是他的国家安全顾问角色使他留在了白宫。
即使担任国务卿，卢比奥也扮演着更非传统的角色，他将大部分精力集中在拉丁美洲，而包括史蒂夫·威特科夫和贾里德·库什纳在内的总统特使则负责处理旨在结束伊朗、乌克兰和加沙战争的谈判。
然而，特朗普试图将其标志性外交政策成就之一与降低物价的努力联系起来的德克萨斯州之行，让共和党人松了一口气，他们认为卢比奥是该党最值得信赖的经济使者之一，几个月来一直希望看到他的身影。
POLITICO 民意调查的结果表明卢比奥可以成为竞选活动中的有用代理人。在本月的三项民意调查中，共和党中期选民一致选择卢比奥作为他们在竞选活动中帮助本党的第三大选择，仅次于特朗普和副总统万斯，但领先于德克萨斯州参议员特德·克鲁兹、卫生部长小罗伯特·F·肯尼迪等人。
在特朗普的2024年联盟中，卢比奥在竞选过程中的支持率也相当稳定，支持MAGA的选民(31%)和非MAGA特朗普选民(23%)之间只有8个百分点的差距，他们认为国务卿如果参加竞选就会帮助共和党。与此同时，“MAGA”的忠实拥护者比非“MAGA”特朗普选民更有可能支持特朗普和万斯继续前进。
值得注意的是，与其他人物相比，卢比奥产生的负面反应也较少。民主党广泛支持弹劾特朗普、万斯、肯尼迪等人。但弹劾卢比奥的支持率低于其他数字，推动整体民意反对弹劾。

title_en: Billionaire taxes, trans rights, abortion, voting rights: This year’s biggest state votes
title_zh: 亿万富翁税、变性人权利、堕胎、投票权：今年最大的州投票
summary: At least $400 million has been spent on TV ads for ballot initiatives this cycle.
summary_zh: 本周期至少花费了 4 亿美元用于投票倡议的电视广告。
body_en: Statewide ballot measures are flying under the national radar — but some are drawing big spending.

At least $400 million has been spent on TV ads for ballot initiatives, according to data from the ad-tracking firm AdImpact. The 145 ballot measures across 39 states include fights attracting the attention of future presidential candidates and millions from dark money groups on both sides of the aisle.

The focus of this year’s ballot measures reflect broader shifts in the political discourse. The number of abortion-related initiatives has dropped precipitously since 2022 as states have had time to determine their individual laws following the repeal of Roe v. Wade . At the same time, voters in five states will weigh in on ballot measures focusing on transgender issues, the most in history.
Here are the most consequential ballot initiatives facing voters in November

By far the most expensive and most aggressively targeted ballot measure in November is California’s Proposition 40, which if passed would levy a one-time 5% tax on the state’s billionaires. An eye-watering $92 million has been spent on TV ads debating the issue, mostly on the “No” side, although that pales in comparison to what the Silicon Valley tycoons opposing the initiative like tech investor Peter Thiel and Google co-founder Sergey Brin would be forced to pay should it pass.

Leading progressive figures including Bernie Sanders and Ro Khanna are backing the “Yes” side. Caught in the middle is Gov. Gavin Newsom, a potential 2028 presidential candidate, who’s opposed the measure even as he’s tried to claim some populist credibility by proposing a national tax hike on billionaires. A Citrin-POLITICO poll earlier this month found the measure receiving 46% support, short of the majority needed to pass.

Newsom and Brin are both backing another ballot measure, Prop 42, a separate question that would cancel out the Prop 40 wealth tax if it passes. If both pass, Prop 42 could still cancel out Prop 40 if it receives more votes.

Maryland Gov. Wes Moore is making himself the face of a constitutional amendment that, if it passes, would pave the way for the state legislature to draw new lines turning the state’s lone GOP House seat solidly blue. Moore, a potential presidential candidate in 2028, is taking a cue from Newsom, who passed a redistricting referendum last year that is likely to swing five House seats in favor of Democrats. Former President Barack Obama cut an ad for the “Yes” campaign this week.

Missouri Democrats recently won a contentious legal battle that barred the GOP from using a new gerrymander to erase a Kansas City-area Democratic seat held by Rep. Emanuel Cleaver and allowed voters a referendum on whether that gerrymander will be used in future elections.. Now, voters get to choose what the state does going forward. The campaign pushing “No” on the referendum reported raising $6 million earlier this month, with big help from Democratic megadonors, including LinkedIn co-founder Reid Hoffman and Illinois Gov. JB Pritzker.
Transgender rights restrictions hit the ballot
This year marks the first time multiple states have taken up ballot initiatives focusing on transgender issues.

The six initiatives across Colorado, Missouri, Washington, Arizona and Nebraska help make up the most LGBTQ+-related ballot measures in a year since the Supreme Court legalized same-sex marriage in 2015. Each of the measures asks voters to either ban transgender surgeries for minors or restrict access to girls sports for transgender girls.

Measures in Nevada and Virginia would enshrine abortion access in those states’ constitutions, similar to measures that have passed over the last few years in Ohio, Michigan, Montana and other states.

A measure in Idaho, which would override the state’s near-total ban, is a statutory change rather than a constitutional one, meaning the GOP-dominated state legislature could (and is expected to) vote to override it if it passes.

Missouri has a social conservative combo: a proposition to overturn the abortion-rights constitutional amendment that voters approved in 2024 and reinstate a near-total ban on the procedure that would also prohibit gender transition surgeries for minors. Advocacy groups on both sides are pouring millions into the initiatives, with abortion rights groups spending $22.5 million and anti-abortion groups spending $8.7 million on TV ads, with most of that money being spent in Missouri.

Over a dozen ballot measures will weigh election administration rules for future elections. In seven states,voters could approve requirements for valid ID to vote. Six states will give voters the chance to explicitly codify in state law that only U.S. citizens can vote in the state. Massachusetts voters will weigh in on whether to establish a top-two nonpartisan primary system, like California has, while Alaska voters will decide if the state will end its top-four primary and ranked-choice voting laws in favor of traditional party primaries and first-past-the-post vote counting.
body_zh: 全州范围内的投票措施正在全国范围内进行，但有些措施正在吸引巨额支出。
根据广告跟踪公司 AdImpact 的数据，投票活动的电视广告至少花费了 4 亿美元。横跨 39 个州的 145 项投票措施包括吸引未来总统候选人和两党黑钱集团数百万人关注的斗争。
今年投票措施的重点反映了政治话语中更广泛的转变。自 2022 年以来，与堕胎相关的举措数量急剧下降，因为在废除罗伊诉韦德案后，各州有时间确定各自的法律。与此同时，五个州的选民将参与针对跨性别问题的投票措施，这是历史上最多的一次。
以下是十一月选民面临的最重要的投票倡议
迄今为止，11 月份最昂贵、最具针对性的投票措施是加州的 40 号提案，该提案如果获得通过，将对该州的亿万富翁一次性征收 5% 的税。令人眼花缭乱的9200万美元花费在电视广告上，用于辩论这一问题，其中大多数是反对派，尽管这与反对该倡议的硅谷大亨（如科技投资者彼得泰尔和谷歌联合创始人谢尔盖布林）如果该法案通过将被迫支付的费用相比显得相形见绌。
包括伯尼·桑德斯和罗·卡纳在内的领先进步人士都支持“是”一方。夹在中间的是可能成为 2028 年总统候选人的州长加文·纽瑟姆 (Gavin Newsom)，他反对这项措施，尽管他试图通过提议对亿万富翁提高国家税收来获得一定的民粹主义可信度。本月早些时候进行的 Citrin-POLITICO 民意调查发现，该措施获得了 46% 的支持，低于通过所需的多数票。
纽瑟姆和布林都支持另一项投票措施，即第 42 号提案，这是一个单独的问题，如果通过，将取消第 40 号提案的财富税。如果两者都通过，如果 42 号提案获得更多选票，它仍然可以取消 40 号提案。
马里兰州州长韦斯·摩尔正在为一项宪法修正案代言，如果该修正案获得通过，将为州立法机构划定新界限铺平道路，将该州唯一的共和党众议院席位变成纯蓝色。摩尔是 2028 年潜在的总统候选人，他从纽瑟姆那里得到了启发，纽瑟姆去年通过了一次选区重新划分公投，可能会将五个众议院席位转向民主党。前总统巴拉克·奥巴马本周为“是”运动剪了一则广告。

密苏里州民主党最近赢得了一场有争议的法律战，该战禁止共和党使用新的选区划分来消除众议员伊曼纽尔·克利弗(Emanuel Cleaver)在堪萨斯城地区的民主党席位，并允许选民就是否在未来的选举中使用该选区划分进行公投。现在，选民可以选择该州未来的行动。反对公投的竞选团队报告称，本月早些时候筹集了 600 万美元，其中包括 LinkedIn 联合创始人 Reid Hoffman 和伊利诺伊州州长 JB Pritzker 等民主党巨额捐助者的大力帮助。
变性人权利限制进入投票
今年是多个州首次针对跨性别问题发起投票倡议。
科罗拉多州、密苏里州、华盛顿州、亚利桑那州和内布拉斯加州的六项举措构成了自 2015 年最高法院将同性婚姻合法化以来一年内与 LGBTQ+ 相关最多的投票措施。每一项措施都要求选民要么禁止未成年人进行变性手术，要么限制变性女孩参加女童运动。
内华达州和弗吉尼亚州的措施将把堕胎权写入这些州的宪法，类似于过去几年俄亥俄州、密歇根州、蒙大拿州和其他州通过的措施。
爱达荷州的一项措施将推翻该州几乎全面的禁令，这是一项法定变更，而不是宪法变更，这意味着共和党主导的州立法机构可以（并且预计将）投票推翻该法案，如果该措施获得通过。
密苏里州有一个社会保守派组合：一项提议推翻选民于 2024 年批准的堕胎权宪法修正案，并恢复对该程序的近乎全面禁令，该程序也将禁止未成年人进行变性手术。双方的倡导团体都向这些倡议投入了数百万美元，其中堕胎权利团体花费了 2250 万美元，反堕胎团体在电视广告上花费了 870 万美元，其中大部分资金都花在了密苏里州。
十多项投票措施将权衡未来选举的选举管理规则。在七个州，选民可以批准有效身份证件投票的要求。六个州将让选民有机会在州法律中明确规定只有美国公民才能在该州投票。马萨诸塞州选民将权衡是否像加利福尼亚州那样建立前两名无党派初选制度，而阿拉斯加选民将决定该州是否结束前四名初选和排名选择投票法，转而支持传统的政党初选和简单多数票计票。

title_en: A judge halted D.C. golf course renovations. Trump says they'll still start next month
title_zh: 法官叫停了华盛顿特区高尔夫球场的翻修工程。特朗普称他们仍将在下个月开始
summary: A federal judge has barred the government from clearing more trees or making other alterations to D.C.'s East Potomac Park without proper notice. Trump says his administration will appeal.
summary_zh: 一名联邦法官禁止政府在没有适当通知的情况下清除更多树木或对华盛顿东波托马克公园进行其他改造。特鲁姆
body_en: A judge halted D.C. golf course renovations. Trump says they'll still start next month

President Trump, seen touring the East Potomac Golf Links in late June, says his administration will appeal the judge's ruling and close the course for renovations next month. Kent Nishimura/AFP via Getty Images hide caption

After weeks of tense hearings and late-night court filings, a federal judge has temporarily blocked the Trump administration from making any further alterations to East Potomac Park, the municipal D.C. golf course that the president wants to redevelop into a championship-level venue.

The long-simmering legal battle kicked into high gear in recent weeks, after the government cut down 430 trees on the golf course with less than a day's notice. That prompted a pair of lengthy court hearings that at times turned heated, with government officials repeatedly insisting that the tree-clearing was unrelated to the renovations President Trump had touted on social media. They contradicted the president's own social media posts from that very morning by saying there was no final plan for those renovations at all.

"Rarely, if ever, has the United States Department of Justice urged a federal court not to believe the sitting president," U.S. District Judge Ana Reyes wrote in her 70-page opinion . "And yet, here we are."
A D.C. park was made 'for the pleasure of the people.' Trump's plan would change that

Reyes extended what was initially a two-week halt to tree removal, ordering the government not to cut down "or substantially prune or otherwise damage or impair" any trees at East Potomac Park without a court order. She also ordered it to provide "no less than ten business days' written advance notice" before closing or making any "irreversible modification" to any parts of the park while the legal battle plays out.
"By issuing this preliminary injunction, the Court does not end the round: it simply marks the ball until the parties can fully and fairly litigate this case," Reyes wrote.

Monday's ruling is a win for the D.C. Preservation League and a pair of local golfers who sued to prevent renovations earlier this year — and for the growing grassroots movement to protect the municipal course and the surrounding recreational area, which is beloved by runners, cyclists, birders and others.

"We are grateful the court intervened to stop the Trump-Vance administration's greed and lawlessness while the case continues, and we are eager to argue the case in court," said Skye Perryman, the president of the nonprofit Democracy Forward, which is representing the plaintiffs.
Judge chastises Trump administration plan to push ahead overhaul of DC golf course
In a Truth Social post late Monday, Trump said the Department of the Interior will appeal the ruling. NPR has reached out to the Department of Interior but did not hear back in time for publication.

Trump also doubled down on his earlier announcement that construction will begin on Nov. 15 and keep the park closed for 15 months, adding that the "judge has absolutely no right to hold up this very important and beautiful Project."

"To have to give advanced notices to a judge who has no expertise in Golf, Architecture, Landscaping, Construction, or anything else having to do with building such a World Class Project, is not fair, appropriate, or Constitutional," Trump wrote.
Reyes herself has said she is not interested in policing the federal government's landscaping efforts.

That's why, as she explained in Monday's opinion, she repeatedly declined to intervene in the case — instead issuing repeated warnings against any unannounced major alterations — until "the Government did what it assured all it would not do."
"The Court earlier stated, 'I am not the Lorax. I do not speak for the trees,'" Reyes concluded. "The Court still does not speak for the trees. It speaks only for the rule of law."

On Tuesday afternoon, Reyes made a record of Trump's post and gave the government about 24 hours to clarify whether a plan exists to close East Potomac in mid-November and, if so, "how that can be reconciled" with what its lawyers previously told the court. She said she will schedule a status hearing for either Friday or Monday.
The judge took aim at the government's contradictions

Reyes' strongly-worded 70-page opinion came exactly a week after a seven-hour hearing in which she clashed repeatedly with the government's lawyers. She had already rejected the administration's request to recuse herself from the case because of alleged bias.
body_zh: 法官叫停了华盛顿特区高尔夫球场的翻修工程。特朗普称他们仍将在下个月开始
六月下旬，特朗普总统参观了东波托马克高尔夫球场，他表示，他的政府将对法官的裁决提出上诉，并在下个月关闭球场进行翻修。 Kent Nishimura/法新社来自盖蒂图片社 隐藏标题栏
经过数周紧张的听证会和深夜法庭文件后，一名联邦法官暂时阻止特朗普政府对东波托马克公园进行任何进一步改造，总统希望将东波托马克公园改造成锦标赛级场地。
最近几周，政府在不到一天的通知时间内砍伐了高尔夫球场上的 430 棵树，这场酝酿已久的法律战近几周进入白热化阶段。这引发了两次冗长的法庭听证会，听证会有时变得激烈，政府官员一再坚称砍伐树木与特朗普总统在社交媒体上吹捧的翻修工程无关。他们与总统当天早上在社交媒体上发布的帖子相矛盾，称根本没有这些翻修的最终计划。
美国地区法官安娜·雷耶斯 (Ana Reyes) 在长达 70 页的意见中写道：“美国司法部很少（如果有的话）敦促联邦法院不要相信现任总统。” “然而，我们到了。”
华盛顿公园是“为了人民的欢乐”而建造的。特朗普的计划将改变这一现状
雷耶斯延长了最初为期两周的树木清除禁令，命令政府在未经法院命令的情况下不得砍伐“或大幅修剪或以其他方式损坏或损害”东波托马克公园的任何树木。她还命令公园在法律诉讼期间关闭或对公园的任何部分进行任何“不可逆转的修改”之前提供“不少于十个工作日的书面提前通知”。
雷耶斯写道：“通过发布这一初步禁令，法院并没有结束这一轮比赛：它只是对球进行标记，直到双方能够充分、公平地对此案提起诉讼。”
周一的裁决对华盛顿特区保护联盟和两名当地高尔夫球手来说是一场胜利，他们今年早些时候提起诉讼，要求阻止翻修工程，对日益壮大的草根运动来说，这是一场胜利，以保护市政球场和周围的休闲区，这些休闲区深受跑步者、骑自行车者、观鸟者和其他人的喜爱。
代表原告的非营利组织“民主前进”主席斯凯·佩里曼表示：“我们很感激法院介入，制止了特朗普-万斯政府的贪婪和无法无天行为，同时案件还在继续，我们渴望在法庭上辩论此案。”
法官严厉谴责特朗普政府推动华盛顿特区高尔夫球场检修的计划
特朗普周一晚间在《真相社会》帖子中表示，内政部将对这一裁决提出上诉。 NPR 已联系内政部，但没有及时收到回复以供发布。
特朗普还强调了他早些时候宣布的施工将于 11 月 15 日开始并将公园关闭 15 个月的说法，并补充说“法官绝对没有权利阻止这个非常重要和美丽的项目。”
特朗普写道：“必须提前向一位在高尔夫、建筑、景观美化、施工或与建设这样一个世界级项目有关的其他领域没有专业知识的法官发出通知，这是不公平、不适当的，也不符合宪法。”
雷耶斯本人表示，她对监管联邦政府的景观美化工作不感兴趣。
这就是为什么，正如她在周一的意见中所解释的那样，她一再拒绝干预此案，而是反复警告不要进行任何未经宣布的重大变更，直到“政府做了它保证不会做的事情”。
“法院早些时候表示，‘我不是洛拉克斯人。我不代表树木发言，’”雷耶斯总结道。 “法院仍然不为树木说话。它只为法治说话。”
周二下午，雷耶斯记录了特朗普的帖子，并给了政府大约 24 小时的时间来澄清是否有计划在 11 月中旬关闭东波托马克，如果有，“如何与律师之前告诉法庭的内容相一致”。她说她将安排周五或周一举行状态听证会。
法官直指政府矛盾
雷耶斯在长达七小时的听证会一周后发表了措辞强硬的 70 页意见，听证会上她与政府律师多次发生冲突。她已经拒绝了政府因涉嫌偏见而回避此案的要求。

title_en: Experts react to new findings on CTE in former NFL players
title_zh: 专家对前 NFL 球员 CTE 的新发现做出反应
summary: A new study from Boston University looks at the rate of the brain disease CTE in former NFL players who died between 2008 and 2023.
summary_zh: 波士顿大学的一项新研究调查了 2008 年至 2023 年间死亡的前 NFL 球员的脑部疾病 CTE 发生率。
body_en: Experts weigh in on study estimating 75% of NFL players who died in recent years had signs of CTE - CBS News

A new study from Boston University estimating that nearly 75% of NFL players who died over a 15-year period had signs of CTE in their brains is raising concern, and experts say it demonstrates the need to collect more data on the condition.

CTE, or chronic traumatic encephalopathy, is a degenerative brain disease found in people who have suffered repeated blows to the head. It can only be definitively diagnosed after death. It has also been found in the brains of other athletes , first responders and military members, but is rarely seen in the general population.

The Boston University research builds on data published in The British Medical Journal in August. That data estimated that anywhere from 25% to 98% of ex-NFL players who died between 2016 and 2021 had CTE. The broad estimate reflected uncertainty about how representative brain donors studied were of the overall NFL population, since brain donors are more likely to have symptoms believed to be related to CTE.

The Boston researchers looked for signs of the condition in brains donated by 387 players who died between 2008 and 2023 — a subset of the 2,362 former NFL players who died during that period. Ninety-four percent of the donors had some form of CTE. The researchers estimated that former NFL players with cognitive symptoms were 5 times more likely to have their brains donated to science than others, and estimated from there that 74.5% of players had some form of CTE. The research is published in JAMA Network Open .

CBS News chief medical correspondent Dr. Jon LaPook cautioned that that figure may be an overestimate. He noted that the research looked at how many former players had signs of CTE in their brain — not how many showed actual symptoms of CTE.

Dr. Kristen Dams-O'Connor, director of the Brain Injury Research Center at Mount Sinai , said the results of the paper "cannot and should not be interpreted as being representative of current living athletes." She pointed out that of those whose brains were studied, "many ... ended their careers long ago." In recent years, the NFL has implemented rule changes that are designed to reduce concussions on the field, and introduced more protective equipment, including Guardian Caps .
"This should translate to lower CTE risk in recent generations of players, compared to those who played decades ago," Dams-O'Connor said.
The NFL told CBS News in a statement that it "continuously strives to make the game of football safer, including by implementing strategies to reduce concussions and head impacts."

Dams-O'Connor said that while Boston University used "strong methods" to adjust for selection bias in the data, there are still other gaps, such as accounting for the approximately 20,000 NFL players who could have died during the study's 15-year timeframe but did not. She also said the results could not be applied to the "vast majority of people who played youth football" or other non-professional contact sports.

"It's a helpful study in trying to look at the bigger picture, recognizing that those who donate their brain are more likely to have cognitive symptoms, and often are more likely to have had changes," said Dr. Jeremy Tanner, assistant professor of neurology at The Glenn Biggs Institute for Alzheimer's and Neurological Diseases at the UT San Antonio Health Science Center. "Even taking that selection bias into account, when you look more broadly, it's at a minimum 20 to 25%, which is eye-opening and really shows the need to both advance the research."
Dr. Jay Alberts, director of the Cleveland Clinic Concussion Center, said the data shows the need to look for early warning signs of CTE.

"We often think about neurological disease, including CTE, as having a silent phase. These things are changing, and we can't detect them," Alberts said. "But I don't think it's silent, per se. I think what we need to do is listen more carefully and use better measurements to understand what those changes are."

Those measurements could include studying a person's "instrumental activities of daily living," or IADLs, Alberts said. That includes skills like driving a car or balancing a checkbook, where a person must use both cognitive function and motor function simultaneously. In patients with Alzheimer's or Parkinson's disease, IADLs start to change between five and seven years before a diagnosis is made. He said CTE may be similar.
"Those types of activities are really insights into brain function, and I would argue those are things that would help us to listen more effectively," he said.

Understanding how a person's brain function may change during the early stages of CTE could make it easier to diagnose, Alberts said. That could also lead to interventions that might "slow it or even potentially reverse it."

Alberts and Tanner also highlighted research focused on determining if there are biomarker changes that could be connected to CTE. Ongoing studies, including one that has a study site at UT Health San Antonio, follow current or former players throughout their life to see if there are any abnormal changes to the body or brain over the years. Alberts called for even more long-term research, and Tanner said that such studies can benefit more than just former NFL players.

"This has really been a rapid area of scientific advancement over the last 10 to 20 years, and has led to breakthroughs in the new therapies for Alzheimer's disease, and hopefully (will) for many other neurodegenerative diseases like CTE, Lewy body disease, and others in the years to come," Tanner said.

"Hopefully we can develop tools and biomarkers to detect these brain changes during life, which will enable us to study these diseases during life, and in the best case, learn ways to better prevent or treat these diseases."
Hayden Panettiere's death ruled accidental by police in South Carolina
body_zh: 专家们参与了一项研究，估计近年来死亡的 NFL 球员中有 75% 有 CTE 迹象 - CBS 新闻
波士顿大学的一项新研究估计，在 15 年内死亡的 NFL 球员中，近 75% 的大脑中存在 CTE 迹象，这引起了人们的关注，专家表示，这表明需要收集更多有关这种情况的数据。
CTE（慢性创伤性脑病）是一种退行性脑部疾病，常见于头部反复受到打击的人。只有在死后才能明确诊断。在其他运动员、急救人员和军人的大脑中也发现了这种现象，但在普通人群中很少见。
波士顿大学的研究建立在八月份《英国医学杂志》上发表的数据的基础上。该数据估计，2016 年至 2021 年间死亡的前 NFL 球员中有 25% 至 98% 患有 CTE。广泛的估计反映了关于所研究的代表性大脑捐赠者在整个 NFL 人群中的不确定性，因为大脑捐赠者更有可能出现被认为与 CTE 相关的症状。

波士顿研究人员在 2008 年至 2023 年间死亡的 387 名球员捐赠的大脑中寻找这种疾病的迹象，这些球员是同期死亡的 2,362 名前 NFL 球员的一部分。 94% 的捐赠者患有某种形式的 CTE。研究人员估计，患有认知症状的前 NFL 球员将大脑捐献给科学的可能性是其他人的 5 倍，并据此估计 74.5% 的球员患有某种形式的 CTE。该研究发表在 JAMA Network Open 上。
哥伦比亚广播公司新闻首席医学记者乔恩·拉普克博士警告说，这个数字可能被高估了。他指出，这项研究着眼于有多少前球员的大脑中有 CTE 迹象，而不是有多少人表现出实际的 CTE 症状。
西奈山脑损伤研究中心主任克里斯汀·达姆斯-奥康纳博士表示，这篇论文的结果“不能也不应该被解释为代表当前在世的运动员”。她指出，在那些接受大脑研究的人中，“许多人……很久以前就结束了自己的职业生涯。”近年来，NFL 实施了旨在减少场上脑震荡的规则变更，并引入了更多防护设备，包括监护帽。
达姆斯-奥康纳说：“与几十年前的球员相比，这应该意味着近几代球员的 CTE 风险较低。”
NFL 在一份声明中告诉哥伦比亚广播公司新闻，它“不断努力使橄榄球比赛更加安全，包括实施减少脑震荡和头部撞击的策略。”
达姆斯-奥康纳表示，虽然波士顿大学使用了“强有力的方法”来调整数据中的选择偏差，但仍然存在其他差距，例如考虑到在研究的 15 年时间范围内大约 20,000 名 NFL 球员可能已经死亡，但最终没有死亡。她还表示，研究结果不能适用于“绝大多数参加青少年足球的人”或其他非职业接触运动。
德克萨斯大学圣安东尼奥健康科学中心格伦·比格斯阿尔茨海默病和神经疾病研究所的神经学助理教授杰里米·坦纳博士说：“这是一项有益的研究，试图着眼于更大的前景，认识到那些捐献大脑的人更有可能出现认知症状，而且往往更有可能发生变化。” “即使考虑到选择偏差，当你更广泛地观察时，你会发现它至少在 20% 到 25% 之间，这令人大开眼界，也确实表明了推进研究的必要性。”
克利夫兰诊所脑震荡中心主任 Jay Alberts 博士表示，数据显示有必要寻找 CTE 的早期预警信号。
“我们经常认为神经系统疾病，包括 CTE，有一个沉默阶段。这些事情正在发生变化，但我们无法检测到它们，”艾伯茨说。 “但我认为它本身并不是沉默的。我认为我们需要做的是更仔细地倾听并使用更好的测量来了解这些变化是什么。”
艾伯茨说，这些测量可能包括研究一个人的“日常生活工具性活动”（IADL）。这包括驾驶汽车或平衡支票簿等技能，在这些技能中，一个人必须同时使用认知功能和运动功能。对于阿尔茨海默病或帕金森病患者，IADL 在诊断前五到七年开始发生变化。他说 CTE 可能类似。
“这些类型的活动确实是对大脑功能的深入了解，我认为这些活动可以帮助我们更有效地倾听，”他说。
艾伯茨说，了解一个人的大脑功能在 CTE 的早期阶段如何变化可以使诊断变得更容易。这也可能导致干预措施可能“减缓甚至可能逆转它”。
Alberts 和 Tanner 还强调了专注于确定是否存在可能与 CTE 有关的生物标志物变化的研究。正在进行的研究，包括在圣安东尼奥大学健康中心设有研究中心的一项研究，跟踪现任或前任球员的一生，看看多年来身体或大脑是否有任何异常变化。艾伯茨呼吁进行更长期的研究，坦纳表示，此类研究不仅能让前 NFL 球员受益。
Tanner 说：“这确实是过去 10 到 20 年来科学进步的一个快速领域，并导致了阿尔茨海默病新疗法的突破，并有望在未来几年针对许多其他神经退行性疾病，如 CTE、路易体病和其他疾病。”
“希望我们能够开发工具和生物标志物来检测生命中的这些大脑变化，这将使我们能够在生命中研究这些疾病，并在最好的情况下，学习更好地预防或治疗这些疾病的方法。”
南卡罗来纳州警方裁定海顿·潘妮蒂尔死于意外

title_en: High-speed train crash in Spain kills at least 68, dozens injured
title_zh: 西班牙高铁相撞事故造成至少68人死亡、数十人受伤
summary: Dozens of people were killed or injured when a high-speed train crashed into another train in central Spain, officials said.
summary_zh: 官员称，西班牙中部一列高速列车与另一列列车相撞，造成数十人死亡或受伤。
body_en: A high-speed train slammed into the rear of another train that had stopped in central Spain , derailing two cars and killing at least 68 people Wednesday morning, according to local authorities.

The regional government of Castilla La Mancha confirmed the death toll and said another 58 people were receiving medical treatment at hospitals. Rescue workers continue searching the wreckage for survivors and bodies.
The crash occurred Wednesday morning in the province of Toledo, according to Spain's rail system operator ADIF. Rail service was suspended between Madrid, Ciudad Real and Andalusia.

Padilla told state broadcaster TVE the accident was between two high-speed trains heading in the same direction from Madrid to Seville and that one ran into the tail of the other while it was stopped, knocking two of its cars off the track.

The accident involved a train from Spain's state-owned RENFE company and the private rail company IRYO. Trains from those two companies were also involved in a deadly crash in January. Padilla said 397 passengers were in the RENFE train and 147 passengers were in the IRYO train.
"Today all of Spain is grieving," Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez said from the crash site, where he announced that his government would declare three days of national mourning.
Sánchez called for increased safety measures to restore confidence in a high-speed rail system that was once a source of national pride.
"It is unacceptable for a country like Spain to suffer two high-speed rail accidents in the same year," said Sánchez, who faces a national election on Nov. 29.

Spain's Transport Minister Óscar Puente said the crash was caused by what he called the "inexplicable" order from a central command center for Spain's trains after a security system had failed. He said the train engineers were not to blame.

Puente said that at 8:30 a.m. the security system on a stretch of 63 kilometers (39 miles) stopped working due to a computer malfunction, causing all trains on that stretch to stop. But the central command told the RENFE train to start running again without any speed restrictions, and it ended up colliding with the stopped IRYO train at 8:53 a.m.

Puente said the train should never have been told to start moving again since there was still a "stop signal" active on that line. And if it had, at least it should have been told to go at reduced speed.
Authorities were still studying information to see how fast the train was going, but it could have been at 200 kph (124 mph) for that stretch of the track, Puente said.
"I am not attributing responsibility to anyone, I am just stating the facts," Puente said.

The crash, which occurred in a flat stretch surrounded by olive fields in between the towns of Urda and Los Yébenes, left carriages shredded into bits of metal and other material, scattering debris down a gravel slope.
Spanish Health Minister Mónica García said that emergency workers were focused on rescuing survivors and bodies from the most damaged train cars.
"It was a high-speed impact, so we are expecting this to be a tragedy," García said.
One passenger said, "We were all thrown into the air." He said he was "reasonably OK" but that his friend was in much worse condition.
Passenger Ignacio Relaño was traveling on the RENFE train. He told state broadcaster TVE that the train had stopped momentarily on the line before it started again and then crashed into the IRYO.

"We all felt the train abruptly slowing down and then the impact," he said. "The car leaned to one side like it was about to tip over. I hit my nose, everything went flying, luggage, cell phones. Everything shook."

Another passenger recounted to Cadena Ser radio how she felt the train slam on the brakes and was thrown forward in her seat, breaking the small table in front of her. She said she saw body parts and trapped people covered in blood.
body_zh: 据地方当局称，周三上午，一列高速列车撞上另一列停在西班牙中部的火车尾部，造成两节车厢脱轨，造成至少 68 人死亡。
卡斯蒂利亚拉曼恰地方政府证实了死亡人数，并表示另有 58 人正在医院接受治疗。救援人员继续在残骸中搜寻幸存者和尸体。
据西班牙铁路系统运营商 ADIF 称，事故于周三上午发生在托莱多省。马德里、雷阿尔城和安达卢西亚之间的铁路服务暂停。
帕迪拉告诉国家电视台TVE，事故发生在两列从马德里开往塞维利亚的高速列车之间，其中一列高速列车在停车时撞上了另一列列车的车尾，导致其中两节车厢脱离轨道。
事故涉及西班牙国有RENFE公司和私营铁路公司IRYO的一列火车。这两家公司的火车在一月份也发生了一起致命事故。帕迪拉说，RENFE 列车上有 397 名乘客，IRYO 列车上有 147 名乘客。
西班牙首相佩德罗·桑切斯在坠机现场表示：“今天，整个西班牙都在悲伤。”他宣布政府将宣布为期三天的全国哀悼。
桑切斯呼吁加强安全措施，以恢复人们对曾经是民族自豪感的高铁系统的信心。
“像西班牙这样的国家在同一年发生两起高铁事故是不可接受的，”即将于 11 月 29 日举行全国大选的桑切斯说。
西班牙交通部长奥斯卡·普恩特表示，这起事故是由西班牙火车中央指挥中心在安全系统失效后发出的“莫名其妙”的命令造成的。他说火车工程师不应该受到责备。
普恩特说，上午8点30分，由于计算机故障，63公里（39英里）范围内的安全系统停止工作，导致该范围内的所有火车停止运行。但中央指挥部要求 RENFE 列车重新开始运行，不受任何速度限制，最终于上午 8 点 53 分与停止运行的 IRYO 列车相撞。
普恩特表示，火车不应该被告知重新开始行驶，因为该线路上仍然有“停止信号”。如果有的话，至少应该告诉它放慢速度。
Puente 表示，当局仍在研究信息以了解火车的行驶速度，但该路段的行驶速度可能为 200 公里/小时（124 英里/小时）。
普恩特说：“我不会将责任归咎于任何人，我只是陈述事实。”
事故发生在乌尔达镇和洛斯耶贝内斯镇之间一片橄榄田环绕的平坦地带，车厢被撕成金属和其他材料的碎片，碎片散落到砾石斜坡上。
西班牙卫生部长莫妮卡·加西亚表示，紧急救援人员的工作重点是从受损最严重的火车车厢中营救幸存者和尸体。
加西亚说：“这是一次高速撞击，因此我们预计这将是一场悲剧。”
一名乘客说：“我们都被抛到了空中。”他说他“还算不错”，但他朋友的情况要糟糕得多。
乘客 Ignacio Relaño 乘坐 RENFE 列车。他告诉国家电视台 TVE，火车在线路上短暂停留，然后再次启动，然后撞上了 IRYO。
“我们都感觉到火车突然减速，然后是撞击，”他说。 “汽车向一侧倾斜，就像要翻倒一样。我撞到了鼻子，所有东西都飞了起来，行李、手机。一切都摇晃起来。”
另一位乘客向 Cadena Ser 广播电台讲述了她如何感觉到火车猛踩刹车，她的座位被向前抛起，撞碎了她面前的小桌子。她说她看到尸体残骸和被困人员浑身是血。

summary_zh: 密西西比州参议院竞选最后阶段播放次数最多的广告，内容是杰弗里·爱泼斯坦的幸存者攻击共和党参议员辛迪·海德·史密斯以争取投票
body_en: The most-aired ad in the closing stretch of Mississippi's Senate race features a Jeffrey Epstein survivor attacking GOP Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith for voting against releasing files related to the convicted human trafficker.
Why it matters: In the past week, Hyde-Smith has been outgunned on the airwaves. AdImpact data shows that only one of the eight most-aired spots portrays her positively.

Five of the ads either positively portray her Democratic challenger, Scott Colom , or attack Hyde-Smith for her Senate record, largely painting her as an out-of-touch senator who cares more about her rich donors. The other two ads are for down-ballot races.
Zoom out: The Epstein survivor ad has aired more than 1,200 times over the last week, costing the left-leaning New Deal for All super PAC over $329K, per AdImpact.
In the ad, Jena-Lisa Jones condemns Hyde-Smith for her vote on the Epstein files and urges Mississippians to vote against her to protect their children.
That vote, which passed 51-49 last year, indefinitely postponed an amendment that would have required the full release of the Epstein files by then-Attorney General Pam Bondi.

"I do want transparency, and I support releasing information that can legally be released while protecting Epstein's victims. But a procedural vote on one amendment is not the same thing as saying the Epstein files should remain secret," Hyde-Smith said in a statement to the Mississippi Free Press.
Hyde-Smith's campaign cut its own attack against Colom, calling him the "transgender defender" and naming him the "most radical Senate candidate of our lifetime."
The ad played over 2,800 times across Mississippi and Memphis, Tenn., television markets in the 30 days since its Sept. 10 debut, costing the senator's campaign over $854K, per AdImpact.
Hyde-Smith's campaign appears to have pulled back on the ad, spending less than $150,000 to air it between Oct. 19 and Oct. 26.
The bottom line: Hyde-Smith is still expected to win, but the race is far tighter than anyone expected.
As President Trump said during a rally for Hyde-Smith in Corinth, Miss. on Monday: "I'm here because Cindy is doing great, but I've just got to make sure."
body_zh: 密西西比州参议院竞选最后阶段播放次数最多的广告中，杰弗里·爱泼斯坦的幸存者攻击共和党参议员辛迪·海德·史密斯投票反对公布与被定罪的人口贩运者有关的文件。
为什么重要：在过去的一周里，海德·史密斯在电视广播中的表现被击败了。 AdImpact 数据显示，播放次数最多的八个节目中只有一个对她进行了正面描绘。
其中五则广告要么正面描绘她的民主党挑战者斯科特·科洛姆，要么攻击海德·史密斯的参议院记录，很大程度上将她描绘成一位不切实际的参议员，更关心她富有的捐助者。另外两个广告是针对下一轮投票的。
缩小范围：据 AdImpact 报道，爱泼斯坦幸存者的广告在上周已播放了 1,200 多次，导致左倾新政超级政治行动委员会花费超过 32.9 万美元。
在广告中，吉娜丽莎琼斯谴责海德史密斯对爱泼斯坦档案的投票，并敦促密西西比人投票反对她以保护他们的孩子。
去年的投票以 51 比 49 获得通过，无限期推迟了一项修正案，该修正案原本要求时任司法部长帕姆·邦迪 (Pam ​​Bondi) 全面公布爱泼斯坦的档案。
海德-史密斯在给《密西西比自由报》的一份声明中表示：“我确实想要透明度，我支持发布可以合法发布的信息，同时保护爱泼斯坦的受害者。但对一项修正案进行程序性投票并不等同于说爱泼斯坦的文件应该保密。”
海德-史密斯的竞选团队也减少了对科罗姆的攻击，称他为“跨性别捍卫者”，并称他为“我们一生中最激进的参议院候选人”。
据 AdImpact 报道，该广告自 9 月 10 日首次亮相以来的 30 天内在密西西比州和田纳西州孟菲斯市的电视市场播放了 2,800 多次，参议员的竞选成本超过 85.4 万美元。
海德-史密斯的竞选团队似乎已经撤回了这则广告，在 10 月 19 日至 26 日期间播出该广告的花费不到 15 万美元。
底线：海德史密斯仍然有望获胜，但竞争比任何人预期的都要激烈。
正如特朗普总统周一在密西西比州科林斯举行的海德史密斯集会上所说：“我来这里是因为辛迪做得很好，但我必须确保这一点。”

title_en: "Nauseously optimistic": Anxious House Democrats brace for midterm Election Day
title_zh: “令人作呕的乐观”：焦虑的众议院民主党人为中期选举日做好准备
summary: Democrats will happily tell you how good they feel about retaking the House on Tuesday — just as soon as they stop hyperventilating into a paper bag. Why it matters: They've been burned too many times on Election Day to feel anything more than "nauseously opti
summary_zh: 民主党人会很高兴地告诉你，他们对周二重新夺回众议院的感觉有多好——只要他们停止对纸袋的过度换气。
body_en: Democrats will happily tell you how good they feel about retaking the House on Tuesday — just as soon as they stop hyperventilating into a paper bag.
Why it matters: They've been burned too many times on Election Day to feel anything more than "nauseously optimistic," as one House Democrat put it to Axios.
The polls point to a decisive Democratic victory on Nov. 3, yet fears of a massive polling error or some other eleventh-hour disaster are giving party members sleepless nights.
"One woman at a rally in New Jersey told me last week that she was 'nauseously optimistic,'" Rep. Jamie Raskin (D-Md.) told Axios. "That may capture a lot of people's last-minute jitters."
A House Democrat who has spoken to leadership told Axios: "They feel optimistic. You know, guarded. Guarded optimism. Where we're going to end up, you never know."
State of play: Democrats are targeting dozens of Republican-held seats they think could flip, some of which President Trump carried by 10, 15, even 20 percentage points in 2024.
Democrats' House Majority PAC, for instance, went on the air Wednesday in retiring Rep. Elise Stefanik's (R-N.Y.) district, which Trump won by 21 points.
They also began spending against Rep. Mike Flood (R-Neb.), who won his last reelection with 60% of the vote.

HMP is so bullish it has moved money out of the races to replace retiring Reps. Don Bacon (R-Neb.), Chuck Edwards (R-N.C.) and Darrell Issa (R-Calif.), which they believe Democrats are on track to win handily.
"I am cautiously optimistic we win between 20-25 seats," Rep. Ro Khanna (D-Calif.) told Axios.
Democrats' landslide scenario puts them closer to 40 or 50 pickups, which would be a historic night for the party.
Yes, but: Mid-decade redistricting in Republican-controlled Southern states is all but certain to cut into those gains.
The GOP is expected to easily flip redrawn seats in Tennessee and Louisiana where the incumbent Democrats chose to retire rather than face uphill reelection battles.

Democratic leadership is also nervous about several Democrats who opted to run in their new seats, including Reps. Kathy Castor (D-Fla.), Darren Soto (D-Fla.) and Shomari Figures (D-Ala.), according to three lawmakers familiar with their thinking.
What they're saying: All of the nearly 20 House Democrats who spoke to Axios on Wednesday expressed some degree of confidence about the election.
"I've been to 26 states this campaign, and I'd say Democrats have been riding a wave of tremendous optimism and activism over the last several months," said Raskin.
Rep. Hillary Scholten (D-Mich.) told Axios she is feeling "legitimately good" and that "the cautious optimism is there only because of … history."
"The optimism is real and I think for good reason," said Rep. Johnny Olszewski (D-Md.).
But virtually everyone also offered reasons for keeping their expectations tempered. "Dems have been burnt by good polling before," Rep. Dave Min (D-Calif.) told Axios.
Min also said Democrats are "hyper-aware of the election tampering that Trump and his goons are engaging in right now," something several other lawmakers echoed.
body_zh: 民主党人会很高兴地告诉你，他们对周二重新夺回众议院的感觉有多好——只要他们停止对纸袋的过度换气。
为什么重要：正如一位众议院民主党人对 Axios 所说的那样，他们在选举日已经被烧伤了太多次，除了“令人作呕的乐观”之外，没有任何感觉。
民意调查显示民主党将在 11 月 3 日取得决定性胜利，但对大规模民意调查错误或其他最后时刻灾难的担忧让党员们彻夜难眠。
“上周新泽西州一次集会上的一名女性告诉我，她‘乐观得令人作呕’，”众议员杰米·拉斯金 (D-Md.) 告诉 Axios。 “这可能会引起很多人最后一刻的紧张情绪。”
一位与领导层交谈过的众议院民主党人告诉 Axios：“他们感到乐观。你知道，谨慎。谨慎的乐观。我们最终会走向何方，你永远不知道。”
现状：民主党瞄准了他们认为可能会翻转的数十个共和党控制的席位，其中一些席位是特朗普总统在 2024 年赢得的 10、15、甚至 20 个百分点。
例如，民主党众议院多数派政治行动委员会周三在即将退休的众议员埃莉斯·斯特凡尼克（纽约州共和党）选区进行了广播，特朗普以 21 个百分点获胜。
他们还开始花钱对抗众议员迈克·弗洛德（内布拉斯加州共和党），后者以 60% 的选票赢得了上一次连任。
HMP 非常看好，因此已将资金从竞选中移出，以取代即将退休的众议员唐·培根（内布拉斯加州共和党）、查克·爱德华兹（北卡罗来纳州共和党）和达雷尔·伊萨（加利福尼亚州共和党），他们相信民主党有望轻松获胜。
“我对我们赢得 20-25 个席位持谨慎乐观的态度，”众议员 Ro Khanna（加利福尼亚州民主党人）告诉 Axios。
民主党的压倒性胜利使他们接近 40 或 50 名选票，这对该党来说将是一个历史性的夜晚。
是的，但是：共和党控制的南方各州在十年中期重新划分选区几乎肯定会削减这些成果。
预计共和党将轻松推翻田纳西州和路易斯安那州重新划定的席位，现任民主党人选择退休，而不是面临艰苦的连任之战。
据三名熟悉其想法的议员透露，民主党领导层也对选择竞选新席位的几位民主党人感到紧张，其中包括众议员凯西·卡斯特（佛罗里达州民主党）、达伦·索托（佛罗里达州民主党）和肖马里·人物（阿拉巴马州民主党）。
他们的言论：周三接受 Axios 采访的近 20 名众议院民主党人都表达了对选举的某种程度的信心。
拉斯金说：“这次竞选我去过 26 个州，我想说民主党在过去几个月里一直处于巨大的乐观和激进主义浪潮之中。”
密歇根州民主党众议员希拉里·肖尔滕 (Hillary Scholten) 告诉 Axios，她感觉“理所当然地很好”，并且“谨慎乐观的态度只是因为……历史”。
马里兰州民主党众议员约翰尼·奥尔谢夫斯基 (Johnny Olszewski) 表示：“这种乐观情绪是真实存在的，我认为这是有充分理由的。”
但几乎每个人都给出了降低期望的理由。加利福尼亚州民主党众议员戴夫·明 (Dave Min) 告诉 Axios，“民主党以前就曾因良好的民意调查而感到沮丧”。
敏还表示，民主党人“高度意识到特朗普和他的暴徒目前正在进行的选举篡改”，其他几位议员也对此表示赞同。

UN condemns U.S. economic embargo of Cuba though more nations sit out amid Trump push

UNITED NATIONS (AP) — The U.N. General Assembly condemned the U.S. economic embargo of Cuba for the 34th year on Wednesday, even as Washington's campaign to influence the outcome led to a number of countries voting against the resolution or sitting out the decision for the first time.
WATCH: Trump at GOP rally in Florida revives idea of military intervention in Cuba after Iran

The vote was 130-17, with 25 abstentions — a notable decrease in support from last year, when more than 160 nations supported the measure and only 12 abstained. While such resolutions at the U.N. General Assembly are not legally binding, they do reflect world opinion.

For the first time in 34 years, Western countries like Germany, Italy and Latvia were among those that refrained from voting. Bosnia, Colombia, Costa Rica, Ecuador, Lithuania, Morocco, North Macedonia, Paraguay and Slovenia are among those member states that voted no — most for the first time.

It marks a stunning shift in international support at a time when the small island country weathers outages, shortages and other deepening financial troubles as the Trump administration looks to force changes to Cuba's political system by increasing an already punishing economic campaign. President Donald Trump last week once again raised the specter of U.S. military intervention, saying American warships could stop over in Cuba on their way back from the Iran war.
"A great power is attacking through economic war a member state of this organization," Cuban Foreign Minister Bruno Rodríguez said ahead of the vote. "Cuba is not a threat. The blockade is a threat."

U.S. Ambassador to the U.N. Mike Waltz told member nations that, "your vote today is the only thing standing between the corrupt, kleptocratic communist regime and using this body and your vote for another propaganda victory at the expense of the Cuban people."

Tensions between Washington and Havana have spilled over into fiery public spats at the United Nations. On Tuesday, Waltz and Rodríguez got into a shouting match on the floor of the General Assembly while debating the embargo resolution.

Shortly after Waltz had begun his criticism of the socialist government, Rodríguez walked down to the podium where the U.S. envoy was addressing the hall and called him a liar while trying to get a point of order from the official presiding over the session.

"This individual needs to back away from this podium. He's not going to intimidate me in the United States of America," Waltz said as U.N. security and personnel tried to intervene. "You understand who you're dealing with? This is America. Back up."
In a post on X, Rodríguez reminded Waltz where he was making his remarks, saying he's at the U.N., not at a national security meeting at the White House.

"With his crude lies at the UN General Assembly, the U.S. government has launched another desperate attempt to justify its economic aggression against Cuba and its criminal energy blockade," he continued.

On the sidelines of the GA hall, Waltz accused a member of Cuba's delegation of attacking an American diplomat who was filming him. He said Secretary of State Marco Rubio has ordered the official sent home. The State Department on Wednesday confirmed to the AP that the individual accused has left the U.S.

A week earlier, a similar interaction between Waltz and his Cuban counterpart, Ernesto Soberón Guzmán, took place outside a U.S.-hosted panel with Cuban dissidents and former prisoners that sought to highlight allegations of the oppressive behavior of the island's government.
It all reflects a clear break from the traditional diplomatic decorum expected at the U.N. and the new phase of contentiousness between the U.S. and Cuba.

The U.S. embargo against Cuba was first imposed in 1960 after Fidel Castro led a revolution that toppled dictator Fulgencio Batista and nationalized properties belonging to U.S. citizens and corporations.

As a result, the Caribbean country has spent decades facing the dire impact of longtime economic and financial troubles and is now being pushed to a breaking point after Trump announced in late January that he would impose tariffs on any country that sells or provides oil to Cuba.

联合国谴责美国对古巴的经济封锁，但更多国家在特朗普的推动下袖手旁观
联合国（美联社）——周三，联合国大会谴责美国对古巴实施的第34年经济禁运，尽管华盛顿为影响结果而采取的行动导致一些国家对该决议投了反对票，或首次缺席该决议。
观看：特朗普在佛罗里达州共和党集会上重申了伊朗之后对古巴进行军事干预的想法
投票结果为 130 票对 17 票，25 票弃权——与去年相比，支持率显着下降，当时有 160 多个国家支持该措施，只有 12 票弃权。虽然联合国大会的此类决议不具有法律约束力，但它们确实反映了世界舆论。
德国、意大利和拉脱维亚等西方国家34年来首次没有参加投票。波斯尼亚、哥伦比亚、哥斯达黎加、厄瓜多尔、立陶宛、摩洛哥、北马其顿、巴拉圭和斯洛文尼亚等成员国首次投了反对票。
在这个小岛国经历停电、短缺和其他日益严重的金融问题之际，这标志着国际支持的惊人转变，特朗普政府希望通过加大本已严厉的经济行动来迫使古巴改变政治制度。唐纳德·特朗普总统上周再次提出美国军事干预的担忧，称美国军舰在结束伊朗战争返回途中可能会在古巴停留。
“一个大国正在通过经济战争攻击本组织的成员国，”古巴外交部长布鲁诺·罗德里格斯在投票前表示。 “古巴不是威胁。封锁才是威胁。”
美国驻联合国大使迈克·沃尔兹告诉成员国，“你们今天的投票是阻止腐败、盗贼统治的共产主义政权利用这个机构和你们的投票来以牺牲古巴人民为代价换取另一次宣传胜利的唯一因素。”
华盛顿和哈瓦那之间的紧张关系已在联合国引发激烈的公开争吵。周二，华尔兹和罗德里格斯在联合国大会辩论禁运决议时发生了一场争吵。
华尔兹开始批评社会主义政府后不久，罗德里格斯走到美国特使正在大厅讲话的讲台上，称他是个骗子，同时试图从主持会议的官员那里得到一个程序问题。
“这个人需要从讲台上退下来。他不会在美国恐吓我，”在联合国安全人员和人员试图干预时，沃尔兹说道。 “你知道你在和谁打交道吗？这是美国。后退。”
在 X 上的一篇帖子中，罗德里格斯提醒沃尔兹他是在联合国发表讲话的，而不是在白宫的国家安全会议上。
他继续说道：“美国政府在联合国大会上撒下粗鄙的谎言，再次绝望地试图为其对古巴的经济侵略和罪恶的能源封锁辩护。”
在大会堂外，华尔兹指责古巴代表团的一名成员袭击了正在拍摄他的美国外交官。他说，国务卿马可·卢比奥已下令将该官员遣返回国。美国国务院周三向美联社证实，被告人已离开美国。
一周前，沃尔兹和古巴同行埃内斯托·索伯龙·古兹曼在美国主办的由古巴持不同政见者和前囚犯组成的小组外进行了类似的互动，旨在强调对该岛政府的压迫行为的指控。
这一切都反映出联合国传统外交礼仪的明显突破，以及美国和古巴之间的新阶段争端。
1960年，菲德尔·卡斯特罗领导了一场推翻独裁者富尔亨西奥·巴蒂斯塔并将属于美国公民和企业的财产国有化后，美国首次对古巴实施禁运。
结果，这个加勒比国家几十年来一直面临着长期经济和金融问题的可怕影响，而在特朗普一月下旬宣布将对任何向古巴出售或提供石油的国家征收关税后，这个加勒比国家现在正被推向崩溃点。
